title: Jonah Jackson, Tyrique Stevenson, Colston Loveland on staying consistent | Press Conference
text: Obviously, a new center was going to impact you. Coach said this morning that Garrett is elite at his communication. Where have you seen that the most in him? >> Uh yeah, he's just a he's a smart guy. You know, he's been in the game for 8 years, so he's got a a lot of skin in it. And um you know, a lot of things he's done in the past is similar to what we do now, so I feel like it's it's been a smooth transition. >> What have you seen in Braxton coming off the injury and back to full health now after what was a tough year for him last year? >> Yeah, um he looks he looks great, you know, he he definitely looks the part um physically, mentally. Um yeah, he's he's moving really well. Uh he looks like a complete player from what I seen last year to now, so I'm excited for for what's to come with him. >> You've been around Ben for a while. >> How important is the running game right now? >> Um to setting up what he wants to be able to do this year. >> Yeah, I think the the I mean, the run game is everything, you know, if you if you can't run the ball efficiently, then you got to drop back and you know, that's kind of an alignment's worst nightmare is to have to pass the ball more than you run the ball, so you know, being able to do what we do and you know, um set up the run game and opens up everything, play action, drop backs, screens, everything, so. >> Jonah, an extension of that, what have you seen in your time with Ben that allows him to really put his fingerprints on the running game? >> Um yeah, I mean, well, it starts up front with us. Um the guy the the front five, you know, if if we're not rolling, then it it it's kind of a uh bad operation, but I feel like we've got a good unit and you know, whenever the the front five have been moving and rolling, everything's opened up. >> Jonah, what is Ben like in a run game install meetings? Does What is he What is he like? >> Um I mean, yeah, he's he's he's he's he's himself, I guess, you know, it's not like uh like he's like, "Ah, we got to do this." But you know, it's he knows what we need to do and he knows what we're good at and he he implements that in the run game for us, yeah. >> Jonah, do you think it's perhaps realistic that the offense can be you know, top echelon of the NFL this year, top five? Do you do you think that's sort of a goal you guys are setting? >> Definitely. >> Yeah, yeah, that's I mean that's what we're working for. >> And what's it like to come off a fully healthy season, same team, same coordinator, just for you to have that kind of stability, continuity? >> Um it's great, you know, I feel like I've been in this this offense now for for going on 6 years, so you know, it's just new names to it, but um it's awesome. >> As a whole on offense, how do you feel or I guess what's the key to being [snorts] able to handle more volume as you guys go through more installs and why you're doing how you're able to do it better this year than last year? >> Say that one more time? >> Okay, the the amount of volume you have, like seems like you guys are handling it a lot, picking it up quicker now as opposed to a year ago. What do you think the key is? >> I think it's just repetition, you know, being able to do what we did again last year, you know, we had a full year of it and now some more time. I think it's it's helped us to >> [snorts] >> for sure. >> Is there an area of the offense you feel like it just comes a lot more quickly? >> Um definitely yeah, the run game, you know, especially for our line. I don't know too much about what's going on in the routes and stuff, but I know protection, but yeah, the run game, I feel. >> Jonah, what have you seen so far from Devin Bush with his with his speed in the middle? >> Yeah, I mean, he's he's flying around. He's another guy who's got a lot of skin in the game and uh you know, he's a he's he's a good guy vocally and and physically, so he's going to be a good match up for us. >> Uh offensive linemen talk all the time about how much they love running the ball and they run blocking and things like that. Do you think is it is like the peak of that the run game when you have three tight ends out there? >> Because definitely, yeah, that that's definitely up there with with um the plays that are are called with with that personnel. Um yeah, they're they're our favorite downhill type of play, so it's a bit exciting. >> What specifically do you love about that that makes your job so much >> Um a lot of things are built off double teams and combos, so more combos and double teams are built across the line, so it's less one-on-one and you know, you really get to hammer the D-line. >> How has How has it What have you seen in Colston's maturation and just what he's able to he's kind of the same guy, you know, he came in a grown man. He was ready to roll. So, I'm excited to see what year two has for him. >> How does Logan compare to the other rookies that you've got on the In terms of the presence in the room and what he brings to the table? And how does he compare to the other first-year guys? >> Um yeah, I mean, he just he goes about his business the right way. He's a pro's pro. Um Yeah, he's he's been He's been playing ball for a while. I think he did six years. So, he's He's a man now in the league. So, I think he's ready. >> How has Ben changed in his role if if at all from offensive coordinator to head coach? >> Yeah, I would say he he was ready to be a head coach when he was an OC. Even in Detroit. So, I don't I don't think much has changed besides maybe some things he does outside of the football. I don't know. But, yeah, he's he's he's maintained the same mentality as as he was when he was OC. >> Jonah, what's next for you going into year seven? >> Um keep rolling, you know, get some get some get some wins, get a ring, and stay healthy, and you know, help this team as much as I can. >> What's your takeaway about playing in the Super Bowl last year? It seems to me like he's coming here and he's he's been where a lot of you guys want to go. >> Yeah, we talked a little bit about it, but you know, that's that's the ultimate goal in mind for everybody. >> How clean do you feel like the operation was for the offense versus Saturday? >> Today versus Saturday? >> Yeah. >> Um I feel like it was it was you know, there's always going to be hiccups. You know, we're just getting back into it from OTAs and stuff, but I feel like like our transition to things has been much cleaner than it was this point last year. >> Jonah, coach Rashad has credited you for being kind of an energy source in the O-line room. What do you think that you bring into that room that kind of bring out that outgoing personality? >> Um just just being me, you know. Um know when to hit the switch, you know, being able to bring the guys up and you bring some energy, bring some nastiness, bring some tenacity, and uh that's just part of my game, being myself. >> What role does that play in bringing this year's line together? You know, you have a new center and maybe two new centers, and you know, even if you have the same guys at left tackle, do you feel like you need to do that a little more so or >> No, I feel like I you know, we did the same things as we did last year, and things things worked out pretty damn good. So, you know, we'll keep it the same. >> To that point, does it feel smoother this time around? I mean, you are having same conversation with the old line, center competition, left tackle competition, but in year two here, year six for you, does it feel like it's a smoother transition with all five? >> Yeah, certainly. And as a whole, as an entire offense, for sure. >> How much does that continuity, you're talking about the run game earlier, the continuity of having all these guys back, how does that help your run game specifically? we all know what we're doing, you know, the the assignment's much cleaner, the technique's much cleaner, you know, um we understand what Dan and Kyle want from us and what they want us to do specifically to whatever the the play or the scheme is, so I feel like uh year two of that will be even better. >> A few reps now going against Neville Gallimore, what what do you see in him? >> Yeah, I've I've been I've been going against Nev since since the Senior Bowl, and he's always been a um he's a he's a very big body, very fast, um strong. He's got a good abrupt subtle uh hump moves, quick moves, and and he can mix it in with power, so I'm excited to see what what the >> the next day is ahead, you know, what's he going to do? Yeah. >> Freshman >> He was big then. I actually seen him on one of my official visits, and I seen the squat board at Oklahoma, and it was like 600 lb. I was like, "Who's doing that?" Then he walked through, I was like, "Oh, I got it." >> Going into another year with with Darnell right on your right side, what have you seen from him just early on right now. Yeah, I mean, he's he's he's coming into his own like he did last year and I think this year will be even better. He's he's he's in better shape. He's he's his mind's better in a better place. Um technique and you know, taking coaching points. Um so, I'm excited. >> Still a couple more. >> Trey told us that he's not thinking of he knows he's going to be here for a long time. Nothing really affects that. Is that like an offensive lineman mentality or that also >> How just how darn good he is? >> Yeah, I mean, if for for for our position, you know, as you handle business, things will things will come um to you and a guy like him, I if he keeps going about business the way he is, I've told him, you know, don't worry about these things. Just handle each day accordingly and and everything will fall into the right place. >> Anytime the coaches critique your game talking about DA and coach [clears throat] Johnson, it's never really about your physical ability. It's always about consistency and focus. As a pro, how do you feel when you hear that and then how do you go about >> Do you do the most things, too? >> Uh I feel like I just you know, I just take it as it come. I don't just need to improve, you know, I feel like every day you come here in life in general, you just find something to improve in. You know, it just happen to be something I got to get my game up and improve better so that they feel like it's where they needed to be and how I approach it is just come here, do do the small things right and just approach the game as a professional every day just to we both on the same trust level where my focus need to be. So. >> Why do you think if if you believe it does, why do you think the focus goes away? >> Uh I don't feel like it goes away. I just think it's just goes back to like my physical talent. Like I can make any play sometimes, you know, when it just don't happen, it's you know, you got to find something to figure out and I think that's just the focus point like you know, uh maybe maybe I'm not looking at what I need to on that play and you know, that just ties back into focus. So. >> Where you at with your connection with Al? I know you've been very excited to kind of continue working with him. >> Uh it's just been great. It's great since the first day I met him. Um When I went on the 30 visit to Dallas, so it's always it's always been the same. We talk ball. He's big on interceptions and I'm big on I need him. So, you know, we we we connect on that and we got a better relationship outside of football. You know, I listen to him about you know, how to take care of your family and everything cuz he's been doing it for a while. So, our relationship been great. >> Ben said he was going to make a concerted effort to be in defensive meetings more this year. How what's he like in the meetings? >> Say one more time. I'm so sorry. >> Ben said he's going to be in defensive meetings more. Like what's he like in the meetings? Does he does he speak up a lot? Is he letting D.A. handle that? Position coaches? >> Uh, D.A. D.A. do most of the talking and he just he just he pops in and out sometimes and um I sit kind of close to him. So, if I if I see a certain play, I ask him a question and stuff like that. But, he's not really like vocal in there vocalizing. He just I think he just pop in and out sometimes. >> You said in during OTAs that you were talking offensive coaches more about, you know, how would you play me on this on this play specifics? What have you learned in being able to pick their brains that you think you can then apply to training camp tomorrow? >> I would say offense is about timing. So, best thing you can do as a defense just disrupt the timing. So, uh far as like what route break or like uh, giving me the same stem but giving me two different routes off of what to look for. So, I would say I just I've been taking that from from the quarterbacks and the offensive staff as well and just you know, plugging it into practice and just trying to work on my craft. >> When when free agency arrived, were you curious if if Jourdan was going to come back here or if they would get some other corners? Is that something you kind of >> No. >> waiting to see what happened? >> No, I just no. Off season I I took my two week put my two weeks in and then I got back to work, you know. Whatever they do, that's on them. Best I can do is just show up here, be available, be a team guy and you know, do my job. >> It's a huge opportunity for you in front of you now though, right? Like looking at the depth chart, opportunities you've had on the through what five practices? >> Uh yeah, you know, I feel like every chance you get the the step on the NFL field is opportunity. So, I'm always looking at every down I come out there is is opportunity for me to lose it or to keep it. So, not really looking at anything else outside of me just coming in this building, connecting with the coaches, getting getting their trust and getting our trust the same and you know, just coming out here and being the best player I could be. >> Is it hard to not think about your contract situation like what comes next? >> Uh honestly, I'm not like a you know, a real down the road thinker. Honestly, I want to come in here and you know, my my goal is to be just the best corner on this team, you know, aside of Jaylon Johnson and just help this team win and I feel like me doing that and being a selfless guy for this team everything will work itself out, you know. >> We've heard you guys spend a lot of praise here since the spring about Luther. When you go up against him, what's standing out to you when when you cover him? >> He can give you everything, you know, if you're too high and he wants to get under, he can get up under and now you're chasing him across the field. If you're too low, he'll take the top off. So, Luther to me is just a complete receiver and he's aggressive to the ball, you know, so I would say he's just complete receiver when when it comes with the ball in his hands, you know, after the catch and everything. So. >> And if he goes down today, what's going through everybody's heads there, you know, first padded practice of the year? >> Uh I really don't have too much info on that. I just was doing 101s and I found out like 7 on 7 Kobe went out cuz I was asking questions. So, uh I don't really have no info on that, but definitely praying for him to be out there tomorrow or you know, at the end of this week with us. So. >> And what what does he mean to the defense so far just you know, as training camp OTAs? >> Uh he's like a spark plug, you know, he's coming with the juice. You know, y'all actually from practice, you know, when he coming out the middle of field to make PBU's and so it's like he's just a spark plug and you know, he's bringing that energy every day. He's not he don't want it at the highest level, so he's not letting nobody slip under the standard. >> I know we're talking about how the team they've added speed and obviously a couple new receivers in here. Well, what does it look like from your perspective having to guard cover those guys? >> [sighs and gasps] >> Uh it is It's been a long one because each receiver is fast with their own different game. Like Rome is fast and could take the top off. Luther is fast and could shut it down. Then you got Leaf could do both. So, it's like, you know, just coming out there and practicing hard. I would say they just give you different parts of the game that just makes up makes us better as DBs to go out there and cover anybody. >> Going back to to Luther one-on-ones today you had to play where you was right there perfect coverage, great positioning, he still came down with the ball. What did you see on that one? How frustrating is it when you are in such position and he still make the catch? >> Uh end of the day uh I chalk it up to I've been in this league for a long time now. So, it's like I perfect throw beats perfect coverage every time. So, uh you know, just with that, you know, best I could do is just try to perfect my craft from the line of scrimmage to where I can throw him off the red line or something. But at the end of the day he you know, they get paid just like we do to go out there and make them tough catches. But uh it definitely makes me um know that I come back I got to come back and improve on something. Just just find the little thing like maybe can I widen them just a little bit more so he can't stack or you know, something like that. So >> To that point, what have you seen from Caleb that it just seems like he's been so consistent throughout camp that has taken his game to this next level early on? >> I see him more confident with his throws now. Like um you know, uh he can make we we all know he can make any throw and I feel like he's just leaning more into like I can make any throw and and throwing the ball where it needs to be for his for his receivers. Going back to his Rome and everybody got their different skill set. I just think he's honing into his receivers. >> Very good. So, what's impressed you about Malik so far? >> He's a dog. He's a dog. He you know, he's definitely twitchy and he you know, he he don't like the off thing. You know, he he likes to go down there and cover. And I was telling him you got to you know, in the league got to be able to do both. But he he wants to get hands-on and cover. But definitely like his his energy when it comes in. You know, smallest cash or smallest mistake he he ready to shut not not shut down, but he's ready to you know, get better and improve. So, I just like it I like his attitude. >> You like that too coming into the league? You were known as pretty good press corner. >> Yeah. Um I just think it was just something like, you know, we just work on daily in college, you know, I think that's where you make your money in college showing that you can press a receiver, you know, that runs whatever route in college, you know, cuz mostly out of time to throw the ball. So um you know, just I just want to I just let him know like you got to open up your game with the off coverage and being able to read some of these quarterback steps and stuff like that just to enhance his game. >> So is one-on-one drills definitely favor the the offense? >> Always. Always. Always. Always. Always. They give you any release, any tempo, no rush. Quarterback not going nowhere. So um quarterback make a perfect throw. You You feel me? So um but I I feel like that's just for um for defense to get better, you know, cuz at the end of the day sometimes game on the line it comes down to a one-on-one, you know, match protect and it's just you and him out there. So it turns into one-on-one anyway. So >> From your vantage point, does it feel like Jaylen is looking back to the all-pro Jaylen Johnson? >> Uh yeah, of course. Yeah, he you know, from his braids to his to his speed and everything he's looking back he looking like who he was, you know, I know I know he was frustrated with last year, but you know, I think he's back to or he's getting getting completely back to where he where he was before everything happened. >> You see it. What What's going to be the key to replicating those team-leading takeaways, particularly the interceptions? >> Uh just trusting in our self and going to attack the ball, you know, Al has a aggressive mindset to the ball and we I think once we adapt that as a team again and and we trust the coaches and we trust what we see on the field, I think that's just going to come back to what it was last year. Just attacking the ball and making sure we we come up with any fumbles, anything that you know, just going to get the ball back to our offense. >> Last one then. How many of the four training camps you've walked in and this season seems to have the most legitimate team potential. What's your read on on kind of going out here on the practice field with a group that can dream the biggest dreams? >> Um it's all on us, really. Um it's really it's really on how we come out here and prepare to go play um, you know, this 20 game season starting with the preseason. So, it's really on how we hone in and lock in to what we good at and what we going what we going to go out here and attack teams with. Um, and once we focus on that and we we come together as a team, I feel like nobody can stop us. >> AJ, close to the way you feel as a team trait. You feel >> [laughter] >> you're taking the next step as you come here early in the camp. >> Um, I feel like a biggest thing probably. I was talking to Hood today. It's like last year was like, all right, let me figure out what I got to do. Let me really master this offense, this position and see what I got to do. Now, that's coming a little a lot easier. Now, it's like, all right, let me look at the defense, their techniques, their alignments and uh I think that's a big thing for sure and then just extra steps on everything. Technique, continue to work on that. Um but just diving deeper into stuff, scheme. Um, and really what the defense is doing. >> You talked to Raven about your work ethic before practice, talking about the way you are in meetings, being a sponge and these things. From your perspective, what's your internal drive to to seek out that level that you want in your career? >> Yeah, I think uh like we always mess around a couple of us like like I'm getting an edge on you, you know? Um, so it's like I don't want anyone to have an edge on me, meaning I want to study just as much or more than everyone. I want to get as much touches, uh get as much, you know, whatever it may be. Um so yeah, it's just like if I see other people doing it, it's like, why am I not doing it? and then like I said, like back to the basics. Like if it's stuff I already know, >> [clears throat] >> it's like, all right, let me just continue to write this down and just keep ingraining it in my mind and then further from that, like, all right, what are the receivers doing? What are what are these guys doing and just expanding the the knowledge for sure. >> You feel like that is just coming out now for you year two and and second year in this offense? >> Uh yeah, I got a lot long ways to go though for sure. >> Who else is the neck group of people talking about getting an heads on the team? >> Uh really all around but like me and uh JP Richardson we mess around about it a lot. Um I'm trying to think who else. Uh tight end room we will too but uh really I just think of JP when I do it cuz normally really started on the golf course and then we then we brought it to here with all right you would do it do a couple extra extra reps of uh some grip strength or something. He's like I got an edge on you today. So now I got to go back in there and get some grip strength. >> Who's got the edge on the golf course? >> He's got me right now. We'll talk It's just football season now. >> Since the end of last season how do you describe the growth you've made in the connection with Caleb? definitely [clears throat] a lot of growth for sure just off the field like like you said in the off season went out in LA threw threw a little bit which is nice had had had all all the guys out there and then even just like you know doing stuff playing golf going to the movies going to his spot he always invites the guys over. Um so I mean I mean he's the guy you know he's always wanting he's always wanting people to come over he's a leader and he wants to build that bond with people outside of the field. I think that goes a long ways on the field just knowing that you can trust him having that relationship. Um and then on the field I mean continuing to get the extra reps after practice. Um knowing that if I you know drop one or do something wrong I'll be like you know you know I got you on the next one he knows that and vice versa. and we're continuing to build that relationship it's never ending. >> I see that he said that he thinks you could be the best tight end in the league. Did you Did you >> Yeah I I have seen that yeah. >> What What do you think? >> Uh yeah man that's it's an honor coming from him. I got a lot of work to do that for sure. Um but I think he could be the best quarterback in the league too. >> Kind of in like tight end grad school with Ben Johnson. How how much do you feel like you've learned about the position since you've been working with him? >> Uh ton man from Ben all the coaches but it's been coach Dre as well. such a great coach. Um so good with the fundamentals and the technique. And it's fun now, you know, not being having a year under my belt, being able to talk about it some more instead of like, all right, let me just figure out what I got to do. Now we can kind of bounce ideas off each other. Um, and the vets in the room as well. Um, just really continue to soak it all in in this year, too. Um, never never know enough, you know? I never know it all, yeah, really just continue to be a sponge, and it's been great, man. Learned a lot. >> Coach Miller, there's not many NFL teams that you can see uh the tight end could be the the leader in receptions and in yards for a team. Uh what do you think about that potential in uh that responsibility that you have in this offense as a chief? >> Uh like I've always said, man, I think we got so many weapons on this team. Um, and whatever my job is, whatever my role is on this team, I'm going to attack it. If that's being the leading receiver, then that's what it is. If it's getting 30 targets, that's what it is. Um, obviously I'm going to work my butt off to do whatever and be in put be put in those positions to make a play. Um, but we got so many weapons, and the coaches know what our strengths, our weaknesses, and they're going to put us in the right spot. Um, so just continue to build as a team, build as an offense, and then with the team success everything will come after that. >> Coach Miller, this summer like for you, I imagine it's probably the most attention you've ever had on you, most people know who you are. What's it been like to kind of manage that? And I'm I'm sure you know, how how how do you deal with that? >> Uh it was good, man. It's a blessing. Prayed for times like this, for sure. Um, had a lot of opportunities. Uh yeah, I mean, it come comes with it. >> Speaking of opportunities, how much did you enjoy going to see Michigan play earlier this year in route to the championship? >> Uh yeah, that was sweet. You're talking about uh United? Yeah, that was cool. That was cool that they uh they got to play here, two games actually. Um, got to tune into those, you know, seen a lot of people haven't seen in a while, so it was cool. >> Coach Miller, what was your initial emotion when you saw Kobe go down this morning? >> Uh you know, you know, always sucks to see. It's part of it. Um, but you know, he's a tough. He's a dog. He's going to be fine. Um, we're not worried about it, but I'll I'll I don't know. Leave that to coach Johnson. >> Okay. Having so many [clears throat] things like so many different things that look the same, run game, pass game, but does that make you just 1% more focused earlier in games when you're doing something that you know is setting up something later? >> Yeah, for sure. And that's what I'm continuing to work on, too, is seeing it all come together. Like, okay, we ran this so many times and now we're going to play action off of this something off of this. So, making it all look the same, making the splits look the same, not giving any tells. Um, continue to work on that, but yeah, the coaches do a great job of putting us in those positions. >> Colston, can you quan- quantify like how much more information you're taking in uh about the offense versus last year? >> Yeah, uh, definitely. Like I kind of said last uh, couple questions ago, just now knowing what I need to do, I can, you know, think of the offense as a whole, which I was doing last year, but really dissect it and then, especially what the defense is doing and that's helping, for sure. >> Colston, what's the chemistry between the tight ends and offensive line been like in regards to the run game? >> Uh, it's been great, man. I feel like it always is pretty great. Uh, good bunch of dudes in that room, in the O-line room, tight end room, as well. Um, and they do a great job communicating to us, you know, it's got to get down all the way down the line. Um, and that can be tough sometimes, but as long as we can get it out fast, get the calls out, and uh, come off the ball, the good things will happen and I think it's been good so far. >> What traits have you seen out of Sam Rousch, you know, just physically and how he's absorbing things? >> He's just uh, man, he's huge, first off. big guy, super fast, strong, um, and just seeing him out there with the pads on, he he's going to be he's going to be a weapon, for sure. Um, and he's obviously very smart, um, doing the right things, so I'm excited.

title: Ben Johnson looking forward to first padded practice | Press Conference
text: First day of pads. Everyone ready to go? >> Yeah, let's do it. >> Okay, let's do it. Go and open up, guys. >> Can you give an update on Kyle Murray and Guy Forest? >> Uh it's it's really a status quo. Um we're taking it day by day right now, but uh we're we're working through it. He's working hard uh with his rehab, and and it should be on the shorter side here. >> Specifics of what the injury is? >> It's just a soft tissue deal. Yeah. >> I mean, it's the obvious stuff when the pads come on in the trenches. Are there other things you like to look at specifically with positions or drills or whatever that like when pads come on, you get a closer look at certain things? >> Uh yeah, I mean, certainly we got one-on-ones going on today. I love looking at that cuz uh it it's our first time to really really really compete in in that type of setting, and I think you you bring out the best of both sides uh in that dynamic. So, I'm looking forward to that, and you know, I I I think these guys is you go through the acclimation process, you can kind of feel it the intensity pick up a little bit. And so, I I know they're ready for this, and um the team drills will be great for us here today as we get back into it, and and I think we're going to have a really good block of 4 days here coming up. >> How are you scheduling that block? Cuz are there pads tomorrow? Pads How is >> Yeah, we we got 2 days of pads. We got shells, and then we got pads again. >> We know you were eager to see the tackles get the pads on for that competition. What do you want to see them carry over from the off-season work in the first week into now this session? >> Yeah, it it's consistency for me. Um you know, we're we're judging every the ability to block these defensive ends one-on-one uh and then you know, the ability to cut off on the back side of our wide zone schemes huge for us. Um there's there's things in and out, and and I think each one of those guys is probably a little bit stronger in in certain areas than the other guy, and and I think when we look at it, who's the most consistent player that we feel like is going to help us on a on a weekly basis. >> With Will specifically, what do you see his strengths? >> Well, I know Alabama, Cleveland before he got hurt that he was a very powerful player. And so, it's hard to say um that yet. Hopefully, we'll see over the course of next few days, next couple weeks, if if that continues to be the case. Um you know, it's it's he hadn't played football in a while, and so you're a little bit like where's the confidence level at? And and from what we've seen in the last 4 days, it's been it's been pretty good. It's been a good start. And so, uh we'll continue to build that and he like I said, Braxton's been great. Um Jed's in firmly in the mix. Quran got some reps with the ones. I think Theo's worth mentioning as well. I mean, I think we got a really good group uh of guys that continue to ascend and get better. So, hopefully, it's a really difficult decision for us. >> And what are your plans for playing Caleb in preseason games? I know you have joint practices, and I know you have a practice right after that first exhibition game. >> Yeah, I think for for all of our starters, it it to be determined. We'll see what it looks like. Um And and so, that's how we're going to approach it over the the next couple of weeks, and and we'll be smart, you know, obviously, we need all these guys to be as healthy as we possibly can going into the season, cuz it's a long year. Um but at the same time, we want to make sure that we're we're prepped and we're ready, also. So, we're looking at numbers, we got sports science data, the number of reps we're getting, the quality of the reps that we're getting. It all goes into it. >> Is there Is it different this year that you and Caleb have worked together before, so there might not be any kinks to work out just practically in a preseason game? >> We're we're looking at it. Um I think it's always it's probably always good to at least go through the the warm-up procedure to where game one's not the first time of doing that, you know? So, there's there's a lot of merit in that regard. Uh and and we'll see what it looks like, but we haven't made a determination yet. >> Coach, big picture with your offensive philosophy going back probably a few years here. Um what when was the start of really gravitating toward the ideas of three tight ends and everything that that could create. It's just unpredictability. >> Um, to me it's it's it starts more with what defense you want to attack and so uh when I first got in the NFL 15 years ago now, you would run 12 personnel out there, which is two tight ends, two receivers, and most teams would give you base defense. And now more teams than ever are playing nickel or a version of their big nickel to that. And so um in order if you want to continue to attack base defense, the heavier packages may or may not generate that. And so I I think there's there's just some merit more teams are installing their nickel or their big nickel packages earlier on in camp, maybe day one, day two, because they're in it more often. And And so for us as offensive coaches, we may want to attack the the lesser used defense if we can. And so it just gives you flexibility. Um we look at that every week. Some weeks will we can go exclusive 11 personnel, which is all all three of our wide outs out there. Other weeks we might lean into a heavier package, but um we want we want to be able to weave through whichever way we want to go each week. >> Uh yeah, the other day Cole said it's been seamless going to Garrett Bradbury at center in terms of the communication up front. Is that kind of how you've you've seen it so far? Have you been pleased with that? >> Yeah, he's he's extremely impressive. He's super smart. Um you know, he's he's played high-level football in a couple of places now and he's brought that here. I think what what stands out the most is he's got an elite level of communication. He he is loud. He is decisive. Um He does a great job with with seeing the defense. There's a couple things so far he's seen that I would have done that and it was he's not in. I can kind of hear him in the back. I would have done this, blah blah blah. You know, and it's like, well, good. Yeah. Well, we're kind of we're cooking. We're cooking right now with him out there. So, um really pleased with what that's looked like and and you can tell that he and Joe have played together. You know, there's natural rapport there and I think he's really taken to the room. >> Ben, the offense has gotten a ton of early praise here, but getting to know you a little bit, I'm sure there's something as pads come on in the details that you're like, this has to be gotten right as we continue through here. What is that for you as you head into this week? >> Well, I mean, we we've been up and down a little bit. We we started off okay and then, you know, that that last practice wasn't very good from an offensive perspective. We had way too many mistakes. Um couple delay games mixed in there, false starts. The the little things like that started to accumulate and I I think that's probably normal with the volume continuing to increase and uh and yet it's not okay for us. And so, we we uh we're going to nip that in the bud and hopefully we'll we'll get a little bit better in that regard, but I'm uh I'm I was happy with the first four days. Just I I I think that the team speed is what showed up more than anything. Both sides of the ball is is we got some some guys that can run and and they're doing a really good job of that right now and and it's only going to make both sides better as we go. >> How much I know I did with tight end being a complex position. How much more have you been able to add to Colston Loveland's plate? >> Um I would say pretty significant. He knows he knows pretty much every spot. I mean, he's looking at the receiver routes. Um It's amazing to me when you go into a special teams meeting and you hear him you see him taking notes and then you hear him asking questions about special teams units that he's not likely to be on. And and so, it just says a lot about who he is. He's just a sponge right now. He wants all the information. He knows all this knowledge is just going to make him a better player and he's going to continue to play faster, so um yeah, I think there's a lot that he's learning, continue to learn and and uh he can apply it in real time, which is great. >> Jason and Dan. >> Ben, where do you feel like you're at with DeAndre Swift as far as uh just his fit in your offense after one season and maybe how much more you could do with him? >> Yeah, I I feel really good about where he's at. I've had long history with him, obviously, so know the skill set um might be a guy that we just keep an eye on as we go through camp. We need him fresh and ready to go for for 17 plus games this year and that's really what um what we're most concerned about, but yeah, there's things in the in the pass game that um we'll continue to look at and and challenge him on, uh but where he is as a runner right now, I think we feel really good about. >> Ben, when you talked to Ty Johnson about being more consistent >> Saying who? >> Ty Johnson. >> Yeah, yep. >> Where are the specific areas where you really want him to drill down and take his game to the next level? >> Yeah, yeah, it's really the focus level from uh being in the building um paying attention to meetings and continuing to apply that on the field in in uh you know, throughout a two plus hour practice and so um I think we've seen strides there. It's it's certainly uh improving, it continues to improve, he knows it and uh and so I think we're pretty happy with where he's at.

title: Mike LaFleur Press Conference 8.2.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: What's up guys? >> How's it going? >> What's going? How you doing? >> Just talking [snorts] about scorpions here. >> Scared me. >> Scorpion you got? >> It's so funny you asked that. Yeah, about 2 weeks ago um my wife was going down to tuck tuck in the kids and there was a a nice sized scorpion right outside the little man's room. So, that was our first uh first inside encounter. Needless to say there was people at the house the next day spraying. So. Yeah. Good. >> What do you got on injuries right now in terms of guys that are healthy, limping off the field, that kind of stuff? >> Yep, Walt's good. Um you know, more of uh you know, sometimes you name the player when they've had a a serious injury like they did when when they kind of feel some type of way about it. It it's uh you know, there's a process both mentally and physically getting through that, you know. So, he he's good um which is obviously a good thing for for most importantly him but but the Cardinals as well. And then uh you know, we're going to hold Joey out today. Uh he he got a stinger um but you know, with with what you guys know about his past injuries and and stuff from from the neck up. Um you know, we're going [snorts] to uh do some more testing and go from there. >> Was it anything that Walt felt? >> Yeah, just a little uncomfort un- he was not comfortable in that knee um that uh you know, he had an issue with a year ago. So, uh checked it all out, everything looked good and um and he'll be ready to roll today. >> When you look at that defensive line and and the depth that you guys have kind of collected, how are you seeing it right now? How how crucial are guys like Nolan and Darius to take that step? >> Yeah, not just those two. I mean, like you said the the entire depth. Like it's uh I can't say I've been on a very good football team that didn't have a very good defensive line that that wrecked havoc. Um you know, we've talked about in here about the quarterback being the most most important position in sports and it's about as hard as it gets, but I'll tell you what um that that D-line they got to they got to cause havoc up there. Snapping and snap out. Uh And and the importance of having depth so those guys can when they're out there they can go and then you can set send in that kind of that next platoon. I won't even call them the twos, just the next platoon to get after whether it be in the run game setting edges attacking making it difficult for the offensive line or obviously you know rushing the passer there on third down. So haven't totally you know had that conversation in front of the team yet in terms of what I think of D-line and O-line for that matter. But this D-line needs to go and they need to go hard. >> Like besides obviously getting more reps for your players, more teaching time for your coaches, what what's the what's the big advantage of playing in this game a week before everybody? What do you expect and hope to get out of it? >> Yeah, I think well I think you just said it, you know, I've been on record just how excited I was to get that one extra block, right? And and it also, you know, having having that extra game but then if we have to to kind of maneuver a day, man, we built so many reps off of that first block. So just the totality of what that's going to provide for us and then then you think about the game. You know, I'm going to hold off. I don't know if anyone's going to ask but I'm going to hold off in terms of saying who's going to play mainly and I'll tell you why mainly cuz I I want these guys only focus on now. Like it the preseason those games matter in the moment but what really matters in the preseason is the practice that that we're preparing for and that's where I want these guys and that's where I all those guys are at. So the guys that do play it's their first you know time out there where where coaches aren't you know right behind them or giving them a script. There is no script. We'll be tight with our plan and you know, what I want to go see is these guys their play style come to life and and us go operate before the before the snap. That's it, you know, and then everything else is just you know those guys going out and and letting it loose. >> With that said, what's your plan for this week as you as you go through the week here? >> Yep, so the same block. So we got our our practice today coming off an off day, which typically is going to be just a tick less of reps from what you guys saw these last two practices. Um Tomorrow will be fun. Um really fun in terms of just the amount of reps and and you know, there'll be some really good work put in. Then we'll go back to our jog through day and then our travel day, which will resemble the third day third practice of that four-day block. We will be practicing and and we'll be good getting after it that morning. We just have to modify in terms of the guys that are playing and the guys that aren't playing and obviously the travel time getting to, you know, the Phoenix airport there to to take off to Cleveland. >> So then you're not going to get specific, but in terms of how players approach preseason and how you want to approach preseason. For instance, Jeremiah stood up here the other day and insisted he wanted and needed to play in this game. Do you do you take any players input and whether they want to play or is it is it your plan and and you just need to tell them whatever the plan is? >> Uh it'll never just be my plan. It it's going to be a collective and communicative you know, effort in terms of in in great communication amongst everybody to see who needs it and who doesn't. For instance, name player that's been in the league for 10 plus years that's played a lot of football probably going to be a little different than a rookie, right? And so I appreciate Jeremiah saying that. You know, these guys love football. They want to play. I learned really early in this league like yeah, it's the preseason. It doesn't matter in terms of the win-loss, but these guys are still out there one fighting for jobs, two trying to put their best product out there and three they're putting their bodies on the line. Like it's real football. And if they the guys that are playing, if they don't go out with that mindset, I mean that's that's how you get hurt. It's how you don't put a good product on the field. So I kind of almost made the mistake in my mind as a coach when I first got into it about Um, just the the probably not being as serious as I needed to be with the players and I learned really quickly. Um, so we'll the guys that are playing, I mean it's, you know, it's an amped up environment. It's real. >> You talked about your plan now leading up to the game on on Thursday. What's your plan after the game? When are you guys going to get back to it with practice? Is anyone sticking around for the ceremony on Saturday? What does that look like? >> Yeah, that's a great question. So, uh, cuz I follow one block at a time. So, not honestly, I'm not even there yet in terms of I mean what's today? Sunday? Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, we play Thursday, get home at I mean I don't even 4:00 in the morning, whatever it is, 3:00 in the morning. We got to evaluate the film and then we got to get ready for that next block. So, um, obviously the, you know, when um, when Larry gets inducted and and he gets his speech and his time there, that's going to be a pretty special special moment. But, uh, yeah, I'm really not even there yet with that next block. I just know that when that next block comes, it's we still have a four-day deal, which is great, you know, and that fourth day is going to coincide with us taking off from here, um, getting back to Tempe and that'll be, uh, two days before we play Vegas. That's really all I know so far. >> With preseason being such a different idea for rookies, having not played preseason games in college, do you talk to them at all as a group saying, "Hey, like this is how you should approach this game?" Or is there anything differently than how you would >> I think I don't want to over talk it. It's just it's it's a game and and it again, when you when you put your body on the line, it's real live bullets out there. Like you you got to mentally get yourself right and uh, and that's it's not a problem as long as we approach it that way. And so we won't over talk about it. It's just, "Hey, we got to go play good football. We got to operate the right way and our play style's got to come to life." And then when the ball's snapped, you got to go execute. And sometimes it's going to be clean looks and sometimes it's going to be a look that you've never seen, particularly in the preseason, cuz it's not like we're watching film on Carolina. Um, at all. Like I'm not going to watch a snap of them. So, we're just going to have, um, you know, a a tight plan that is all-inclusive for whatever they they bring at us, you know, protected plays if you will. And then you just want to see these guys, you know, come off the rock and and and go. >> [snorts] >> You've talked You've talked before about your respect for Will Johnson. I'm curious opposite of him, the competition between a Denzel and Max. Has there been anything that stood out to you about that? >> Competition. You know, I see these guys continuing to just, you know, worry about themselves and attack one play at a time. But again, it's it's like anything in life. The The more quality players that you have in in one position room, the better it's going to be for for not only the team, but for that player. Like guys thrive on competition. When someone's getting pushed, you never want to get comfortable. And you have the rare instance where you have a guy that doesn't really care. Like Trey McBride, you could have two Trey McBrides and he's probably not worried about that other Trey McBride. He's worried about himself and continuing to move the needle. So, but it doesn't hurt to have those bodies. You mentioned those guys. And I think we have we have multiple guys in that corner room that are worthy of being NFL players and and contributors. >> Coach, it's about [snorts] two weeks into the camp. What do you think this team does really well? >> I think they come to work. You know, I think they're they're focused in the day-to-day. I think they are where their feet are. I've enjoyed the urgency. I've enjoyed the um the way they, you know, they approach each and every day. With that being said, we got a long way to go. You know, I I I thought two days ago was our best practice. That really doesn't matter unless we move the needle today. I thought we operated the best. I thought it was the cleanest that we looked. And then at the at the flip side, like I told the staff today, it's never as good as it seems. It's never as bad as it seems. I left here and I was, you know, naturally, man, that was pretty cool competitive practice. And you watch the tape and there was tons of details that need to be cleaned up. Tons. And that'll always be the case cuz we're going to hold ourselves to a high standard. But again, I I appreciate these guys' approach and I, you know, I look forward to what they're going to do today. >> Coach, any progress with the pub guys? >> Yeah, I'd say progress, but no timeline right now. You know, if you ask Tip, Tip's feeling feeling good. Garrett's feeling good. Sweat's feeling good. So, but I don't have a timeline for you and and truly I mean that. >> You had said during spring that you thought there was actually an outside chance that Garrett could be ready for week one. Do you still feel like there's a chance of that or is that >> Yeah, I do. I feel really good about that. So, he's feeling better every single day. And you know, I love I love the approach that guy. I mean, he's you talk about clockwork. I mean, at 6:00 a.m. every morning he's walking in that building doing what Garrett does, you know, and that's just kind of that's that's just how he's wired. >> And is Sweat close? I mean, because you said it was just a matter of kind of building him up and it's been two weeks now since the start of camp. Is he is he getting close to being built up? >> Continuing to build. >> When you're watching Josh, we'll make this the last one. When you're watching the practice film, how do you balance plays where if you guys were holding out it'd be a sack or be a hit or be a tackle for loss, but the play's made and then like how do you balance that? >> Yeah, I mean, it's You ever You ever hear D-line coaches out there during a practice and all they yell is scream a sack after every play? And it's like guys, if that were true, then we'd have 14 sacks per game for 17 games and we'd lead the league. So, like there is a a weird balance to that and you know, so until I actually see that in real life where it's that many sacks, then I'll believe it. But at the same time, hey, for that play, yeah, I guess that was a sack. But you know, they stay away from the quarterback and the quarterback's got to go through his unless it's just absolutely egregious where he can't even maneuver or step up. Obviously, then those quarterbacks just naturally kind of shut it down at that point. But you know, when when we do get edge a little bit and there is, you know, we're firm in the pocket, well, we can step up, you know, and so the other thing is obviously we're not going to to do some of the things that we feel like gives us an advantage from an offensive perspective with with a lot of our protections, the way our backs shave off the the you know, off the defensive ends and stuff like that when they clear their protection responsibilities, like we'll never do that to our players. Like they they I just I mean you could break a rib quickly. And we're not going to do that. We're going to protect our guys. But in season when [snorts] it's a different color jersey, they're going to go after that. And and to to make sure we get some of those, you know, um concepts off, if you will. So. >> Thanks, guys.
