title: Mike LaFleur Press Conference 7.31.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: With uh >> [snorts] >> with Jeremiah, how do you balance the expectations for a high draft pick like Jeremiah, but also balance the expectations that he he is still a rookie as well? >> The the same way I do with all these guys. I expect them to have their, you know, put their best foot forward today and continue to improve. So, um there's always going to be high expectations for high draft picks. You name the position, you know, everyone wants to see these guys be all pros right off the rip. Uh but uh not really concerned about what he looks like on September 13th. Um concerned about, you know, making those necessary improvements uh from the first five practices going into practice six. >> Tyler talked about how you reached out to him after the draft after Jeremiah got drafted. Just how important was that for you to reach out to him and and do that? >> Yeah, just yeah, try not to catch these guys off guard. I I just think uh when when you have guys like Tyler who are, you know, the the exact pros that you want in your building, uh I think you owe it to him to just communicate. I think where communication lacks, negativity fills the void. Not necessarily with him, but just in general. I mean, not just in football, in life in general. So, being able to just make sure that he knew where we stood as an organization. Um didn't just talk to him, talked to James Conner as well. Um just to give them a heads-up and and keep it moving. >> I think you could build a really good tandem together and then we've seen that kind of play out the first couple weeks with them splitting first team reps. How do you envision that kind of thing two months out? >> I envision them getting, uh you know, a good amount of reps today. I I It's September 13th. It's such a far ways away and uh but I do know this, not one running back can take all 65 snaps. We've seen that story when guys are a little bit overloaded and whether it it hurts them in one year, I think over time, one year, two years, whatever it is, um being able to split those guys up to one, keep them fresh throughout that game, but two, to keep them um as healthy as they can for 17 games is the appropriate way to go. >> Where are you guys at right now in your install process? Are you still installing things for the first time or you now at a process of reinstalling things that you did during OTAs? >> Uh I'd say it's it's more of a reinstall at this point. When you look at the totality, there's a lot on these guys right now. What's great about our defense is with the multiple looks that they give, our guys are seeing a lot of different stuff. So even though we might be running the same play, they're getting two, three, four different, you know, looks at it every single time they go. And that's part of the scripting process as well. This is a controlled environment in terms of of the scripts. Like, "Hey, I want to see this tough look from you, Nick, today." So see if how our offense handles it and then, "Hey, here's a clean look and let's make sure we can execute those clean looks. So kind of kind of right in the middle. I mean to give the I mean NFL defenses and players, particularly ones that, you know, are are I would say more in the veteran mold like our guys are. If you give them the same exact looks every single practice, like you're not giving the offense a chance, either. So I mean there's a competitiveness on that as well. But yeah, I'd say we're right in the kind of kind of the thick of it. >> You [snorts] guys did the practice with the two-minute drill a couple days ago. What were your takeaways as far as that exercise? >> Uh we've got a long way to go. You know, there was a lot of a lot to clean up there both execution-wise and and more importantly to me operation-wise. Um with that being said, I like the amount of reps we got. I like the response that we got from the players. You know, we just got done with a team meeting and just kind of showing them. And if you look at that second group toward the end, I mean there was a lot of reps there. And it I mean there was a point it looked like a jog through. And that's okay. It was, you know, July 28th. They're not ready to go through a full game and and and, you know, again September 13th is not for a long ways away. But the message was, "Look where you're at right now and look where we got to get to." We got a lot of work to put in to be able to go out there and and go through a a 12-play two-minute drive if need be. Hopefully it doesn't take 12 plays, but it might. And both sides have to be prepared and physically ready to go through that process. >> So, catching Jacoby up, the fact that you're on the that you're mostly reinstalling the offense, does that mean that he'll get a chance to basically see everything that's in your playbook and and run that at some point because you're rehashing the things that he needs >> Yeah, well, which would have been no different had he been here all OTAs. I mean, you always go right back like I actually told the staff today, I said, you know, part of our job is to never assume they remember anything. I want every single time that that we go into those installs to treat it like it's the first time they heard it. I think that's, you know, something that we give to them as players. They have to go out and do it, but to continue to hear the same things, the same details over and over and over till they almost get exhausted with it, that's okay. And so, even if Jacoby had been here through OTAs, it really wouldn't have changed our process. Now, him and I's conversations, particularly separate maybe in the quarterback rooms, can be slightly different, you know, maybe a little bit more of the wise because some of it is the first time. Um the good part is Jacoby's not a rookie, either, like I keep saying. Um he doesn't have to learn the speed of the game. He doesn't have to learn his teammates for that matter. I mean, obviously a few of them, but uh for the most part, he knows how these guys move, how these guys shake. So, uh you know, that's a that's a net positive. >> You're assuming if you if you're operating under the assumption that this is the first time they're hearing it, how do you build on that? Like, how do you move forward if you keep rehashing these things? >> Well, I mean, you're not going to like there's there's certain things that we did in practice 2 days ago that we're not doing today. So, I'm not going to just fill them with stuff that we're not going to rep today. When you get to a game plan, like training camp can sometimes be harder cuz the whole offense is up. You know, but like I mean, what is he going to call? When you get into the regular season, I mean, it is extremely tight. You have your first and second down plan that you can just nail. Like, you you spend you you send it out Tuesday to the quarterbacks so they have a shot at it. They come in early, they start to just kind of digest it themselves that they will, maybe with Shobby. Um then you get to the install portion of it, then you get to the walk-through portion of it. We'll always do a walk-through in the building before we actually get to the real walk-through. I've told these guys get ready to walk through cuz we're going to do a lot of it. So that we're sharp and we know what the heck's going on. And then you then you do the same process Thursday, you do the same process Friday. And so that man, you just own this plan. Well, then you get to the next week and there's going to be some overlap like there always is. But we're going to install it just like it's the first time they heard it. Um you know, and and that's just what I believe and then I think that's how the best offenses operate. >> Starting next week when you have preseason game, will you lighten the load of plays being called or since it's preseason and training camp, you'll continue to have that larger >> That's the price of doing business in in this league. I mean it is still training camp over the preseason, particularly this first game. And and I'm very excited about this game. This game means a lot for this organization. This mean game means a lot for the NFL. And we'll treat it as such. But we got work to put put in. And so we'll we'll take block three as it is. Practice, practice, jog through practice. That last practice Danny will be modified because we do got to get on a plane to head out to Cleveland. And there are guys are going to be playing, but we will be practicing right before we leave. >> You got it on a rotation now? At quarterback for that game yet? >> Uh yeah. And I'll I'm going to hold it just for a minute and then but I'll early next week you guys will know. >> We're we're a couple days into pads. Have you seen guys start to kind of separate themselves whether for good or worse or is it still kind of too early to say? >> Uh somewhat I guess, but I I would say a little too early. I want to I want to you know, hold off judgment or or crown anyone before we get too far into this game. We're at July 30th. Um I can't preach peaking at the right time and then all of a sudden start crowning guys or saying this guy can't do it. Uh what what we do want to see these guys is again, not make the same mistake twice and continue to play with the play style that's going to be necessary for us to win football games. >> We've We've seen a lot of Kendrick Bourne in this offense. He's obviously a guy that has mostly throughout his career played on the outside. What did you see from him and especially working with him in the past that made you think that he was going to be a fit in this slot role in your offense? >> He played some inside. 2019 he played quite a bit inside for us in San Francisco. But no, it's It's Well, yes and I get you know, New England's very different than us but but you know, I got a lot of history Kenny. And I'm I'm kind of joking with you there but you know, a lot of our guys like we've talked about in here. Um It the XCF but but they're all interchangeable. The Y plays inside until he doesn't. He can play outside, you know. Now, to get to the answer to that question, what I believe if you're going to be able to play inside one, you got to be able to muck it up in the run game and he has no problem doing that, you know, he can get in there. He can block nickels. He can insert in the B gap if he needs to. He can do all those kind of things. But you got to be if you're going to play inside the numbers and be efficient, uh you got to have efficient feet and you got to be not afraid of contact with really good hands and I think he has all those. I think he is only gotten better with his lower half. I'll say this to him cuz I love him. I'll say it to you guys. He's not the fastest guy out there. Uh he's never always been the most dynamic guy. Uh so he's he's kind of aging pretty well. He's not he he's not losing any of the traits that he that he's always had. He's actually in my opinion, he's only getting better with it. I think he he looks more grounded. I think he looks more confident in his hands and he's always been confident in in his hands. We used to joke with him. He'd he you know, I lose people when I say I think he has some of the best hands in the league and they're like, well, look at the drops. It's like, well, he's so sure in his in his hands that he's not even looking at the ball half the time. He's figuring out how to knife up the field and so he'll drop one. Typically when a guy drops a ball, the next time they get the throw, what would you do? There's no way I'm dropping it. So I'm going to really look this in. Not Kendrick. He just continues on his way. And and that's what makes this dude pretty special. And so um you know, he's uh been a he's been a great addition thus far. Um, uh I love the energy he brings. I always have loved his energy and and I think that's only improved since the last time I've been with him. >> Like the process of being a first-time head coach, finding your voice, finding out how to command a room, what's that been like for you from the day you got the job until now? taking one day at a time and always, uh, you know, evaluate yourself and being hard on yourself and figuring out what you can do better, what you liked, we need to lean on. Um, don't don't try to overthink it, just try to be authentic and and true to myself and and tell these guys truth. So, um, not something that I I I would say I I overly consume myself during the day, but yeah, I mean, I guess I you could say I put thought into it at night when I'm driving in. >> What does having a guy with Kendrick's skillset do for the offense as a whole to elevate that whole unit? >> It Kendrick, you're saying like >> what what what is having that skillset that you just talked about? Like what does that do for your offense kind of as a whole? >> You know, anytime you have a guy and and we have I in my opinion multiple guys. You think of a guy like Trey McBride, what I tell these guys if we can get you between the defender and the ball, we need to make those plays. So, you think about when he gets into those sticky situations, third and five, third and six, two-minute red zone, all that, uh when you have a guy that has efficient feet, lower half, and has confidence in himself and can make those contested catches, um you feel good about it cuz you don't have to get him wide open, uh to to obviously be effective. So, um again, I think we have multiple guys that can do that. He just happens to be one of them. >> What went into your decision to shake up the seating chart in the locker room? For three years it's always been by position, now it's all mixed up. Why you want to do >> They're talking about it. You know, they're getting to know some other people, um that that that they may not not have. So, um again, we didn't address it with them. I just wanted it organically to see if anyone figured out what was going on there and obviously the cat's out of the bag and and uh but they're talking about it and it seems like they're enjoying it. So, I'm getting to know some people. I think that's the coolest part. One of the coolest parts is that that I like about football. You got all walks of life in one locker room and and for the most part, it's a pretty perfect society in there. Um you know, guys getting to know each other and and you know, um I love my brother to death, but there's times that him and I go after it a little bit. Well, that's going to happen too in that locker room and that's okay and they'll work it out and uh it's um it's it's it's a unique place, not just ours, but but the whole league. >> Has anyone come to for something to say something to you about it or bring it up to better talk to you? >> Oh, no one's brought it up. I just hear them talking about it with you guys. >> There's a lot of intrigue about the the right guard spot between Isaiah Adams and Chase Bisontis. What have you seen from both of those guys so far? >> Yeah, I think two uh two players that are in in two different uh stages of their career. Um I could go 4 and 1/2 minutes on this answer like coach Friday yesterday if you want. Uh He's [snorts] a beaut, man. I love him. Um I didn't know he was a journalism guy. So, you guys are all kind of fitting in good with him, but no, I think uh I think they are um you know, like I said, two different stages. Uh you got a guy that's been in this league for a few years now. Um had some ups, had some downs and some stuff in between and and I just like his approach every single day in terms of trying to get better, trying to understand why, um hitting his combinations, hitting his sets. Uh he's been a very consistent um dude for us so far at right guard since OTA one on. I think I said it the other day. Uh I feel like I've just seen improvement every single day from him and that's all you can ask for from these guys. Like have great intent every time you come, have great play style and let's see improvement, not making the same mistakes twice. And then you look at Chase and I I I guess from a rookie standpoint, I could say the same thing. Um OTA one, I don't know if he came off the snap snap count once at the right time. OTA two was probably 50% and it's just continued to get better. That's okay. That's where he was on that day and uh you know, you can definitely see the talent. I I love um kind of his approach, his vibe. He's um he's got a good look in his eyes. Got that little jersey jersey uh passion to him if you will, which I've I've gotten to know pretty well my two years over there. So I'm pleased with where those guys are at. >> You see a lot more 11 on 11 here than in previous camps. How much is that of an evaluation tool for you in training camp and how much does it carry over to the regular season scrimmaging 11 on 11? >> It's how you play football, you know. Again, leading up to to practice and and having their individual groups and the routes on air, working on timing, getting loose, all those kind of things. Very beneficial obviously get to that point, but I don't know how you get better at football if you're not actually practicing football. I I wish we could go live and tackle and do all those things, but that wouldn't be smart. We know that. So this is the closest thing we can do to get them ready to peak September 13th. >> Ball security is as basic as it gets in football, but do you have anything that you stress whether it's quarterback, running back I mean in training camp from day one on on ball security? >> It basic. It might be ordinary, but we better do that extraordinary and and taking care of the ball. Matt Merritt does a great job of getting in front of the offense every single week. We'll stress it every day in our own rooms. We'll stress it in the unit room if we need to and then Matt Merritt's going to come up our running back coach and give a ball security presentation every week kind of where we're at, where we can get better, where you know, and what we're doing well. So it's going to be stressed every single day. There's there's outside of points, there's um truly two stats that are actually have a pretty good percentage of winning and losing this league. Obviously ball security is one, turnover margin. It's like everyone said that. And then the other one is is explosives. Um it's hard to consistently drive the ball down the field in this league. At some point usually the offense makes a mistake or the defense just makes you make a mistake because, you know, an individual effort scheme what what have you. Um and and so that's the the second one. Don't overly stress it. I think that's kind of part of how we teach these guys from an offense perspective how to transition, how to knife up the field. Like it could be an 8-yard catch, but you could turn that into 16 if if you, you know, transition the right way. You have no wasted movement. And the same the flip side, I got to give these guys opportunities to go make explosive plays, whether it be getting them in space underneath or obviously attacking the intermediate deep deep parts of the zone. So a lot of different things, but you're right, it's very basic, but it's not easy. >> Last question here, Ted. >> The emphasis on 11-on-11, does that also come from from the Rams? Like you talked about your things like schedule, replay boards, that's come from you've seen it with other people and it works. Does the 11-on-11 emphasis also come from the Rams? >> Yeah, I mean I I want to say I I I want to say I'm I'm actually thinking about it right now. I don't I don't really remember. Outside of like non-padded, sometimes a Friday in season red zone um seven-on when it's just dropback, but I can't remember the last time with pads that that I've really done seven-on-seven. I got one for you. Jimmy Garoppolo coming back from his ACL in 2019, we had to do a little bit more seven-on-seven than than we were accustomed to cuz we had a So.

title: Princely Umanmielen: 'I executed discipline in all areas of my life'
text: Huh? >> Questions for you. >> Move it up. >> Quickly, uh we spoke to General Counsel the other day. He said you were probably the best pass rusher in the world. Um to get that title praise from a guy who's considered to be the top pass rusher in the league. What does that mean? And then what have you done during the off-season to kind of improve on what we saw last year? >> Um it it meant a lot, you know, I had saw it on Instagram and I had walked up to him and I told him I appreciate him for, you know what I'm saying, showing love and you Yeah, just showing love to me and yeah, it just means a lot coming from a guy that like that, you know, first round guy, guy that's made a name for himself in the NFL. And then you asked what what I did this off-season to improve my game. I mean, I feel like >> [clears throat] >> I just tried to tone in on just everything in my life as a whole, like I improved my sleep quality, how long I go to sleep, I improved my nutrition, start taking, you know what I'm saying, vitamins. I um start reading more, you know what I'm saying, I just tried to execute discipline in all areas of my life. >> What would you say got you to that point? Those aren't necessarily X's and O's kinds of life changes. >> Yeah. Uh I would say uh I would say actually giving my life to Christ. >> Did you get baptized? >> Mhm. >> Like to just elaborate. >> Uh I would say ever since, you know, I've been a uh Christian my whole life, but I didn't really uh you know what I'm saying, live completely like it and the moment that and it was actually before I got baptized that I fully, you know, started committing myself and actually started to see, you know, changes in my life and it wasn't it wasn't like a choice if that makes sense. You know what I'm saying? Like it just happened. I don't know how to really explain it, you know what I'm saying? I just started uh doing everything in my life a different way and uh it's been paying off for me. >> And actually with that, um you had posted on X about a month and a half ago logging off until I make the Pro Bowl. >> that all kind of align with this kind of new shaping of you and how has that been going staying off of that part of social media? >> Yeah, well, I was on the phone with my like uncle / mentor and he was talking about how social media is just no good and then he just went on to talk about how Twitter's especially not good. Like he was like there's no need to even have Twitter. And then he was like I was like I'll get off of it in like a week. He like no you not. He was like if you really serious then post logging off till you get a Pro Bowl. I'm like damn. And then I didn't do it for like a week and then I said, all right, I'm going to do it. So then I did it, ain't been on there since and what was the second part of your question? >> You said you've made a lot of other like kind of changes. I was asking how that all kind of coincides with the of just cleansing maybe from that part. >> Yeah, for sure. Yeah, Twitter was step one and then I was going to try to uh you know what I'm saying? Get off everything eventually. Instagram is the hardest. They didn't made some type of algorithm made it super addicting, but yeah, I'm trying to I'm trying to at least take a few months break from at least all social media. So step one was Twitter. >> You are a favorite. You are a fan favorite on social media. You >> I'm curious how you balance that because the fans like it. I'm sure you I'm sure you enjoy that interaction but I'm >> Yeah. I mean they can come mess with me on Instagram, but >> [laughter] >> um uh that's a good question. I mean, it's not like uh uh a lifelong thing, you know what I'm saying? I feel like um I feel like everybody should uh take uh breaks off of social media. I know a lot of people make their livelihoods from it. There's ways I can make uh money and things like that from social media. So, it's just short-term things, you know what I'm saying, and I'll be back and forth. >> You were pretty active. Were you like standing in the locker room now just saying things to guys that you normally tweet? >> Um I wouldn't say that. Um Dang, that's a I think I just No, I don't be doing that. I I just keep it to myself now. I get Well, I was active because I was saying things. Now, I don't see anything, so you know what I'm saying? >> So, your justice for your >> The way crew posts will be now on Instagram? >> You said what? It'll be on Instagram? Yeah. Instagram. >> Going back to the DeForest Buckner comment like about you being the best pass rusher, Canalis has kind of echoed a lot of that as well. He said, "What we need now is like the consistency." >> Do you see that as the next step in your game, and how do you get there to Do you have the skills, but now you're consistent play after play? I mean Um I feel like I've been uh doing a good job of displaying that. Obviously, we're still early on in camp. So, I'm going to try, you know, my best to just uh you know what I'm saying, let that continue. And I think the way that I do that on the field is by continuing to do it off the field. I've noticed like when I'm consistent in my life off the field, then I'm I'm it usually correlates to being consistent on the field. >> You've always been really good athlete. Is that something that I think you just didn't have to do in college? >> Yeah. I was like I kind of was just telling my little brother not too long ago. I'm like, "Bro, there's no question if like I was doing everything I'm doing now, I would have went first round." So, I like I'm trying to like tell him this, so you know what I'm saying, that he doesn't make the mistakes I make. You know, cuz I was very talented, and I look back, and I'm just like, "Damn, like I wasn't doing I was like I was telling him like I I couldn't imagine like what I would have been." And I was still very successful in college, but how much more successful I successful I could have been if I was living my life the way I am now. >> Do you feel like seeing your ex-big brother? >> Um to a certain extent, yeah, to a certain extent. >> Frankly, we haven't seen you, I don't think, since or haven't talked to you since Nick Bosa got injured. How did that affect you? >> Man, when I seen him down on the field, he wasn't making too much noise, so I thought he was okay. And then, once I seen him getting carted off the field, I just walked up to him, dapped him up, said it's going to be all right. I sent him a text after, and I and I just tried to comfort him, told him to you know, keep like keep God first throughout his throughout his journey and recovery. >> Nick going down is obviously tough for the team, but does open up opportunities potentially for you this season. Has it kind of sharpened your focus knowing that you guys are going to miss Nick, and you could potentially take that spot this second year? >> No, I wouldn't say it sharpened my focus because I was already on my focus was already sharpened, you know what I'm saying? So, you know what I'm saying, another guy going down didn't really change my mentality at all cuz I I came into this thing with the the same mentality. >> There was a play today where you and Jaylon both rushed together from the same side to to get to the pocket. What can this pass rush group kind of do now that you have all these different pieces? Obviously, you can't see Nick, but have all these different faces in there together. Like what how exotic can they be? >> I mean, I think we could be very successful. I feel like we just have to execute in in all aspects. You know, we got Jaylon, you know, Patrick's back. Patrick had a great first few games before he got injured, and then, you know, mid-season we're going to get Turk back, and you know, we just have a we have a room two rooms full of talent, and I think all we have to do is continue to execute and communicate with each other, and we'll be great. >> A couple more, please? >> Are you still in this young group of young guys that has to stay at the hotel for camp? >> And can you kind of give us a little snapshot of like what camp life, just life you around here or the hotel if there's y'all driving through. >> I mean for me, I wake up pretty early and then I I get to the hotel. I wouldn't say super late cuz we have a curfew, but I just the only time I'm in the hotel is when I'm sleeping. So, I probably look at the hotel for like 30 20 min minutes a day, you know what I'm saying? I go in there and I go to bed immediately, wake up, leave. So, really life is really in the locker room during camp. >> What's that like? >> Uh >> Is it different than the regular season? >> Just a lot of testosterone. >> Yeah, but what are you looking forward to most about the game Thursday night? And and >> I'm looking forward to being on the sideline in a jumpsuit. >> No. Uh I mean, if I do play, I'm just looking forward to displaying uh my skills and the work that I've been putting in this off season. >> What can the team get out of it all? I know obviously most of you started learning to be playing, but what can you guys get out of a game like this? I know it's >> Um I mean, especially for the young guys, I feel like we could see I mean, what we could get out of it is seeing guys uh seeing what guys can put on tape, you know? And you know, if if I play, seeing what I could put on tape and it just um and and uh the older guys, you know, coaching up the young guys and helping guide them. >> Are you expecting to play or to be out? >> I actually have no clue. I don't know. Hm? >> But you got the jumpsuit ready? >> Ironed. >> Thank you guys. >> Appreciate it. >> [music] [music]

title: Brandt Tilis: 'Bryce's ceiling is unknown'
text: Uh hey everyone. Um just wanted to start off by thanking the fans for coming out to Fan Fest. Uh that was an incredible showout for our fans. Uh I don't know how many were there exactly, but in February when we were going over the schedule for the preseason, I was I was talking to Christy Coleman and and she was adamant that it be on a weekend night. And so we we planned the the schedule around that and I was like, "Okay, well, you know, we'll see how many people show up." And it was definitely exceeded our expectations on the football operations. So, way to go, fans, and thank you for all the support. Um to that end, you know, you guys have seen the sales center and some of the renderings for the stadium. Like that's that project is really exciting. I'm I'm happy to play a small role in it uh with our group. Um and just a a lot of credit goes to Christy and Jake Burns and Eric Sodol for for all that that's gone into that. Um as for on the field here, you guys saw another competitive practice. Um I think that's kind of been the uh the mantra of this training camp is just compete and and bring your best. So, excited to see that and see what else happens. So, with that, I'll take your questions. >> How much has analytics played into the way you guys look at the waiver wire towards cut down deadline, but also shaping your roster numbers and like what you know you need and all the practice squad as well as the draft? >> A lot. I mean, we're always looking at data. Eric Eric Eager and and and his crew, um they provide us a lot of good insight into things that have happened in in the past and and what we can expect in the future. And and Dan and coach do a great job of of weighing all that as they make their their decisions. >> You um your department a lot of credit during free agency for bringing you in. How much do you get freedom now like as opposed to like the off season? Is this more like when you're rebuilding kind of negotiate new things in the tryout year or draft year? >> You're talking about like my personal schedule? >> like as far as like doing the roster management of negotiating contracts or bringing in people to work out. >> Yeah. So, everything we do is collaborative and that's that's how we've we've wanted to build it. So, yeah, the more that Eric can do, the more we can collaborate on other things and the more I can collaborate with Eric when you know, when when the projects get built up to where they need to where they need to be to present to Dan or to coach. Um and vice you know, vice versa with anything else we do with whether it be cap management or operations or anything like that. Um the more we can all work together, the better the better our results are going to be. >> Brian, how valuable is the extra preseason game as you're sort of evaluating all the way down the roster? >> It's funny. I it is valuable and and a lot of teams they they look at it as a kind of as a boon, but for us it's a it is it is going to be a tool for us to be able to evaluate the roster and and really see some of these some of these guys and and how they're ascending and and how they're competing against against other teams. So, it's exciting for us. >> Brian, I know we have to ask about Bryce, his extension and where you guys are in talks about that. >> Yeah, any any extensions whether it's with Bryce or anybody else, any of those negotiations we'll just keep those conversations internal and and amongst the organization and the agent. >> Last year you talked to me and characterized Bryce as an ascending player. I am curious with the benefit of another season, how you would characterize where he is now. >> Yeah. Um I would state I would say he he ascended last year and and and there's still room for him to ascend. Like his his ceiling currently is unknown and and I think that's exciting for us and and he's he's working hard to uh uh to to get himself there. >> What would you want to call it on the >> Cuz it could be I mean it it could be it could be here. It like we don't know where it is. >> what I'm asking is would you have thought you'd have a better idea of of where that ceiling is at this point? >> Not necessarily. I the the team is growing, too. So, he's he you know, he's going to ascend as the team ascends and and vice versa, the team is going to get better as as as he does. So, it's all it's all good. >> You guys have one of the smallest set of third guys that are 30 or older that are not specialists. How much have you guys factoring age when it comes to extensions as well as how you're building this roster in your guys' image? >> Where So, wait. We're we're like low in under 30 players? >> You're you're Yeah, you're >> Oh, that's that's kind of cool. >> You're bottom three as far as >> Oh, wow. >> who has guys over 30. Um >> You have Moton, you have some other guys >> I got it. >> Like how much has age factored into how you guys have built this stuff? >> It does. It factors because we're when when when we when we do anything with our roster, we are projecting into the future and we're making a prediction as to how this player is going to play. And and there's more upside, obviously, with younger players and there's and there's more certainty that that there's going to be a you know, a high level of play with a younger player. That doesn't mean we're only going for younger players. It just means that that that they end up getting all the tiebreakers. >> Frank, going back to Bryce for a second, uh it's kind of understood that third year in a system is really important for a quarterback. Do you think the Panthers have provided a [clears throat] a really good option for Bryce to show what he can do for you. >> Absolutely. Yeah. Yeah, we the team the team is better, the coaches are good. Um and Bryce is putting in the work, too. So, it's it's all there. And like we'll just see how the year plays out. And I think we're all really excited for what Bryce is going to show and and how the team's going to be. >> So, what's your philosophy as far as discussing potential or even preliminary talks when it comes to extending your what you call it, franchise? >> What do you mean? >> Like in the past, you've done these deals before. Do you decide Do you go into talks ahead of season? What is your What is your overall philosophy >> Yeah, you >> in this type of situation? >> I mean, it's a Look, it's a just like anything else we were just talking about with the organization, it's all collaborative. So, I could have my ideas. Dave and Dan may want to do something else. So, like we're all going to meet together and then we got to meet meet the player where where he is. So, it's it's a case-by-case thing and you know, it's it is it's good to have good players. >> Grant, understanding >> understanding where you're at with Bryce and having team options for next year, but I mean, do you want to get something done before the season starts or does it not matter? >> I want what's best for the organization. And so, that's not for me to to decide, but it's it's again, it's a collaborative deal. >> On that same note, just a second ago, you said we'll see how the year plays out. Which would indicate you're going to let it play out this year. Is that Is that been discussed this side? >> Again, all those discussions I'll just keep to with the within us. >> Grant, what worries you this time of year? What what keeps you makes it hard for you to sleep at night? What makes you nervous? >> Yeah, that's a good question. >> It sounds crazy. I'm already on to next year. Like I'm looking at next year and I'm seeing, all right, what's the team going to look like next year? How are things going? How are we going to feel the team? Who's going to be on that team? So on and so forth. So I I I spend a lot of time on that. Um I'm lucky to have Justin Davidoff who who works with me and and he gives me a lot of good insight there. But it's really that. Um That's where that's where my mind That's where my worried is. >> This is a question about 2026 but also 2027 as you mentioned. Ickey Ekwonu is playing his or well, sidelined now, but this is his fifth year. Um and and he's got obviously the fifth-year option. What is the future like with him? Uh and I know you can't disclose time or you're not going to disclose time like that injury, but like how do you approach his year knowing that he might not play for a substantial amount of this year? >> Yeah, it's a known thing, right? Like his his salary is known. His injury is known. And we'll just let the whole thing play out and look, if if Ickey can come back during the season, that's great. That I mean you can't have enough good players on your roster and Ickey is certainly a good player in this league. So, you know, he's working He's working his tail off out there and and we're excited to hopefully get him back. >> You talked about how you like to look ahead to the season prior. Um I would imagine this time last year you were probably looking ahead about maybe a guy like Ickey and the only thing I had was the fifth-year option. How much did that injury impact any potential plans you guys would have? >> Yeah, so I can't I'm not going to talk about Ickey in particular, but just in general like health is certainly a factor in any contract decision that we make. title: Dave Canales: 'Love to see the energy'
text: All right, finally some heat. We got a little a little humidity out there. Sun came out for us. Perfect. It's what we need as we get ready for the season, but a lot of great energy first day back. Some rust to knock off after a couple of days following Fan Fest just getting the guys bodies right. A lot of recovery happening. But they worked through it. We had a little break in between. They came out. They were all chirping and competing by the end of it in our two-minute drill. So just love the guys coming out here pushing themselves getting themselves game ready and and love to see the energy and feel that today. >> Dave, Felipe has been a guy who's been pretty aggressive, but he was kind of on the receiving end of the play today and didn't respond afterwards. What type of growth do you see in guys maybe with the physicality of the game? >> He's one of us. He just, you know, his response was great. He pops up, signals a first down. Now, clock is running. We're in a two-minute drill, okay? We can't put the ball on the ground. You catch the ball, you get knocked down, whatever. The ball's got to stay right there on the hash and hand it to the center. I've seen the ball get kicked around and teams lose precious seconds, you know, 8 to 10 seconds because the ball's all over the place. You're celebrating. I know you're excited, but we got it was we needed a touchdown to win the drill, so now we just take the next step, right? It's it's it's part of the progression, but Felipe has been doing a great job. Just playing his butt off, playing a physical style of football, which we love. And so glad he was able to make a big play on that drive. >> Is it possible he knew the clock was stopped for the penalty? >> I I don't think so. I don't The flag came out from the flag came out from way on the sideline, so but I let's give him the benefit of the doubt, Joe. Okay? >> A minute or two later, we saw T-Mac go up. That You've had a couple practices now in with Bryce and T-Mac hooking up. What do you attribute that to? It could be another year together, but is there something more to it than that? >> Yeah, it's just about time on task. It's about opportunities, and I really love that Bryce has been giving him opportunities down the field. You know, just really trying to stretch it, some of the vertical concepts that we have. T-Mac does a great job of holding the defender off, uh playing it at the high point, you know, um he feels strong, he looks great, so I love seeing those plays. Those are game-changing plays in a drive when we can take a an explosive on the outside in a one-on-one matchup, so something we have to take advantage of. I love that they're taking those opportunities. >> Is there any picket play on Thursday? >> Yeah, Kenny will start the game off. Um for how long, I'm not sure, but uh we have a we have a good number of guys, um you know, that'll be helping out early on in the game. Um just just because we don't want to overload any one particular group on our team. We do have practices leading into the game, and we have practices coming out of it. So, I felt that with the with the number of guys um being out there, being able to take a couple of series, will really help the whole group, and we just need the football. So, I'm excited about it, and uh Kenny's excited as as as well as uh rest of the group, and they've been talking a lot about it. >> So, no main starters? >> No starters? >> Yeah, no starters. So, uh there are some competition battles for starting positions where guys will have an opportunity to play a little bit, but um some of the guys we're expecting to be out there right off the bat, you know, I think we won't play those guys in this game. >> Okay, so no one really just to be clear. >> Correct. >> Dave, given your experience over the first two seasons, how did you decide how you wanted to manage playing time through the preseason? >> Yeah, it you know, this this does uh present kind of a unique situation. We report early. Um we got a little bit of extra time that does give us a chance to evalue our evaluate our players. There's always things that show up in the first three to five days of camp, whether it's a uh ankle, knee, back, calf, hamstring, whatever. There's stuff that that guys may come in with that aren't that present once you start playing football. So, we've had an opportunity for a couple of guys that we've held out of some practices um to to catch those, and really gain that time on the back end. So, that was that was one part of it. The second part is just figuring out how to play four preseason games. Again, it's been a while for me um Um, since we've gone to the three preseason game kind of rotation, but this is valuable. These are valuable opportunities for all these guys fighting for these positions, whether it's on the active roster or on practice squad, just more game reps uh to be able to see what they can do and how they can take the game plan and make it come alive on the field. >> On that T-Mac catch, again, to end practice, right? We saw that before, and I'm just it looked like good coverage, just a better play by the offense. Like to end on a play like that, what does that do for just the team sort of go out like >> Well, it's by design. We try to oscillate between having the ones finish the practice, having the twos or threes finish the practice, and I just like having that finish moment. Everybody knows here's the last drill, minute some odd seconds, no timeouts, got to have a touchdown to win it. Um, we just have to be comfortable in those positions and to to see the guys, you know, it was really a fantastic coverage on the, you know, the play before with Will Lee. Early hold, put the ball down there at the 14-yard line for one more opportunity for the offense. So, again, it was a good uh teachable moment for the group. We got to be clean with our hands, we got to be clean on the pre-snap, so we don't give the opponent any advantage. >> What have you seen out of Kenny so far? >> Uh, just really efficient and again, a veteran player, so he knows how to work, he knows how to study and prepare for a day. So, he comes out and all the checks are right, getting the protections the way you want it to, and then on top of that, just, you know, every day there seems to be some special throw down the field. He's got that in his bag, and then for us now, it's just about catching him up with all the concepts, so he feels really comfortable and rhythmic, and that's what we're still in the middle of of uh working. >> Dave, you brought up the opportunities. >> Before that last catch on the T-Mac, Will had a few good pass breakups. How important is it to have him in there facing the ones and like getting that tough work this early on? >> Absolutely, that's where we make us. That's how we get better as Will going against the best guys uh that we have to put out there, and he's responded really well. He's given up some plays, he's made a lot of great plays, had a chance at an interception on one of them, just couldn't come away with it, but he's putting himself in the right position and that's where it all starts. Assignment, technique, being physical so you can make a play and that's where he continues to grow daily. >> Dave, you've heard of opportunities Jackson can watch at linebacker and not being able to tackle live here but getting some opportunities and getting some live reps on special teams. How can that impact his standing within your roster and within your depth chart? >> That's a huge opportunity for Jackson on the defensive side, but especially in that in that special teams role. As we know, you only get a certain amount of guys on game day. So, if you're not out there with the starting group, you will be playing special teams. He looks ama- He looks really good. He's big and he's fast. He's smart. He's taking to the concepts. Now, can he make it come alive in a live setting and get the guy down in space? Another great opportunity for him. He'll have multiple opportunities throughout this preseason to show what he can do. >> Dave, on Kingsley, can you just talk about what you want from Kingsley this year? >> Yeah, Kingsley, just take the next step. You know, for him it it was about, you know, we know he's got pass rush. Can he be consistent in execution across the board with different play styles, with different play types, whether it's play action, run game, the different types of runs and how the outside linebacker has to play those runs. He's got to have all those things um in his tool belt to be able to know how to take on different blocks, the sift blocks from tight ends, the bluff blocks, taking on tackles, uh gap schemes, all those things. It's all just gathering that information so that he can be the complete player we believe he can be. Um that can rush the passer, but that can also give you valuable downs on first and second down. Mitchell Evans was back was back today. Tommy Tremble was back today. Bobby Brown obviously comes off the non-football injury list. Does it feel good to And Robert Hunt obviously back. Does it feel good to kind of have some good injury news uh this offseason? >> Absolutely, and that was all a part of that early week, you know, just getting in, starting camp a week earlier. All those guys kind of working through some things, you know, working through some some nicks here and there and we were able to just attack it here in in our facilities and get them in return to play, address those issues so that we can get them back on the field when they were ready. And so we've gone through these processes with them. It feels good to have a fuller group than we've had and we still got guys like De Lu who's waiting to come back, you know. Siddique Charles did did have a little bit of a calf. We're going to look at that this afternoon and kind of see where we're at. So add one, one goes out. It's kind of the nature of this thing and so but we'll give you more information on that as it as it plays out. >> So going back to Felipe, he had a couple of back-to-back plays with really good strong catches. I know he's been playing tight end for a few years now but in your opinion, what is the challenge of giving a quarterback receiver hands and how long does that take? >> Well, the hands really aren't the issue, you know, cuz you got to think quarterbacks, especially in college now, I mean they're taking shotgun snaps every play. So So most quarterbacks I've been around have amazing hands. But it's all the other stuff. It's it's blocking in line, it's how you fit into the run game, play actions and then the drop back pass game and filling zones. Those are all lessons that Felipe's still accumulating. While he's while he's had a chance to really make an impact as a special teams player, that's why we try to preach it to our guys. When you can contribute in special teams, you buy yourself time to develop in your position, whether it's offense or defense. But special teams is really critical, really important to us here. So that's where it starts but I love seeing Felipe just continue to grow in our scheme. >> Hey we'll have we'll have two more questions here. >> Uh Bryce coming in I'm not sure we'll ask him about Bryce's long-term future as well. >> Yeah. >> From your perspective, what you're seeing out of Bryce and what are you pleased with and what do you feel like he still needs to grow with? >> Yeah, I'm just really excited. You know, the special plays still show up every day. Um moving up the spot, pushing up in the pocket, layering balls, all the accuracy. But the part that I've been really impressed with this camp is just the the chemistry with the with our receivers, the time on task with Jaylen Coker, T-Mac, Xavier Legette, JT Sanders in the tight end group who have been around for a while and now it just seems like he's playing so much faster. It just seems like he's eliminating things before the snap. On his drop, he's starting to eliminate and evaluate things and throwing really anticipatory throws. I got to think, you know, a couple interceptions throughout camp like he's on the money, receivers not quite where they need to be and the these are trust throws. These are things where your whole soul's got to be behind that throw when you hit the back foot, the ball's coming out. That creates opportunity for conversation in the media room to say, "Hey, look, this is how this is my timing on this play and here's when the ball's got to get out. I need you there a little sooner." And those types of things. And so, um that part a lot of just growth in leadership in terms of talking to the players for what he wants on particular routes from the tight ends, from the wideouts in the slot, you know, um where he sees the ball going, where he sees them attacking the leverage of the player. So, I love where he's headed, love that he's all in. He seems to be really enjoying it and um so we just keep taking it day at a time and and try to challenge ourselves that way. >> Everybody good? >> Good. >> All right, thank >> You? You got anything? >> Uh what's your haircut playlist for the new season? >> Uh well, we're we're definitely we're definitely going Common Kings, um a little bit of a Bone Thugs N Harmony, maybe some Jay Bug, and then the green the green pops up like every other song. So, as I learn these these crews, you know, it's my Friday routine. So, just please, you know, give me give me about an hour, you know, and then we can get to our family business. Thank you. All right. >> [music] [music]

title: 2026 Panthers Training Camp Live
text: and welcome to training camp live. Anish Thomas Davis giving you a bird's eye view and an inside look at Panthers training camp. TD we get a look at Chuba Hubard getting loose uh before the start of practice today. This was a big season for the Panthers coming off eight and nine we know, but first place in the division, first playoff birth since 2017, first division title since 2015. The theme all off seasonason has been okay now build off the momentum. >> Yes sir. All of these things that you talked about have been momentum builders for this football team and confidence boost for these players. It gave them an opportunity to see what they were capable of. And then we go out, we make a a bunch of acquisitions, bring in guys that can definitely help improve this roster. And you just saw one there warming up and Devin Lloyd. Man, these this team by far is the the best roster that we've had in a long time. There's a lot of depth and there's a lot of excitement for a lot of players. You saw Jonathan Brooks a moment ago. He's coming off the two ACL's. The early reports out of camp have been good. And you know a little something about coming off multiple ACL surgeries. >> Unfortunately, I do. But you know, it's just one of those things, man, where you can build your confidence back up and you can build it up fast. And uh being out of the game gives you an opportunity to learn a lot about yourself and to learn a lot about the game. >> Yeah, Panthers getting stretched out. Uh, we'll take you through the start of practice. I think it goes without saying, listen, this is a big season for Bryce Young. It's his fourth year, third year in the system. He had his fifth year option picked up in the off season. If he takes that next incremental leap, well, the Panthers are going to be right in the thick of things again. If he takes that massive leap, it's going to be great for the franchise. Certainly, it's going to be great for Bryce Young and his financials going forward. >> Absolutely. He's going to put himself exactly where he wants to be. Man, Bryce to me has gotten better every single year. You know, over the first couple of years, there was a lot of lot of change within the organization from the coaching standpoint, but now he's had the opportunity to have more continuity over the last couple of years. And now with that, we're going to continue to see an ascension of Bryce Young and watch him grow more and more as the roster continues to improve around him. that is that lens for him having a better year and his career just continuing to get better. >> And TD, what we saw going back to OTAA is you're watching a guy who's more comfortable now, more vocal, >> y >> right the the leadership role. He's embracing that more. You know, there was maybe a side of him where he was a people pleaser early in his career and maybe that's still there, but we're starting to see, as Dan Morgan likes to say, that dog and him come out a little more. He's starting to be a lot more assertive and I think with that it he's taking command of this football team. It's something that you want out of your quarterback. I think kind of early on he was kind of thrust into the captain role, but now the difference is he's earned the captain role because he's going out and he's really being more vocal like you talked about. he's not accepting certain things in practice that he was accepting and and allowing to happen as the leader of the of the football team. So now as Bryce Young continues to develop and he's continues to get better, not only can he focus in on being a better football player, but he's doing a much better job of being a much better leader. >> You know, you go back to last year, he had six game-winning drives. The only Panthers quarterbacks with more game-winning drives are Jake Delhom and Cam Newton. He's in rare company when it comes to his fourth quarter magic. How do we get that version, the version we see when they play the Falcons? How do we get that for the course of a season for 17 games and 60 minutes? >> You know what I want to see? And I've been saying this for a long time. If you look at those situations like the comeback situations, the game-winning drives, all of those happen in hurry up situations. And to me, Bryce Young operates a lot better in those moments. So, as a offensive coordinator, my thought process would be create those moments throughout the course of the game and pick up the tempo and force the defense to have to react to what we're doing. If I know that my young quarterback operates at a high level when we have uptempo and we're moving that fast, I'm gonna create those opportunities more often for him to see if that's a part of the process and it takes the thinking out of it for him. >> That's going to be fascinating because teams often play close to the vest in terms of play calling and game planning in the preseason, but Dave Canales called the plays the last two years. He turns that over to Brad Idz. Now, I think that's going to be an interesting storyline to watch. Yes, in preseason, more so early in the regular season. What are the wrinkles that I brings to this offense? >> You know, I think it just creates a new dissension for this team. It gives other teams something else to have to worry about when they get ready to face the Panthers because, you know, you can get dialed in on what certain coordinators do coming into a season and you've practiced it throughout the off season and you know what to expect. But now they're going to be a lot of new wrinkles. We're going to do some of the same stuff that coach Canales ran obviously. But there going to be some wrinkles that are going to improve this offense and make them better. And for a head coach to make that decision to release those titles, those duties as a play caller when that's has been his mo for a long time, that just shows you his confidence in his coordinators and his ability to just step back and lead the team in other areas. And there's Brad Idzik with the blue long sleeves and the white hat on the walkie-talkie. He's the play caller. He had the title of offensive coordinator the last couple of seasons, but now he takes over play calling duties. What does that now allow Dave Canalis to do, not having to be the play caller in game every week? >> You know, it just allows him to focus in on the whole team. like he get to focus in more on the defense and what's going on on their side, focusing in on the um on the special teams and what they're doing. And when you are able to do that as a as a head coach, you can take complete control of your football team. Not saying that he didn't have that before, but when you're making offensive play calling your main thing as a head coach, it's kind of harder to really focus in on all of the other areas of the game. But coach Canales is in the position now where he has the utmost confidence in coach Isac and now that's going to allow him to completely lock in in all of these other areas. So I'm excited about that. >> Yeah, we talked a little bit about Bryce Young. Dave Canales has always said a big part of the offensive philosophy is it starts with the run game. And Chuba Hubard looking for a bounceback season. He was tremendous two years ago. Injuries got to him last year. We talked to him after one of the games. I think it was the Rams regular season game and Jake Delhomme asked him a really good question on the air uh about how banged up he was and Chuba first tried to downplay it and then Jake pressed him on it and you know Chuba opened up and I'm not sure people realized how hurt he was. Yeah. And how he played through that last season. But if he can be healthy and then you know the big wild card in all this is uh Jonathan Brooks who we've been you know wanting to see now for a couple of years. It's been really three years since he's had any kind of workload. You got to go back to his last year at Texas. What are reasonable expectations for Jonathan Brooks? >> Man, I think the sky is the limit for this kid. >> That's not reasonable. I said reasonable. [laughter] >> That's that's what's reasonable for me with with Jonathan Brooks, man. You get to watch him work out throughout the offseason. You get to watch the mindset that this kid has. You see him right now, he just loves football. He loves the game. and he brings a new energy and a and a new element to this offense. He's big, he's fast, he's physical, and he plays the game the right way at the running back position. He's a guy that you can leave on the field on all three downs. And when I say that, a lot of times on third down, the team will take a guy off the field because they're not that good at pass protection. They're not that good at catching the ball out of the back field. But I think Jonathan Brooks is one of those guys. He can do it all. He was the number one running back coming out of the draft a couple of years ago, even coming out with a ACL injury. So, that says a lot about what we thought about him and what other teams thought about Jonathan Brooks. And now, just being able to see him go out and put it all together and and hopefully have a healthy, successful season. Man, I just think that he has the opportunity to give us that one-two punch that we had when we had Rico Do last year as well. The onetwo punch has been a staple for the Panthers in their history on some of their better teams whether it was Steven Davis, Deshawn Foster. You played with Jonathan Stewart, D'Angelo Williams, Rico and Chuba last year. And one thing that we've noticed having been out there at training camp, Brooks's ability to catch the ball out of the back field, >> that gives your offensive coordinator, your play caller some options, some creativity. It's a very small sample size. The Panthers only used 21 personnel 19 times last year. >> Yeah, >> they averaged six yards per play. That's two running backs, one tight end. I go back a couple of years ago, Dave Canal said to me, he said, "Hey, when Brooks was getting ready to come back," I said, "Are you guys looking at potential two running back, 21 personnel formations?"
