He he means a lot not only to the defense, but to the team as well. the energy he brings and uh day in and day out uh is just great and uh yeah you know very excited to have him back and you know that you know hopefully we can take some you know take take you know his mind away on some other stuff of of some other stuff and just you know kind of focus on football but it's just been great to you know be able to give him a hug and just focus in on you know the main thing but it's it's been good to have him back >> urge not to put you in the spotlight for that but you did get emotional when you were in the shock about your teammates >> that uh I mean, just the brotherhood that we have, like the um just the unless you've been in the locker room, you can't it's it's kind of hard to put it into words, but just the the the brotherhood that we have, like you know, there's a lot of people that come in and go, but you know, what we go through on a daily basis. I mean, it's it's not easy and I feel like it just brings us closer together. And like I said, like I love those guys. You know, it goes above football and you know, I'll do anything for those guys. And I feel like kind of reflects in the way I play as far as like just picking guys up, you know, always staying positive. Even though, you know, I might have a bad play, but Bean might break off at 20 yards and I'll be the first one there to pick him up. And whether Kyle catch a pass or whether whether Mike's down, I'll just be the first one to be there to pick him up. So like I love those guys. And even on defense, like you know, when Jesse gets a pick or whatever, like you first one to celebrate no matter what. So I'm just those guys mean they mean the world to me for sure. Slowly this front run office is taking care of these extensions to put these pieces in place for a long time. How much do you believe in the future of what's going on here offensively? >> I mean, yeah, it was a big part. It was a big part on why like I I wanted to get this deal done. Just to see the the attention to detail that coach Stfansky has and Ian and just the the the vision and the the culture that they try to bring in here in Atlanta is just is just awesome. And you could see that, you know, from the starting otaas. So, just very very grateful that I'll be here, you know, with those guys for hopefully a long time. But, uh, yeah, I mean, what they've been doing has been awesome and I'm, you know, fully bought in and I think it's it's it's truly it's going to be truly a great turnaround for sure. Matthew, for so long, we've been talking about you and and Drake and Kyle as kind of like the the young group and and now that you all are receiving extensions, like do you feel like there's greater ownership of kind of like this team that we're we're kind of stepping into that real like pillar role? >> For sure. I think I think you know the guys that you mentioned obviously are you know foundation piece uh for not only for our offense but for the team as well. Just you know Drake Kyle are just great leaders and I think yes, I think you're right. It just is becoming slowly like as the years go by goes by is slowly becoming like our team and there's there's definitely more ownership on the way we practice uh you know if practice is sloppy like we we'll definitely say so and just be able to speak up and kind of hold oursel accountable but also hold the team accountable when uh things are right and also just buying in what coach Stfensky uh is you know is trying to do here. And apologies, I walked in a little bit late if anybody asked this, but first day of pads, like is is that like the best day of the year for you or like what's your mentality when you approach this this particular game? >> I mean, there's definitely some excitement, you know, uh you know, you know, I was I was talking for me it was I was kind of a little rusty out there obviously just kind of getting the handles, getting your hands right, the timing right, and uh so yeah, I just obviously you got to keep working, keep grinding, and you know, once the first day when once the first day goes by, you kind of got to get in rhythm. So it was it was a little sloppy. uh personally, but I just kind of get back on getting get in rhythm and just yeah, just kind of get back to it. >> Uh leading off of that, because you play in the trenches um and are making contact with people basically all the time, can you explain some similarities and differences playing such a physical position with pads and without? >> Uh it's just kind of the the handle and kind of getting the timing of it right. Just kind of your hands. I think it's it's definitely a hands and a leverage game. And I, you know, I think that the defensive line, they play a certain way when it's without pads, obviously, because you're trying to avoid contact. And once the pads come on, you kind of, they kind of play it a different way to kind of put it simple. And you kind of just have to get used to that. And, you know, it's been a while since we haven't had pads on. And, you know, kind of knock the rust off and get back to it. >> Speaking of that hand technique, I'm just curious, do you do any sort of cross training and other things? I know like we were talking to Chris Winstrom the other day and he was talking about doing some boxing, some other things. Do you do anything like that or is it just kind of football related stuff that you train? >> Uh for me during offseason it's more football related stuff just kind of going out on the field, you know, obviously hitting on bags and hitting on, you know, people without bags, you know, it's it's you're never going to get the true feelings of pads. So, it's kind of hard to replicate that. But just kind of getting your your feet right, your your timing right, just your center, your spot and stuff like that is stuff that you can work on out there, you know, with with nobody. So, that's that's kind of what I've been working on offseason. Uh, I've I've heard that Chris is a pretty good boxer, so I can't imagine. He's very twitchy and he has his his hands are super fast. So, uh, yeah, I heard a number of good things about it. So, I might try it. I might try it. It' be a good thing to try. >> I asked uh Divine the style of play between Tua and obviously Mike. He said Tua was more decisive. He said Mike was a little savvy. What how would you describe their style on the field and how they are in the huddle and how they go about their business? Uh, I would say like the way uh, Tua approaches the huddle, like he's very like he he'll take, you know, things in charge and he's very like outspoken and stuff like that. And I feel like Mike is more like he's going to do what he does on the field and he he lets his game talk more than anything. Uh, so, you know, they they they both have different ways to approach it and I feel like they both good and uh, you know, I'm very excited for those guys. They've been doing a great job so far. So, I think it's it's just great to have two, you know, awesome quarterback, not only good quarterback, but good dudes in the locker room as well. And, uh, yeah, just very happy to have those guys on the team. >> You also had a chance to obviously Jack's taken a lot of, uh, reps with the ones. What's it like for him in there? What can fans expect to see from a guy like that? >> Dude, like, you know, I started as a rookie. I I kind of got thrown in the fire when the the left guard got hurt, my my rookie year pass. And like, he's handled it like awesome. like Jack's been an awesome job as far as just the communication aspect and obviously quarterback position is it's not easy. There's a lot of stuff going on and just you know just saying to play in a huddle can seem kind of easy but it's actually hard. There's like a bunch of words and stuff like that. So him just being able to do that, communicate with us. He's he's done an awesome job. So I'm very excited for him and just for him to prove what he can do, you know, it's an awesome opportunity. Uh I was kind of the same situation. Somebody got hurt had to step in and you know now I'm here. So, you know, for him to be able to do that and just step in and, you know, show what he can do on the field is an awesome opportunity. So, very happy for him. And he's a he's a good dude, so it's good to see. >> Has anything changed for you with with two left-handed quarterbacks on the team, though? >> Uh, it's pretty similar. Uh, you know, they both mobile quarterbacks, so it's it's it's pretty similar for me. And uh yeah, so not much difference, you know, for that. Matthew, a lot of people have brought up um coach Callahan kind of how he can use examples from all of the players that he's coached his long career. Is there anybody that he's mentioned or brought up where you see some similarities between your game and kind of their game? >> Uh I mean I would say not really, but I trying to take like stuff from every everything that he shows. Just kind of trying to find something that I can relate to. you know, obviously the t I'm not a tackle no more. So when he shows clips of Trent, like it's kind of hard for me to apply that, but just kind of see what he does and his his approach and stuff like that where I can learn and kind of apply that to my game. But it's kind of it's kind of hard to relate to one player. But if I can just grab different things from different players and just add that to my game, you know, it's always good to have a good arsenal that you can use on the on game day to kind of switch it up, you know. Uh, no. Kind of, you know, you ask rookies like what they're what the first thing they're going to buy when a new contract. Yeah. Anything that you plan on >> uh on buying? Uh, just uh, you know, my family always been they they always been there for me. So, just, you know, making sure they're taken care of and obviously, uh, you know, a goal of mine, you know, even before I signed the contract was to give back to the community. And I feel like now I just have more resources to do so. So, you know, definitely be more involved in uh in the community. You know, Atlanta's given me so much. So, it's, you know, it's only right to give back. So, uh you know, very excited to do that. And I'm into cars, so I'll definitely buy some cool cars for sure. >> No F1 tickets with the first check. >> Uh maybe in offseason. Maybe in offseason, but uh but right now, I think I'm going to stick to that. What >> kind of cars do you want to get? >> Uh so, I I like muscle cars, you know, American American engineering. So maybe a C6 ZR1 and a 70 Hemikuda. So those are my top two right now. So yeah. Yeah. >> Uh pivoting back to my other question, can you elaborate a little bit on how uh defenses approach uh playing against you differently with pads versus not? >> I mean, you know, they they can use uh power rushes now. They can use a lot more contact. It can be a lot lot more physical. And they can use movement. you know, when you don't have pads on, you kind of take the movement away to avoid any sort of uh, you know, contact or whatsoever. So, now they can kind of use that to, you know, disrupt and uh, yeah, disrupt the run game, the passing game. And you see a lot more pressure as well. >> How was the first day of pass? And, uh, what it feel like to actually put your hands on somebody like that? >> It always feels good to put my hands on somebody. First day pass was good. Um, a little sloppy. Well, not sloppy. Uh, a little fatigue. You can tell. We just got to get in shape and that's what camp's for. you also uh first time having Brick back in the building since you know losing his wife. What was that like and what's kind of been the overarching theme that you guys have kind of taken to coach? >> Man, I love Brick. He's like a I don't know a father figure older brother for me. Um so I I was glad to have him back out here. I hugged him as soon as I seen him. Um everybody just wants to play for Brick at the end of the day. Um he he really believes in heart mind fish and that's that's what the defense all about. So uh we're just we're just out there to play for him. >> What are you most excited about with this group? got a lot of couple different new faces around you, especially next to you with that linebacker squad. What are you most excited about with this defense? >> I'm excited about the speed of this defense and that everybody hungry. We all trying to play. We all trying to get better. So, that's the most that's what I'm most excited about. >> Divine, we often talk about how play action can benefit an offense, but I'm curious from your position as the linebacker, it's intended to kind of fool. What are you looking for to diagnose whether something's actually a handoff or a play action pass? >> Uh, usually the old lineman. I feel like if they really come off the ball, that's that's more of a hint at a run play. When they're kind of trying to just stay even, stay at the line, that's that's when you know you can get out and uh play action's coming. >> On Kendall, how how does he look in your opinion? >> Uh I think Kendall and Perk, they both look great. Uh they're way ahead what I expect from any rookie. So, uh they're doing a great job. Obviously, they got to keep it up. Uh we'll see more in the preseason, but I'm excited. >> Ahead in what way? >> Uh just mentally. They're they're they're really smart guys. Uh they know what they do. They don't they don't mess up a lot. They're just on there peas and keys. For sure. >> I I believe Brick said back in in May about Kendall that he's kind of a lot like you were. Sure. >> Have you tried to help him out a lot at all so far here? >> Oh, yeah. Yeah. Whatever question he asked, uh um uh I'll answer him obviously and then if I see anything on the field that he might need help with, I I'll let him know for sure. >> I kind of heard him like like really yelling and like talking loud out there. For a young guy, how impressive is that, do you think? >> Like I said earlier, uh they're extremely ahead uh than what I expect them to be. So yeah, it's very impressive and hopefully they can keep it going. >> Devon, how do you think this defense can take a step forward this year? >> Uh, I would say consistency. I feel like uh there were games where we were on top. Um, and then there were games we really just took a dip off or let the game go. Um, so consistency, just playing the same way every every game. >> You personally heading into this year, you're obviously going to be a big piece of what you guys are trying to accomplish on defense. Where does your mentality lie in what you're trying to accomplish? >> Honestly, uh, I just want to be the best version of myself for this team. uh whatever I can do, if that's extra studying, um extra recovery, extra endurance, like getting in shape, I I'll do it. But I just want to be the best version of myself. >> How do you feel like you personally took a step forward last year >> compared to this year or Oh, uh just in general? >> Oh, just Oh, like Oh, yeah. Over my career. Uh last year, I think, um like I said, just doing the extra stuff. Uh I was doing all the extra studying extra. So, and working with these guys, Iron Sharp Iron, he he mentioned that earlier or somebody mentioned that earlier. I feel like having one like top 10 in each position of the best weapons on offense is great to have out here. It it forces us to work. So, that's a good thing. >> Dean, how has your role changed with Kaden Ellis gone now? >> Uh, obviously I got to step up, be more of a leader, uh, be more vocal. Um, if the energy is down at practice, just pick everybody up. Just just small things, nothing too crazy. Obviously, relay the play call, but that's the easy part. I think just the energy part is where I need to step up. Versatility is a big thing that everybody talks about within the defense, but more importantly with you. What do you think is your best attribute that maybe people don't give you a lot of credit for? >> Uh, I'm going be real. I think I can do a little bit of everything. I I feel like I can pass rush if I really need to. I feel like that was the thing I need to work on the most. So, I did I spent a lot of time on that in the offseason, but I can fill gaps in the run and I can cover. So, I feel like just being able to do that does definitely helps this defense out a lot. >> Give us a little insight into what it's like going against Tua and Mike. obviously went with Mike last year, but having a chance to battle those guys in practice. What do you see out of those two guys that gives you a lot of confidence? >> Uh, obviously I love competition cuz it it brings the best out of everybody. So, both of those guys are coming out to play. Um, obviously they got two different play styles just a little bit and they're both playing so that makes it a little easier. But two different play styles. Quest, you know, knows where he wants to go with the ball. Mike a little savvy with it. So, you know, uh, it's great work for the defense and I just appreciate both of them. Savvy, you said? >> Yeah. Yeah. >> How so? >> Uh, you know, he'll look you off, >> but still throw it right right in front of your face. Yeah, it's gazing. >> Pads on today. How'd it feel? >> Uh, like riding a bike. No, it was good. Um, personally, um, and it's always good to get them on just to get used to them again. Um, haven't worn them obviously since the last game of the season, whatever that was, January. So, um, it was good. Um, I think they've got a good plan for us for the rest of camp. So, just kind of follow the plan. high energy out here today, do you think? >> I think so. And again, it's it's tough sometimes because we're kind of on our own separate field doing our thing. So, we're kind of in and out, but on the special team side, I can say it was good energy. We got through the things we need to get through and um I think we did them at a pretty high level for day one in pad. So, um we just got to keep stacking days together and uh trying to, you know, do as best we can to try to put as many wins as we can on the board later in the season. Do you kind of have your ramp up regimen for the season like nailed down by like this point or do you still try to look for ways to change things up year in and year out? >> I've got an idea, but um and I I keep pretty tedious notes upon what I've done in the past. So um I have an idea, but it changes on how you feel like as you get older sometimes can be hard to get out of bed and stuff. So I got to kind of like eb and flow with it. um trying to get a new routine here. Learn in the training room, learn the weight room. Obviously, I know Craig and Chase a little bit, but the staff as well. So, I'm always trying to plan for week one, not preseason game one because we we want to kind of ramp up to that and we still have a good amount of time till that. But, um I feel like I'm in a pretty good spot right now for being August 3rd, you know. So, um but yeah, I have a plan and it it will change. Um, I think the big things are you have for the most part younger head coaches and points are a premium. So, anytime they get a chance to score points, uh, they they try to do it. Um, they're also a lot of them are young offensive head coaches. So, they're like, "All right, if we miss the field goal, we give up a field goal, we go score a touchdown." You know, that's kind of how they're thinking. Um, and then, you know, kickers are just getting bigger, stronger, faster, just like every other position. Um, the way I kind of equate it is a kid wants to go out um, in high school and he was running a 46, but he's got these other guys running four fours already. Coach, like the only way to get on the field is to kick and so they just get bigger, stronger, faster right behind everyone else. And I think it's showing now with that. And then the last little bit would probably be the football. Um, we've got some better rules than when I first started it was almost, you know, right out of the bag here. Kick that thing. So, uh, that line, you know, of demarcation for when I was kind of coming out for the first bunch of in my career was probably the 35, 53 yard field goal. Um, and now it's kind of it's backed up quite a bit depending on a where you're at, b who the kicker is. But, um, you just see a lot more of it and I think it's exciting. Um, and I've got a lot of other rules I'd like to tell people about, but I'll leave that for another day. >> How does Kevin view it? So, is he more on the I kind of want to kick it more? Is he more >> How much do you evaluate that when you're kind of trying to choose where you want to play? >> Uh, it's a great question. I don't know that answer yet. I haven't talked to him about it. Um, but what I try to do in my kind of pregame routine is I'll find a line where I feel pretty comfortable. Like I call it flow of the game line and then um I'll find like an end of half, end of game where you know the consequences aren't as much. Like obviously you miss a 60, they get the ball at the 50 yard line, right? So they need literally a first down and they're in field goal range. So I have kind of two of those lines and um that's what preseason's for, you know, we kind of get an understanding as a as a group, as a whole team of how we're going to play it, how he wants to do it. If he wants to be aggressive, um that's his call. So it'll it'll just be good communication and I think that's kind of how we'll probably play it. That's I think the best way to do it. >> Get the NFL, you're around long enough, you're going to have familiar ties on different teams that you go to. How much did that help your decision in coming here to Atlanta that there was going to be some familiar faces for you? >> No, it's it's a big decision, you know, with having Craig and Chase and then Jake, you know, it it helps me because I know this the system. I know what their expectations are. Obviously, having a very familiar holder helps a lot. A lot of trust in that. And then building that rhythm with Liam as well right now is is great. So, um it's good to be around those guys and um have them kind of go to bat for you too uh to help to help me come here. So, um it it was a big part of it and then I mean I'm close to home. Um there's a lot of it, a lot of factors, but it was um it was I think the right decision at the right time for me. >> What are some of your first impressions of the rest of the coaching staff, the guys you didn't know? >> They've been great so far. Um I've enjoyed my time here. Um I know it's been short, but I've enjoyed it. They've all kind of embraced me. I've tried to help give as much knowledge as I can to everyone. and I've played a long time. So, if anyone has any questions, I'll I'll give my input best I can. Um, but I've had great conversations, had great conversations with Matt, too, um, about, you know, kind of everything. So, um, it just it's kind of fun to be the older guy. Kind of can see things from a different perspective, a different lens, and I can just hopefully give my advice to whoever wants my advice. >> Okay. You said it's great to be the older guy. >> How often do you feel like the older guy out here? >> Every day. Every day. No, I mean I I feel pretty good. I feel like I'm in a good spot um kicking wise, physically. Um I just got to take care of myself and you know, I can't do things that I could do, you know, 15 years ago. So, I have to understand that, know that. Um keep working to make sure I can do what I need to do on on Sundays. Um but yeah, for the most part, I feel I feel really good. Um but you know, some guys look in I walk in locker room like, man, I keep thinking you're a coach, but no, I'm your teammate. Nick, uh, this might be a little bit of a weird question, but is there like a fraternity of kickers in in the league? Because some of you guys play for so so long in your careers and with like tight end university and quarterbacks and is do kickers kind of >> Yeah, there some kickers uh do. There's uh a couple guys in the offseason who put together some kind of week-long things kind of like that similar to the tight end you and their defensive end stuff. Um, and it really just depends on I think who you've worked with in the past as far as coaching goes. Um, so there there is but um and and a lot of guys know each other. We all respect each other and if anyone has guys reach out uh when they have questions or or concerns or they're going different places, they want to know what it was like. They reach out and and um >> yeah, it's a good it's a good group to to kind of be around. >> Thanks. >> Oh, go ahead. I'll get you next time. >> You sure? You go. Go ahead. One more. say just difference between kicking indoors and outdoors. Looking at your past, your middle home game's been primarily outside. You've been to an indoor. >> Um there's just a less elements to deal with. So you can just worry about yourself, which is kind of nice. Um I've played in Mercedes-Benz one time back in uh 21, I think it was. So um anxious to get down there and and get see what it's like, see what the feels like. I know after the World Cup that putting new turf down, so kind of understanding that. But yeah, it'll be it'll be good to be inside and kind of this sounds funny, but when you're in New England and New York for so long, not worry about the weather, what's going to be on Sunday afternoon. So, um, but I I do enjoy the weather. I I've liked it. I've taken that as a challenge in my career to kind of try to do my best and and do really well in the elements. Um, and I'll take that same attitude when we go inside.

Oh, rookie runs. >> Rookie runs. Run out, get me something. Do this for me. What are the rookie runs you're giving Avian? >> It's hard. Um, really the snacks in the room. They brought in some some BS, but we need >> What they bring in? >> Like one box of chips. The snacks are supposed to go from here to that table. >> I bought the snacks from here to here. >> Yeah, here to here. We need the whole >> Oh, y'all are >> Right, cuz the DB room is the defensive room. >> That's a lot of guys in that room, though. >> Exactly. So, there you got to you got to get the snacks right. But, that's it. I ain't you know, I ain't put too much on his plate. >> All right, here's one for you, Avian. The sky was all mine and I was the same. I am the fastest animal on the planet. To naked eyes, a blur. Swipes of red, white, silver, and black would occur without alert. Prey would have no time to pray. In this dream, my body was a falcon, but my mind was still mine. I could recognize my city and nest from miles away in detail without trying. All dreams feel real, of course, but this one was different still. A bouncing word I heard upon waking even now gives me chills. Atlanta, Atlanta, Atlanta until no sound. I could still see everything as it is and was, but now I'm flying on the ground. A new red rush. >> So good. Such a good I mean, I could watch it a thousand times. I have to give a shout out to my man Virginia Ross. She's the one that cut that video. I mean, she can make any video insane. She's got a real talent there. So, shout out to Jenny. We love that video. If you haven't gotten your uniform or your new jersey yet, please go ahead and get it before week two. >> Dare I say, if you have a red jersey and you wear it to the game, you will not be an outcast. Can I do that? >> Oh, wow. Okay. >> okay. Just had to throw it out there. Just had >> Arch has jokes. >> Let's go. >> I love it. I I the dad jokes. I love the puns. We are now joined by Will McFadden. He was able to watch a little bit of practice today. So, he's been our eyes and he's going to be our ears as well um throughout the duration of training camp. So, Will, thank you for joining us back again on this Monday morning. Can I talk to us about what you're what you've been seeing today at practice that we weren't maybe able to show everyone? >> Yeah, I mean, well, the biggest news right off the bat, Tua Tagovailoa has returned to 11-on-11s. He missed the first, you know, was limited in the first four days of practice some capacity, varying capacities, with back tightness, made it back out there. So, that is far and away the biggest kind of news, I think, on a Monday here. We came in expecting the pads to be on. I think we saw some examples of guys who looked, you know, really ready for those pads to come on, brought the level of intensity needed with these pads. And then I think we saw some guys who are are still kind of ramping up to that level of intensity. But again, far and away, Tua Tagovailoa returning to 11-on-11s, that's kind of the biggest story so far in practice. >> Yeah, how was he? Kind of talk to us about how he was doing. How did he look in 11-on-11? What what were you seeing from Tua today? >> Yeah, I don't think they asked him to do too too much. Um there was a moment where he kind of faced some pressure and had an opportunity to scramble. He kind of wisely, I think, killed the play a little bit um and and didn't take that full run. Uh but I thought he looked really sharp throwing the football. Obviously, when it comes to your back, you don't you don't want to work in too too quickly because it can be finicky sometimes, but seemed like they had him throwing some screen passes, some quick outs. He's been doing individual stuff, so it's not like he hasn't been throwing during training camp. Uh he looked he looked pretty crisp out there, all things considered. >> Love love to hear that about Tua. >> part that's tough for the offense now is you've been playing kind of patty cake, if you will, because they haven't been able to come after you, you know? Now all of a sudden the physicality comes in. And so, the offense is is typically behind the defense when you start training camp with with the pads. And so, that subsequently screws the quarterback up a little bit because Tua is trying to slide up in in where there isn't any place to slide because they've got stunts going on. It'll settle down for the offensive line. The speed of the game, they'll pick back up on the speed of the game because it's two steps and stop when you're in in walk-through type things or with no pads on. Now, you know, other than tackling the quarterback, they're coming. >> And so I've got to be able to as as Bill Callahan said, I've got to be able to finish. And so some of this is going to be getting that ramped up and they'll be fine. But uh the quarterback struggles a little bit in that situation because there's too much interior pressure. Hey, can we block somebody? What's going on up there? You start getting a little frustrated with >> Yeah, the interior pressure can be tough, but that's why the one-on-ones are so fun and I think we have a couple of replays of guys that kind of shined today during one-on-ones. I think we got a Zachariah Branch replay that we could look at against D'Onta Holmes. He was able to get a one-handed catch. If we can get that replay, I don't know if it's ready or not. We'll wait. There it is. There's Zachariah Branch one-handed grab from D'Onta Holmes or against D'Onta Holmes, excuse me. Just a rookie going out there making a name for himself. And here's Jahan Dotson going against Mike Hughes that we saw earlier. Really fun times for these guys. >> Yeah, and and just the we talked a little bit about it when we were watching it live is is the idea of running my route and creating an opportunity from a separation standpoint to give my quarterback someplace to throw the ball. Great job at the top of the route there by Jahan Dotson. Press coverage, Mike Hughes right in his hip pocket. Okay, now little pressure break, just kind of lean into it a little bit and I can't stick my hand out and shove him away, but I can use that elbow to create the separation. I see that as a quarterback and I'm letting the ball go cuz I'm trusting my the guy to get to his spot and and that's exactly what Jahan Dotson did. That's building chemistry between quarterback and receiver. That's why those those moments are so important. >> something with the Zachariah catch, too, is I I want to make it very clear, that's a hard job to go against Zachariah Branch. He is fast, he shifty. You talk about Bijan Robinson and the shiftiness that he and the elusiveness of a running how elusive a of a running back he is. Zachariah Branch is elusive as well. He can stick his foot in and he can go the other direction in 0.2 seconds. It doesn't matter. So, that's a hard job for D'Onta Foreman who's vying for that cornerback two potentially nickel one spot. >> Will, you've you've watched him since he got here. He's been impressive since opening day when he got here. But, what is it that he's he's taken it to another level, hasn't he? >> Well, what's crazy about Zachariah Branch is he has like the things that you cannot teach. But, then he works as hard as anybody to maximize those skills. You mentioned, you know, seventh, eighth grade. He's he's homeschooled so that he's able to work out all the time with his father and his Hall of Fame uncle who has this pedigree. And he's just the hardest working rookie that I think I've ever been around. He comes from the Georgia program. He has been around kind of winning culture, I think, his his entire life. And he's bringing that and he looks the part out there on the field as a rookie right away. >> early on, Will. Where do you see them lining him up? It doesn't seem like they're choking the motor on him. What what are they doing with him? >> That's a great question because I I think when you look at the skill set he brings, there is some of that overlap with Ade Ogundeji and with Jahan Dotson. But, I view Zachariah Branch as I think gadget player feels like it's underselling him. He can be the ultimate gadget player because we saw on one play he goes deep against A.J. Terrell and kind of gets behind him and catches a beautiful deep ball. And then the very next play you can throw a screen pass to him and he can take it 60 yards. So, like you have a variety of ways to use him. And so, to me it's almost get everybody else set and then Zachariah is kind of that fun little joker piece that you can move around and fit him how you need to. >> I think Will's been using the term weapon. I think that's a pretty good way to put it. >> I agree with you. Someone else you mentioned, Elisha W. George, another bulldog that I think is having a great camp so far is out of Jaylen Walker. Obviously, first round pick for the Falcons a couple years ago. And man, what a guy he has become. We talk about him a lot about what were you going to do with Jaylen Walker when he came here as a rookie? Were you going to have him as an off-the-ball linebacker or a linebacker that was on the ball? You saw Jeff Ulbrich kind of specialized him on the ball, more of an edge rusher type of linebacker. What have you seen from Jaylen Walker in terms of the physicality that you've seen today when you got when you get pads on? >> He is a very physical player. He is fast, he is athletic, and that adds to it a lot of pop in his pads when he's able to get up full speed around the arch. So, I think starting him in year one as an edge defender made a lot of sense. Obviously, we saw in college at Georgia he moved around. He kind of reminded me of almost like Michael Myers. He was just like this this imposing force who just like walked into the quarterback. You just couldn't stop him. I haven't seen that out here yet in training camp in terms of him moving around in the way that we did at Georgia. I think that that is potentially on the table in year two for him. He is still working off that left edge. I think that makes a lot of sense. He looked good in one-on-ones. He's bringing the hands, he's bringing the physicality. He's worked a lot this off-season on his pass rush moves, on his run defense. He's one of the guys that was here all off-season long in the weight room working with the strength and conditioning staff. So, I think that coupled with the ability to just kind of have your first full off-season. Arch, you know what that's like going from college to the draft process to your first rookie mini camp to training camp. Like, it is a non-stop 2-year process, and I think Jaylen Walker is really going to benefit from some time away and some extra focus. >> Well, you see just the athleticism, just the raw athleticism, the scariness that Will just talked about. There's no question about it. How would you like to be looking at that dude? He says he's breathing fire coming off the edge. But, the I don't know what's more impressive, Will, about him. His his leadership piece, his work ethic, or just the pure raw athleticism with the brute force he brings to the table. Which one do you pick out? I mean, you love you have the package. >> To me, it's the work ethic. To me, it's the work ethic because everything else jumps out and there that is no way to diminish all of the other qualities, but to me, I like I I sense some Grady Jarrett to him in the way that he is both somebody who speaks through his actions, but he's also not afraid to get vocal when he needs to. In fact, John Teerney, the outside linebackers coach, said he's developing a little bit of a Batman voice. So, I I think that's kind of like his leadership, his like, "Hey, everybody gets that I'm serious" voice. Uh and I'm I'm curious to see how that continues to develop throughout his NFL career. But, to me, it's those leadership intangible qualities because that's what we saw at Georgia. It's part of what made that defense so great. And I kind of can't wait until we really feel that uh flow throughout the defense. >> I I agree with you. I think when you you bring up Batman, if you haven't watched his mic'd up from I think when we were in Germany playing the Colts, please go back and watch it. It is must-see TV. His voice goes down like three octaves. You don't even know if you hear him and not you don't see him, you have no idea who's speaking to you. It is It's wild and he calls himself Batman on game day. But, I agree with you. I think the work ethic is something that this this draft or um the scouts were able to see in Jalen Walker and say, "This is a guy that we need on the team." Do we know how we're going to use him quite yet? Maybe not, but they figured it out in his rookie year and it's going to be interesting to see how he evolves in this role and kind of sits into it a little bit more into year two. But, a guy guy we talked about earlier, Arch, is Brandon Dorlus. He wants to get two times better at everything that he was able to do in year two going into year three. So, Will, for you, when you see Brandon Dorlus, he's kind of taking on this leadership position in a way. He's one of the few guys in that defensive line group who has been here for a little bit. What do you What have you been seeing from Brandon Dorlus so far? >> Yeah, well, I mean, last year mentioned his breakout season, eight and a half sacks, second in the league among defensive tackles behind only Jeffery Simmons, who was a first-team All-Pro last year. So, we saw what the potential is for Brandon Dorlus. What I loved about him last year was a lot of his sacks were kind of effort plays where he did not give up on the play, continued to fight through whether it's a double team, whether he's coming around on a stunt, it just takes a little bit of time. He was so good at that. So, I want to see that continue in year three, but I would also like to see him develop ways to win quicker. And that is where when you're watching some of these one-on-one position drills, mention the style and the and the technique that a pass rusher has to have. How does that continue to come to life for Brandon Dorlus? Is he developing his own flair and style and winning moves? Because Grady had an unstoppable swim move. That was his go-to pitch, if you will. I would like to see what Brandon Dorlus develops as a go-to pitch here in year three because we saw the baseline floor in in year two and it was so so good. >> Yeah, I I agree with you, Will. I think it obviously the sky's the limit for him. He could be one of the more dynamic interior pass rushers. I think that what I love about him when Tori talked to him earlier in the show was the fact that he's more concerned, he knows he can rush the passer. He wants to create more negative plays in the run game, which I think they need to do. They were 24th in the league against the run. He's going to be in as much as he can be in. Obviously, they'll sub out and they'll rotate guys, but Brandon Dorlus is a starter at defensive tackle. He needs to be on the field as much as he can and he wants to be impactful when he's there. So, I think that I love the way he's trying to take his mindset to a different place. He's learning what he can and can't get away with, but he's also learning the things that he can force himself into on an offensive lineman. Talk about the the physicality piece of it. Some of it's imposing your will on those guys and that's what he's trying to do this year. >> And that and I mean you talk about the the interview that Tori was able to get with him. He said a quote and I really loved it. I think it says a lot about who he is is embrace your role, but don't don't become complacent. And I think after you have a year of of your second year like that that eight sacks, I mean he kind of blew up. He If you didn't know his name, you kind of do now if you're a Falcons fan. And now he's saying, "I'm trying to get better. I'm embracing who I am. I'm embracing that I might have this more veteran role of guys looking to me that are new on this team of what should I be doing, but I'm not going to sit back in that and just relax cuz I still have things to prove." I think that's a great way to be. I think most of these guys on this most of the guys on this defense are that way as well. I mean, we've talked about a lot of the guys, but I think Jessie Bates is someone a Pro Bowler who every year he's not getting complacent. He wants to be better. How can I make myself better every single year? Because you know, with guys in the league, they all say it's stands for not for long. You have this this peak point in your career, and then as you get older, you might um start to tick down a little bit. Jessie, no ticking down anytime soon for him. He every single year he comes in and says, "I'm not going to get complacent. I'm going to work harder than I did last year, and I'm going to be better than I was last year as well." >> Yeah, and with that kind of attitude, you become the top-rated safety in Madden NFL 27. Jessie Bates, uh no, his his playmaking ability is so important to this defense. He's always in the right spot at the right time. He communicates so well. He's able to pick up on the little things that make the the great players, the elite players. I think Jessie Bates, the versatility piece that he brings is really I think going to come to life in this defense. Especially this year. We've kind of talked about Sidney Brown as a safety who's playing in the nickel. I'm so fascinated by having maybe three safeties on the field at the same time, and I think Jessie Bates's uh like intelligence, his just communication skills, leadership skills is going to be huge in making that three-headed monster work. >> All right. Well, well, thank you so much for joining us today. You gave us some really valuable information to kind of continue going through training camp. Got a couple more open practices, as you can see a lot of fans behind us on that hill. Lots of open practices left for you guys to come and see maybe before school starts. Bring your kids out. Get some signatures from players, and obviously we have that 88 that's all in silver at 7:00 p.m. it's Saturday night lights. We're going to have another live show for you guys, but come out to Lanier High School if you can. Come be part of this team in some way, form or fashion. If you can't come out, make sure to check us out on YouTube at 7:00 p.m. when practice starts for Saturday night lights. For us for now, we're going to let you go back to work. I know it's Monday, so maybe get back to work and you know, close this one out. Don't show your boss that you're not working so hard, but we appreciate you guys for joining us today for our AT&T training camp life and we will see you on Saturday night lights on August the 8th. Bye, guys.

title: Vega Ioane Impresses, Has ‘Welcome to The NFL’ Moment | Baltimore Ravens Final Drive
text: The Ravens were back on the practice field today and it was the first padded practice of this year's training camp. We were all excited to see the pads come on, the intensity ramp up, and one guy who a lot of people were focused on today was the rookie, the first round pick right guard Venga Yoawane. He's somebody who we wanted to see in these physical padded practices since the Ravens drafted him back in the spring. And he's looked good all throughout this process and he continued to impress here today. Now, one point of practice he did have his welcome to the NFL moment as a rookie. There was a play where he was run blocking for Derrick Henry behind him. Venga cleared the path and made a hole for Henry, but the two kind of collided at that point. They both went to the ground and Venga had a laugh about it after practice today. >> Welcome to the league, huh? I mean, as as Derrick Henry right there. Um, you know, he's a he's a big running back, strong guy, phenomenal player, of course. You know, I'm chasing after the linebacker. I'm thinking I'm going to get him. You know, he we both end up on the ground, you know, but you know, great player. Now I know to stay out of his way, so. >> Now look, as I mentioned, he is somebody who's looked good all throughout the spring and summer and the Ravens are really impressed with what they're seeing from their first round pick. >> He's done a really good job as far as like understanding what we're asking of him, especially in that position. And um, you know, he's got some some really good feet that allows him to do a lot of things up front that being his size is pretty special. And so I just think that you know, he keeps trying to go out and he's got a mindset where he's trying to get better every day. And to me, like he the sky's the limit for that. >> You know, as a rookie, you know, there's a lot of expectations, things like that, but my whole mindset coming in was to, you know, earn my keep, earn the trust of the guys in the room. But, you know, we come in here, we talk a lot about it in the team meeting room, prove them right. You know, I'm that's my whole goal out here. You know, I got to earn my keep, you know, earn my spot out there. But, while I'm doing that, I'm trying to prove the staff right, prove the team right for picking me in the first round. >> So, expectations are always high for a first round pick, and Vanga seems like somebody who is ready to rise to that challenge. That's it for me on File and Drive today, but thanks for watching. We'll see you again tomorrow.

title: Jesse Minter: ‘I Love Where Nnamdi Madubuike Is At’| Baltimore Ravens
text: Training pads always a fun day in uh training camp. Um they get much better than that. We were finally out here, you know, playing a real football. Uh we made the first day in pads more of a tag off day with the uh as far as finishing on the ball carrier. All the all the blocking and block destruction was able to be at a at a much higher rate than what than it was without pads. Tomorrow we'll incorporate a little bit more thud on the ball carriers. Um and so like where we're at. Good first day, energy coming off a day off and uh take questions. >> Jesse, do you feel like today was kind of one of those offensive days that's just within the ebbs and flows of the new system? >> Uh I'm not sure what you mean by the question. I think uh I you know, it's the fifth practice. Um you're you're installing on both sides and there's always going to be back and forth in training camp. Uh they'll look at the tape. There'll probably be some good plays on both sides, some good runs that hit where who knows if we would have made the tackle or not. Uh some good things in the passing game, some good things from the defense. So all in all, I thought it was just good back and forth uh overall. >> Jesse, I know he's been around, but to see Calais Campbell get on the field from what he's been through personally, but also just a leadership standpoint to have him out there with everyone, how meaningful is that? >> Yeah, I mean talked about him a little bit. I mean, he's a he's like a force multiplier. Uh just how he operates, the wisdom that he brings, the leadership that he brings, on top of he's still a really high caliber player for his position. Uh so we're we're excited to work him in, start to ramp him in to to getting ready. Um you know, that'll be at a that'll be at a uh pace that's good for him and uh just again, excited to have him here. The guys love him. He brings such a great value to that defensive line room. Um and just just love having Calais out there. >> Jesse, you were saying consistently you wanted what you expected when you were talking to the rookie mini camp and all that. How have you seen him progress in the you know, the uh start of training camp? >> I think you know, like it you're still a rookie, but when you when you go through the whole off-season um and then you get that break, this year was for everybody in the NFL was a little bit longer break than maybe a normal year because of the calendar. Um man, he feels like he's been doing it for a while now and and it shows up in how he operates, shows up in his retention of everything. it'll be really fun to watch him in that practice with pads on when we get upstairs. So, excited about where he's at. Just keep Just keep being himself. He's He's a really highly talented player, highly motivated, works really hard, has a great coach, has great teammates. Um expect big things out of him. >> Jesse, I know we're about 6 weeks from the season opener. Is there a kind of deadline by which you would like to have your uh starting five on the offensive line decided by? >> I don't know that there's a deadline. Um and and I I really say that only because one of them in the in the mix of the battle is is is coming off of an injury. And so, like that timeline may or may not be perfect for that first game. So, I still think that that's that's an ongoing chase all the way uh to being at our best, you know, uh throughout the year. Um but there there'll come a point in time where we'll certainly focus on getting ready for that first game and you know, I think a couple weeks out that'll probably shake itself out. >> Jesse, uh we last week we heard Lamar talk about you pulled him aside and said, "Hey, I want to have a sit down for meetings where you can look at the offense through the lens of your defense." Said he really liked the idea. Can you just take us through that thought process, decision, and how that able to >> I I mean, I just look at ways to impact our offense and and uh impact our players and it's no different than maybe giving Zay some tips going against certain types of press corners. Um but I do think I do think, you know, being able to look at uh how we play defense, it's it's a trendy league, I would say. Um and so, there's a lot of copycat of of things that are done well. So, whether it's our defense or helping him look at other people's defenses, Uh I just think from my perspective and and studying all that over the last few years, maybe able to give him a little bit of insight into how they're trying to make certain things look the same, but maybe what uh maybe what could help him. So, again, all all in uh just trying to help Amari be the best version of himself. >> What was his reaction? How do you feel like he kind of embraced that idea? >> Yeah, I think it was it was cool. It was exciting. We already talk a lot on the field even just about uh back and forth of plays and coverages. Uh and so, as we really get into like specific opponents, I think uh I think that'll be a good a good thing we can do each week just to try to uh maybe give him a little different perspective. >> Just seeing Amari just seeing you guys work together on his magic, how are you guys feeling? What's it been like building a relationship with him especially kind of given the uniqueness of you guys both being >> Yeah, we were just kind of able to connect um back back when uh you know, as spring training was getting kicked off, exchanged a few text messages. Obviously, met him in person at opening day. I've had a had a some good interactions with him. Uh certainly always, man, just like pull for the teams, you know, pull for the the teams in the city uh for our fans, you know, we we all want the same thing. Uh and so, it's been fun to get to know him and his family. Great to have them uh out of practice. >> Seeing Amari with the defensive line today for the first time, just kind of do you like where he's at and how he's progressing? Do you have any I guess expectations for when maybe or what that next step is for >> I think um it I think you'll see just over a little bit of time like a steady progression for him. Now, what exactly that timeline is, that'll that'll shake out each day. We'll recap and make sure we're not going, you know, too whatever. but I love where he's at. I love where his head's at. He's excited. The room's excited. It's fun when he's out there. Um and so, I think I think that's headed headed in a great direction for us. >> What that role looks like? >> You know, what it like again, it's like whatever play like whatever the players make them feel the best and and play with the most confidence. Um that definitely looks like a little bit of a throwback. >> Yes, seeing you guys released excuse me, released Eugene on the prior roster. Did that come as a surprise to you? And do you feel like you need another veteran tackle to kind of come in and take his roster spot? >> I would say just a a personal situation with him where that where that ended up coming from. We're not going to speak to that just just for for his benefit, but we'll we'll certainly do some things quickly to replace that position on the roster and certainly wish him the best. Good. Thank you.

title: Vega Ioane: ‘My Whole Mindset Coming In Was to Earn My Keep’ | Baltimore Ravens
text: It's not a preseason game, not a regular season game, but first day in pads. Uh, how would you kind of describe that for you? >> First day in pads. It's been a long time, you know, since I put the pads on, but felt good to be out there. You know, it feels different when you love the game. So, I just felt good to be back out there, especially with the guys in the room. So, >> how would you describe this O line and how it looks like right now and how you've been able to bond with the crew out here? We have a bunch of great guys in the room. We have Ronnie, you know, the oldest guy in our room. He's a great leader for us. Got John Simpson, you know, they're on the left side. You know, me and Raj, I mean, sure you guys have heard it, but I feel like I've been playing with him for a long time and he's a phenomenal young player. Feels like he's been in the league for 10 years. You know, when we go out there, it feels like just like I say, we play for a long time with each other. But, you know, going out there just feels natural to play with those, you know, four guys. you know, being a young guy coming in, just feels good for me to, you know, be out there with them. >> A few guys have said that, you know, looks like you've been out there for a few years already, impressed by your coming across like a veteran. What does that sort of mean to you? And then secondly, like how would you describe your comfort level? Mhm. That means a lot to me because uh coming in, you know, as a rookie, you know, there's a lot of expectations, things like that, but my whole mindset coming in was to, you know, earn my keep, earn the trust of the guys in the room, the entire offense, and hearing that makes me feel like I'm doing a good job of that. You know, it's [snorts] never never to be satisfied about, but you know, there's a lot of things to keep building on. >> How would you describe the culture that Dwayne Leford has built specifically within that old line? >> It's a great culture. You know, he's a great coach. Um he's brought in the mindset of being, you know, sure you guys have heard about speed off the ball. You know, that that comes with everything else. You know, he's a big technical guy, but in the room, you know, he's a, you know, chill, relaxed guy. You know, we talk about film. You know, next thing you know, we're talking about lifestyle, things like that. But, you know, it's a good balance in between, but the culture is that, you know, we fight for each other in the room and then we all do that, we bring it for the entire offense. >> Today, it look like you and Derek kind of bounce off each other, see who's coming through the holes. Take me through that and how's it feeling? Yeah. Uh, welcome to the league, huh? I mean, that's that's Derrick Henry right there. Um, you know, he's a he's a big running back, strong guy, phenomenal player. Of course, you know, I'm chasing after the linebacker. I'm thinking I'm going to get him and, you know, he we both end up on the ground, you know, but, you know, great player now. I know stay out of his way.
