text: What do you aim to accomplish with the first day of pads? >> Um first day of gap schemes. So, we'll definitely uh get a chance to see uh movement at the line of scrimmage. Obviously, defensively, we're going to wrap and release. So, tackling-wise, uh there's no really touching off per se. Obviously, O-line-wise is the biggest thing. O-line, D-line, in the trenches. Uh where we're at from a physicality standpoint. >> Todd, the other day we saw our first kind of fight at camp. I don't know if it was a real fight or not. Do you Do you have a policy on that? Do you have a message to the team when that stuff happens? >> Well, I don't think I've ever been through a camp where there hasn't been a scuffle. Uh you know, we got prideful guys, you know, guys that uh love to compete, love to practice. And uh you know, that's going to happen. I mean, that's you know, it's a physical sport. You're going to have those uh pop up every now and then. >> Todd, you mentioned the the O-line and the D-line. How does the evaluation change for those two groups in particular when the pads come on and what you kind of look at? >> Well, without the pads, you're talking about footwork, communication, are you in the right spot? And certainly, you know, hand placement. But then when you put the pads on, now it's finish. You know, now it's uh our ability to defensively, you know, shed and get off blocks, point of contact, uh physicality. So, we're looking forward to that. And our tight ends, you know, that's a big part of it, and our fullbacks. Um I actually all all 11. >> Coach Todd, we talked uh Quincy Williams earlier today. What have you learned most about him since you guys have been together? >> Well, he's so much fun to be around. Let's start with that. Never had a bad day. Maybe not around me, he hasn't. Uh loves football, loves his teammates. That That's what I see every day. I mean, he's he's a special individual. People are wired that way that when you talk about energy, attitude, and body language, I mean, you look that up. I don't even know if that's that's probably not in the dictionary. But if you looked up Quincy Williams, picture's right next to that, cuz that's who he is. >> What Todd, you talked about, you know, first eight days are in install. How much does the the format of practice change once you get past Thursdays, you know, that the eighth day? Do you Do you sort of alter, you know, kind of the cuz it seems like there's been a fairly standard routine for practice. How much does that change once you get out of the >> It'll be similar. Uh what'll change is when we're drilling down to what we're really going to run, what we plan on focusing on. Certainly, you're going to dive into more situational football cuz you're done with your main installs. Uh that'll come into play, but ultimately, we'll continue to build off of our installs and uh the things we're going to do as we move forward. >> Todd, you you were with Mike Evans. I don't know, was it his rookie year >> I was with Mike Evans in Tampa. >> Yeah. >> I was with Mike if I have it right, I was with him in his third, fourth, and fifth year. I think he'd been there a year, then they drafted Jameis, and then I think I got him three, four, five, I think. >> Okay, so Boston compared to him, is it fair early in his in his career, do you see >> We're We're back on that uh Carson and Kuechly thing here. We're We're comparing a little early to compare to uh to Mike Evans, who is an absolute stud. not only from his size, catch radius, ability to bend, get in and out of breaks. Um has a unbelievable competitive spirit to want to win. When I was with him, he never complained about balls coming his way. He knew they would come his way. I loved coaching Mike Evans. I mean, he is a absolute uh stud and fun to be around. and Denzel has some of those attributes in terms of catch radius. I haven't seen it yet, the edge that Mike plays with, but he's still a rookie, so I wasn't there his first 2 years. But I think the catch radius and the ability to throw it up to him, uh you do see certain aspects of Mike's game in him. >> I know we've talked to you already a little bit about Dillon Gabriel. But each day he keeps going out there and making consistent plays. Um is it maybe in some ways a little unfortunate that he wasn't able to show more or do more, you know, with the first or second team just based on the situation that you guys are in? >> Yeah, I I mean, it's uh at some point when you start in the spring or some point in the spring and in the fall, you have to set some form of a depth chart in terms of reps. That's just the way it goes. And I said it the other day, the player everybody's competing, but you're not guaranteed the same amount of reps. So it's up to the player to take advantage and maximize those reps, which I feel like Dillon has done. So, we see as we move forward if that continues, we'll continue to up his reps. I mean, he's earned that. That's what That's what every player should expect, right? If they play well, you have to up their reps, or what's the purpose of playing well? >> Bobby, on the this couple of offensive guys, defense felt like they've been pretty chippy at each other, pushing each other really hard. Do you appreciate that level of intensity between the two groups as cliche as I am dressed for the siren, but are you seeing that out there? >> Sure. I think it's a lot of fun to be around. As long as it stays within it's us against the world. It's us against an opponent, not us against us, from offense to defense. And I have not seen that. I've seen the fun side of that. I don't think the scuffle had to do so much with the you know, with the back and forth. Uh what I do see is our coaches and players having fun in a very, very tough sport uh that you have to stack days and you know, it only gets tougher from here when you put the pads on every day. >> How Ben Niemann talked to us about maybe having a chip on his shoulder and just after the draft and and wanting to prove people wrong. I guess for you as a coach, that sort of drive, how have you seen that so far in him? >> Well, at some point I mean, I don't know how long that goes. I I don't know. I think uh at some point practice, you're not thinking about, boy, I got drafted where I got drafted. I mean, at some point it doesn't matter. I mean, at that point, I mean, what pick was he? >> 39. >> Holy cow, you're the 39th best player in the draft. I mean, that's pretty damn good. I mean, I don't know what to tell you, but I don't see it as that. I see it as there's a lot of really good football players out there and you go with the 39th pick. I mean, that's pretty special. So, if he feels that internally, I'm I'm fine with that. If that's what fuels him, but at this point, it's about being the best player you can be, fighting like hell to get to your second contract when it really matters at that point. >> How important is Mason? >> One of the things I've noticed uh he told us that uh between the walk-through and the that they're two or three hour sessions a day. My question to you is >> What did he say? He said what now? >> He said what? >> He said three hour blocks of meetings in the morning and at night. >> All right. Uh we meet at 8:00 and walk through is at 11:00. So, but there's breaks in there. He's taking it to a an extreme. All right, he's taking that to a whole 'nother level there. I mean, there are some breaks in there and then after practice, we only get them for 11 hours, right? I mean, we do get the full time. So, if they lift at 7:00, they have to be gone by 6:00. If they start at 8:00, they can be gone by 7:00. So, somewhere in there is lift, if we lift that day, meetings, walk, lunch, prep for practice, practice, meet. So, I I I don't really know exactly where all that falls, uh but that is normal camp calendar. >> So, my question is do you have to guard against information overload with all with all the that meeting time? >> That's what the meeting time is for. It's not really to overload them, it's to help them. Does that make sense? Now, do I find it difficult? Do I think our young all of us to sit there the whole time? We give them breaks. They can bring in snacks, help them to take notes. We have video, try to change our voice a little bit, try to keep them excited about it. That's up to them to be a pro. If they start falling asleep, stand up. Got to get the information. It is different than than college. I mean, there's a lot of information there and we accept expect them to be pros. >> Talking with Mason, um what did you see from him last year early in camp, and then just how important is he to what you're trying to do defensively? >> Well, I mean, talk about ball get-off. You know, what what I didn't know is uh I always saw him as maybe an undersized inside guy with great ball get-off that's disruptive. What he is is that, but I think he's not going Luke Kuechly here, but in terms of the D-line, in terms of calls and anticipation, right, of what he's going to see, communication, quarterback, verbal, O-line, you know, in terms of their calls. I see it every day. He is not only that, but he is more cuz he really understands football and um he anticipates what offenses are trying to do to them, and that I didn't know. Jesse Minter told me that at the head of Michigan told me that at the owners' meetings. He said, "No, no, he's much more than just a guy that gets off the ball. He's fun to watch." You know, it's it's hard as an offensive head coach every now and then you you can be a little bit of whiny, you know, when when they're disruptive, but it's awesome for us. >> Todd, you probably saw um a play in which um not yesterday, but the day before, uh where Quinshon kind of lit up Michael Hall a little bit. Um and I'm just wondering, you know, is that football? I know it's football practice, but is that the kind of thing that I mean are are are you cool with that if you know that >> Well, no. I mean, in the heat of the moment, what happened on the prac- practice field, and I've met with Quinshon about it, there is a certain amount of regret right at the moment when it happens, but we are all human, and we do make mistakes, and that's what I always tell our team. I said, "You got to fight to not get hijacked emotionally in a highly emotional game, or all of us, uh whether it's in our work or emotional or our personal lives, try not to get hijacked emotionally, but to me, where you go from here is we are human. I said this the other the we're going to fall short. Are you going to own it? And then are we going to fix it? And and that's just a speed bump. That's all it is. Uh it was a mistake. >> Is Carson there back today? >> What's that? >> Carson's watching. >> He will not be back today. He's dealing with a little minor uh injury, so he will not be back today. >> Any update on Boyer? >> I do not know. >> Okay. >> Todd Todd >> Last one. going back to just the >> A lot of pressure on the last one. Seem like there was a little stagger right there. Just a guy got one. Um this is kind of a maybe a big picture look for you. Um you could probably take it a lot of different directions, but just off the top of your head, maybe the main way you think the coaching profession has changed and the way it's stayed the same throughout your >> Wow, that's the last one that's going to Okay, how the coaching profession has changed and how it has stayed the same. >> And you could even instead of going back to the beginning of your coaching career, you could even start at NFL. That's almost 20 years now. >> Well, first off, the staffs have gotten so much bigger. Hell, we got 28 coaches for God's sakes. I mean, hell, back then back then, I'll just talk college. Back then when I first started like you only had these coaches. You didn't even have the support staff. Hell, you'd be coaching running backs and you'd have travel. Hell, you'd be planning Shoney's breakfast and damn the Holiday Inn Express or where you're staying. You know, you had multi One guy had academics. This guy like hell, you'd see one coach taping and Lining the fields. I mean, that's what my dad did when I was little. That's what you did. You did Now you got so much support staff and you have a big coaching staff that allows you to really focus on certain aspects of the job if that makes sense. Certain guys don't have to draw cards anymore. You have guys to do that. And from a game planning uh standpoint, preparation standpoint, it's the money that now goes into staffing I love cuz it allows you to really drill down into certain things you want to focus on. Um where it's changed the most, I would say is um I would just say it has changed in terms of um first of all what is hard. You know, like everything's always hard. It's just a matter what you compare it to, right? The old three-a-days and two-a-days and one-a-days and then a day off, right? Like of what it used to be, but obviously uh the training these days in terms of where our players' bodies are, but certainly in terms of like training camp has changed in terms of you know, getting them for 11 hours and they're out of here, which I think makes it a lot more manageable, but you know, I like the time with the players, but that is certainly changed in terms of the amount of time you get with the guys also in the off-season. The amount of time you get with the guys and so, but you know, staffs have changed, the sizes have changed um and then the amount of time you get with the players has changed. >> All right, thank you.

title: Quincy Williams Press Conference | August 3rd, 2026
text: So, how would you how would you kind of assess where this defense is these first few days at camp? >> Uh I love it. Uh very energetic. This spring I really couldn't tell you far as like how your team's going to be just because we're just now putting in the playbook. Everyone's new to everyone. Um pieces aren't they aren't there and stuff, but training camp getting to see a full circle, getting to see the speed on the field, getting to see the front line, what we call our engine and stuff moving and stuff moving people. It's amazing. It's a beautiful thing to play behind, too. >> Is there a little extra juice today cuz you know it's pads day? >> Oh, yeah. The pads are my favorite day of the year every single year. The pads day, man. I think I had my pads laid out, made sure I had everything ready. So, I'm excited today. >> It's like Christmas like Christmas day. >> For real. Christmas day. Get to spruce up my helmet a little bit, you know, break in my shoulder pads, might run into a wall a little bit, you know, make sure I'm good. >> What have you learned about Carson Wentz so far? >> He's going to run to the ball. He's like a golden retriever when the ball is thrown. He's going to run to the ball no matter what. Literally going to run to the ball. He don't care where it is down the field. If it's a touchdown, he's still going to run to the ball. So, I like that about him, too, cuz now I'm chasing him to get to the ball. Now we're having competition. It's like, all right. I got to the ball more times than you got to the ball today, which is actually not a lot coming from him. >> Anything surprise you about him that you didn't know heading in? >> Uh no, he's a very smart player. Um helps me out a lot far as like keys and stuff like that, which I like. Um just because most of the time I'll be tired and running around when I come back and he was like, all right, pay attention to this. Um he's also practiced against this offense a lot, too, though. So, the keys is what's going to help him. So, it's really like the game time thing, just making sure he's still on it, making sure uh we're both still running to the ball and things. So, that's the athletic ability, I was surprised by that. Uh just how fast he is and stuff like that. Like when I'm running to the ball, he's literally running right next to me and I was like, okay, bet. We're on the same page then, but it's really just that chemistry that's surprised me that happened so fast. So, that's the biggest thing. >> How would you kind of describe the competition level so far? >> Dog eat dog. Dog versus dog. I'm going to be honest with you. That's how I would That's how I would um That's how I would say this training camp has been, especially because uh competing against this offense, these quarterbacks and things like that. It's like they get some wins, we get some wins, we come back also far as like now the pads are on now. So, we now we're really going to see are are these really sacks right here? All right, did you really complete this ball right here? Do you really think you finna get through this hole when I'm standing right in front of you? So, pads on now, so we really finna get to see today. >> Man, you guys had that little It was not like a full-blown fight, but everybody kind of came together, a little scuffle. >> Yeah, man. I fight with my brother all the time, too, though. That's a great thing, man. That's just that fight just letting everybody know I'm here to compete. Uh that's the biggest thing, man. So, boys going to fight, you feel me? I have There was If you went through a whole training camp and there were no fights, I'd probably worry about your team. You feel me? Just that competitive nature of it. And then like have you seen after the game I mean after after that scuffle we all came together? Made sure we was all on the same page and today we're going to be able to compete again today. >> It seems like the defensive front >> DeAngelo >> like the aggressiveness even though you guys weren't in pads having a convention pretty much every play in the backfield. Just the mentality uh you know, touch on just like the mentality of just having that even though it's early in camp you guys are really getting after it. >> So, we call him DeAngelo and we go as they go. So, the biggest thing is they can get down the field, >> [clears throat] >> correction covers working together and stuff. So, that's the biggest thing and then um just that aggression and things make the holes bigger and stuff for me. So, it's just running down here just making sure I know for a fact these guys are going their best and then I'm going my best and now the DBs don't have to cover that much. So, that's a my favorite part of this defense is the engine which I call the D-line. >> You mentioned that with the pads coming on. How annoyed do >> Now we going to really see those sacks. That's the thing though. >> Yeah, that's what I'm saying. How annoyed do you get when you're out there and like it's look that was a sack or that was and then it turns into a big >> I don't really get annoyed at all, man, just because we play against quarterbacks like uh those like second play quarterbacks who get out of the pocket a lot and stuff like that. So, I still need my back end to be like, all right, what if this isn't a sack and he gets out of the pocket and stuff like that. So, it's very important to me. So, when they do get the sack, sometimes I do be tired. I'll be like, all right, coach, that's a sack now. And but it's also like, all right, if it's not a sack, guys, we got to make sure that we're attached, make sure we're on the same page with our uh coverage drills and stuff like that far as when they break out the pocket, grabbing our guys that's next to us. And then it's also helping us getting our conditioning up, too, though. I think uh Bills in preseason and Bills in um during practice and stuff, too, though. So, he's one of those guys that's going to be running around though. So, we're preparing for that. We're preparing for other quarterbacks who do the same thing. >> What stands out of um as you've gotten to know your verse in practices now? >> The energy. He's part of the engine. So, really the energy, really just the fight in him, really just that dog in him that sticks out um playing on the field with him. And then actually playing in front of him, he's just like, "Hey, Q, just just cover me." And I was like, "All right, bet." Next thing you know, he do a spin move out of nowhere, get the sack, and I'll be like, I mean, I ain't even I ain't even got the snap count yet. So, it's just that engine, just that energy, man. He just keeps going, keeps going, keeps going, whether it's first play, last play. He's running down the field also and then coming back and be like, "All right, we ready. Let's go." So, it's really just that energy, man. >> You talked a little bit about the linebacker room as a whole and then you see yourself making an impact this season. >> Uh there's a lot of guys, a lot of guys that's there competing, a lot of guys from different parts of the world and stuff, but the most important thing is that they're all on the same page with competing against each other. There's no solidified spots and stuff like that. So, the biggest thing is just the dog in everybody that wants to be hungry, that wants those plays, that wants to know more about the game, the knowledge of the game is real big in this one like cuz other teams and stuff is most like the ones and twos who got that big part of the scheme of football like the knowledge of football. Here, ones, twos, threes, everybody's on knowledge of football. Everybody knows the reason why we're doing this, situation of football and stuff. So, I like that because I'm actually learning from the younger guys that's been in this division on what what's to look for when it comes time for the season. So, I like that other than just hearing it from the coaches. I'm hearing it from the players' point of view, too. >> This is a a really simple way to look at it like but I just want to float this your way and see what you what you think. Jim Schwartz, obviously really good defensive coordinator, won a Super Bowl in that role, a successful year. Myles Garrett has won two of the last three NFL Defensive Players of the Year. So, people may look at it and say, "Well, the Browns' defense can't be as good with those guys leaving." Do you guys talk about that? Does it motivate you? And what do you think of it? >> No, I ain't never I ain't even talked about that, heard about that. Every day is day by day, getting better every single day, and approving that every single day we're here to be on the field, proving that the engine is here, proving that we're all one accord, not letting the scheme get in the way, just running to the ball with the energy, celebration. >> Is Is there a chant that the defense has a curse word >> Oh, yeah, you like that? Dog food, man. When we're looking at the offense, man, we call them dog food, and everybody barking on one, let everybody know we ready. And then that's really big for me just because you might have a play where something happens where we get a completion or something like that, might have got a first down or something. So, it's like basically making sure we're all on the same page, letting y'all ready to eat. Dog food, dog food, everybody barks. And it's one big bark, So, we all on the same page. So, like no matter what happened the last play, let's let the last play be the last play, and we all on the same page. Yeah, I came over there, man. Nah, man. It's really just uh the heart, mind, fist thing that my defensive coordinator teach. So, I was like, all right, the heart is really like being on the same page, having accountability for everybody. The fist is the um the physical um hitting people, and then also the knowledge on finishing now. And then, the mind is making sure you're in the right place, making sure you're key to your assignments. So, then I was like, how can I bring this all together on the field? I can't keep saying heart, mind, fist, heart, mind, fist, yeah, next play, next play. Now, I was like, all right, child, we all on the same page. Let me get one big bark. So, when I hear that bark go down a little bit, I had to make sure, hey y'all, last play over with. Let's get it again. So, that bark is going to let me know if my team let me know if my defense ready. >> [snorts] >> Yeah, I wanted him here when he was here. I got faith in all the guys I have. Like I said, I call it an engine. Very comfortable with the line I play in front of, also. That's probably like a coach question. I ain't going to lie to you. Oh, yeah. I'm very excited today. That's probably why I'm standing up here. >> [laughter] >> Yeah, I'm very excited about it. But, when y'all hear I say that chant, though, y'all can join in, too, bro. Y'all know what it mean, dog food, dog food. I need one big bark from the whole crowd, from the fans, everybody. Y'all are reporters here. So, that means y'all got a part in this, too, though. You feel me? So, that's what it mean. We all on one accord. I think they got like the dog pound and stuff. I haven't I don't know nothing about that over there, but I know about what Quincy and what Quincy bring to the team. >> What interesting thing that you do to stay mentally sharp daily outside of studying? >> Outside of studying, getting right with God. that's the number one thing, man. Making sure my relationship with him is above everything. Not really focusing on my body, not really focusing on the outside worldly things. Just making sure me and him on the same page. And if me and him on the same page, I'm on his path and then his page, so I'm good with that. It's already written. That's what my granddad always told me. It's already written, so you can't control anything. This happens all about how you respond. So, as long as I respond with that mindset, I'll be good. >> As you've gotten to know Todd Monken a little more, what How would you describe >> Oh, that's my dog. We talk before every single thing cuz I got to make sure his mental right. Because he on the opposite side of ball, so I let him know ain't nothing personal when we when we barking at them or ain't nothing personal when we we beat their ass, man. I let them know that, "Hey, I got a brown jersey for you or whatever jersey we got. You can always join this side." >> How would you kind of describe his leadership and coaching style? >> Straightforward. Straightforward. Straightforward. He going to tell you how it is. He going to tell you what he want. He going to tell you what he expect. And if you not giving that, he going to let you know right then right there. So, I love that part about it cuz it ain't no question about where you stand with him. It ain't no question about where you are in this position or anything like that. >> So, you've seen Todd Gurley in his limited notion pads time. Are you anxious to see him tackle them? >> Who? Talking about all the running back Every running back? All running backs. Anybody who got the ball and trying to get it. It's like a cheetah chasing a gazelle. I'm hungry today. I'm hungry. Appreciate y'all. >> Thank you. Thank you.

title: Denzel Boston Press Conference | August 3rd, 2026
text: Yeah, you know, I think it really comes from just knowing my job, knowing what I'm doing, having good communication with the quarterback, you know, when you're able to do that, you kind of can just play fluid, play free, and just go out there and have fun. >> I know you've caught passes from all the quarterbacks, but it feels like you and Jerry have some connections early in this camp. Where do you think I guess that connection that chemistry comes from? >> You know, I think that just comes in trust. You know, I I believe I got trust with all the quarterbacks, you know, we've been connecting a lot on a lot of different plays. But yeah, I think it just comes down to trust and that's about it. >> How do you think playing high-level college football has prepared you for this step? >> Um, you know, I would say especially with the Big Ten, there's a lot of NFL like ex-NFL defensive coordinators over there. So, being able to see those every type of defenses and all that type of stuff has prepared me and I think also the physical part of the game as well. >> It seems like so many of the highlight plays we've seen you make are some of those 50/50 balls. Just what's your confidence like in those situations, especially just your ability to to use your height and everything? >> Yeah, you know, I think it just comes down to a mentality of like that's my ball. You know, um I think that's what it comes down to. I do have that height advantage that I can abuse when I can, but at the same time I think it comes down to a mentality of I'm going to get it. >> You know, for a bigger guy, we're talking to the you know, Christian Jones about your ability to separate and break down and how you know, that's rare for a guy your size. And I think we've seen plenty examples of it. >> How have you been able to I guess grow that part of the game and how much of a focus is that for you? >> Yeah, you know, in the off season that was a big focus just you know, working on footwork, working on getting in and out of my breaks and all that type of stuff. And also just with having the coaching from Coach CJ, Coach Monken, you know, I got Judy in front of me right now and stuff like that. So, being able to learn from from him and also take the coaching from my coaches, I think that's what's helped me the most elevate my game. >> Are you looking forward to being in pads finally? >> Oh yeah, definitely looking forward to it. You know, now we can get nitty and gritty. Uh the trenches about to get wild and you know, uh finally we can actually block and stuff like that. So, it's going to be fun. >> So, going back to Jimmy for a second, what specifically kind of advice has he given you uh especially like during like this part of training camp that you've got to take to the field? >> Yeah, you know, it's more just like um subtle reminders of things uh like just certain routes, hands routes, you know, um when we're doing outcuts, incuts, just making sure we're not giving away um what would you say? Like hints I guess you could say, not giving away hints of where you're going to go as in like leaning before you're about to break into the route. >> Maybe it's related to that um but when you're running like a comeback, I saw you catch a comeback against Tyson the other day. What's the key there for you to I guess sell him on the fact that you're going to come back and then be able to create that gap? >> Right. Yeah, you know, you got to push him vertical. You got to make give him to flip his hips and run with you. And at that point, once you get to the breakpoint, you got to make sure you get that body turn. You got to make sure you get that foot almost parallel to the line that you'd be stopping at and uh just come back downhill. >> What have been the toughest part of camp for you so far? >> The toughest part of camp? The meetings, sitting in the meetings all day. You know, you get a little drowsy and stuff. So, I'd say that's probably been the toughest part. Out there on the field, that's just fun. >> Nothing set in stone, they're mixing and matching, but how do you feel like the skill sets of the receiver room and even uh the tight ends sort of mesh together? >> You know, I think honestly, I think we mesh very well together. You know, we have the quick, fast, twitchy guys. We got tall guys who can go make plays above the rim. Um and then you you know, I think we're just meshing very well and I think that you know, we're able to make plays across the board. >> What time do you the meetings start and what time do they end? >> Meetings start at Well, live So, we sometimes have a 7:00 live and then meetings will start at 8:00. And then that first session will end at about 11:00 and then we'll go into um practice and then after practice, we'll have another about 3-hour 4-hour block meetings. >> Is is it uh just your natural ability or did you work throughout your career to just be able to catch passes? >> Um it's definitely something that I work on every single day, but also I have always been a natural catcher. title: TE Adam Trautman on re-signing with Broncos: ‘I always wanted to be here’
text: Adam, [snorts] were there were there any places that you looked about maybe moving on to? >> Um what I mean I'm not going to say who, but I mean no, I was never looking to move on, absolutely not. Obviously, he relates to the players well. Um, and yeah, I mean, we're we're excited to have him. He's a I mean, he is a he is a little ball of energy out there, honestly, and it's pretty it's pretty it's pretty fun. text: [music] >> All right, here we are back at a soggy St. John day four of training camp or practice number four anyway, and uh the rain has returned. It was here the first two days. If it's slippery, the defense can't cut and change direction." Defense had a good day today. >> They did. A lot of pass breakups, which we'll get to in just a second. Um Easily the wettest training camp I have ever seen. Um cuz three rainy days at one camp is a lot over the course of what is usually two and a half weeks, back in the day three and a half weeks of camp. >> Right. >> Uh you'd get like two rainy days, maybe three. to have three in the first four practices is pretty much unprecedented for a Saint John Fisher. So, it's uh it's crazy to see it. But fans are braving the elements. I got to give them credit. They are out here in force despite the weather. >> I wonder how this I ask you this we were sitting out there under our umbrellas watching them slog through this. It's interesting to think about how's this going to manifest itself? Is it going to set them behind? Is it going to put them ahead? I kind of doubt it. But it does change the formula, right? It changes the formula. They've got to think on their feet and they've got to adjust to this cuz they're not getting normal reps. None of these reps are normal. There's always this I was telling Sal Capaccio this on the there you got this thing hanging over you. You're trying to get this through this rep and there's always this rain is it or my feet can I cut like this? Is the ball going to be slippery? Do I have to adjust? Um Kony Ealy Walker, an interesting player, very high-cut, long corner, 6'2, 204, undrafted rookie out of Arkansas, running with the second team opposite Ike Boettger so guy to keep an eye on here uh to see if he can make an impact. And then 11-on-11 red zone, the offense was throwing an awful lot of screens out there. Getting some screen work done today. >> They also did a drill where it was deliberate that Josh is going to run around and they were going to do some They they ran through a scramble drill down close. They're fast and they're athletic, and I I think that's the biggest thing I notice about this camp. >> Yeah. Not participating today, C.J. Gardner-Johnson with his lower calf strain. Head coach Joe Brady saying that they were fortunate the injury wasn't more serious. No timetable on Gardner-Johnson's return. So, I I think everybody's breathing a sigh of relief that it wasn't a season-ending Achilles injury. I was here on Saturday watching that practice, and it was scary. Um >> Yeah. >> Non-contact, grabbing his heel immediately. I was hoping he just got cleated by another player, cuz that's not fun getting that on the back here. Like, that does not feel good. Um Cuz even though he didn't rupture his Achilles, a lower calf strain involves your Achilles. And so, there This is a athletic training staff and a medical staff that errs on the side of caution. Um as for Did I say who had the pass breakups today? title: Michael Hoecht: "Freaks Of Nature" On Defense, Preparing To Be Ready Week 1 | One Bills Live
text: Uh, wet, wet training camp here. Steve was talking about this earlier. First of all, welcome. Thanks for stopping by and giving us some time. Here, I'll give you this towel if you want to dry off a little bit. Um I think the biggest thing coming into this camp for fans is, "Oh my god, Michael Hoare's on the field." Like, people I think people have become accustomed to hearing Achilles injury and automatically thinking calendar year, full calendar year. So, I know there have been some great advances in the surgery to repair these things, and I know you had the lesser I I say it, may not be for you, but the lesser of the two Achilles ruptures. Can you just kind of walk fans through the Achilles rupture you experienced and why it at least gave you the opportunity to maybe come back a little sooner than some other guys. >> So, uh, my understanding of it is there's two ways that it can tear. It's tendon splits in half or tendon rips off bone. Uh, both of them off the heel heel bone. And, uh, so mine was the one that split in half, which means you just kind of sew it back together. Once that's healed, you can start your rehab. And then, if it comes off the bone, you have to anchor and screw it into the bone, wait for the bone to heal, and then start your rehab. So, that's usually why off the bone takes a little longer cuz you have to wait for the bone to heal, then it has to come together, then it has to go. >> And how does it I mean, just walk us through how how different do you feel this year? Is it a new normal for you or is it going to is it just trying to get used to it? What are the doctors telling you about what you can expect? >> Yeah, I I I mean, I feel great. Uh, you know, I think every single person's going to be different. Uh, and I had an unbelievable team with everybody, you know, the two brothers Mika and there, Nick Lidstrom who was an intern with us who helped me out last season. Uh, A.J. Blue, he's our return to play like strength coach. He got me going. Tom Gormley, he was like my uh, outside counsel for a second opinion. And then, Neal ElAttrache is like the goat surgeon. So, uh, you know, if you tear your Achilles, you know, he's the guy that you go to. He's the guy you go to. So, I mean, I had every advantage from like it's putting together the Avengers of a team to get me back out here [laughter] and yeah, they they did really really well. >> I know that I saw you during OTAs and we were just passing in the hallway and I just asked you one question and you're always great with, you know, sharing stuff about your journey here in this rehab and you're like, "I'm already running 18 miles an hour." I'm like like he's just breaking off numbers for me and I'm like I was just saying, "Hey and good to see you're doing well." He's just giving me like lobbing out the info. But, when did you I guess when did you feel cuz you're always resolutely positive in any rehab cuz that usually lends itself to having a more successful rehab. But, when did you kind of feel like I'm going to get there? Like I am this is my goal, but there's a difference between that's the goal and I'm going to make it. Like when did you get to that point where you're like, "You know what? This timing's going to line up good. I'm going to make it." >> Yeah, I mean, I was around for Cam Akers when he did his Achilles in LA and you know, he was 5 months, so I was like, "If it's possible in 5 months, I'm going to be I'm going to be there." You know, we were joking around in the training room that if we had a playoff game to play in May, end of May, I could have probably played in it. So, that was kind of like our goal and then, you know, our sports science team's being smart about rep counts early on and making sure my ramp up is appropriate. But, you know, all the entire goal and system and everything is, you know, headed towards getting me ready for week one. Any concerns about the wet weather? >> Slipping and falling all the I mean, not more than anybody else? >> They didn't tell me anything, so I mean, that's that was sort of my philosophy is like I don't really want to know some of the conversations because I don't want to hear them saying like, "Oh, you know, how much do we trust him?" I tell them I'm going to go 100% every single snap I'm out there and then you guys tell me when to shut it down and I'm just not even going to think about it. >> So, the last time you were on the field for this team, you were playing in a different defensive system. You come back and now it's largely a 3-4 system at its core. Um and you know, coach Leonard has said he wants to be very varied, wants to be very multiple. This isn't foreign to you. You've been in this kind of a defense before in LA. Um and it looks like you're going to have the same role of calling pass rush games when you're on the field in passing situations, but maybe just encapsulate for us what the transition has been like for the group because this is something that you guys all got to do together as a team and even though you have familiarity with it, maybe there are some other guys who haven't. So, how has the group kind of ingratiated themselves and assimilated themselves to this system? >> Sure. I I mean, we've got a really really good group of outside linebackers and they've definitely embraced the challenge. I mean, just visually as anybody in the stands probably saw, you're going to see us standing up a lot more uh cuz you know, [snorts] that's what they want. They want these, you know, 6'4 dynamic 265 to 275-lb freaks of nature out in space hitting guys. Is he a dropper? Is he a rusher? Is he making calls? Is he not? Uh so, you know, I think the main philosophy and this is what pretty much this is the direction of the league is we're going to find our best 11 guys. We're going to put those 11 guys on the field and whatever it looks like, however we have to get there, it's going to be our best 11 verse their best 11 and we're going to that's what we're going to live with. >> Basically speaking for for casual fans or whatever, there's five guys on the line of scrimmage and the two end guys have their hands off the ground. The difference between that and a 4-3 is you got four guys on the line of scrimmage and three guys behind them. The The difference is now you have five guys the fifth guy is that much closer to the quarterback and the offensive line have to make their decisions and sort through it that much faster. Um and you can still just rush four guys but they don't know which four of the five are coming and they have to decide it faster. So, that kind of gives you the ability to for your coordinators, hopefully, to play more games and you guys on the field, obviously, to pick games and do your stuff. But, it gives you a lot more freedom to get a little bit more of a quicker pass rush and more pressure on the quarterback even using the same same four guys or a different four or whatever four. So, is that kind of the basic philosophy that you guys are getting at and it seems like you maybe Russo, certainly Jovan Solomon, are fit better for this kind of thing than you were even the one you had last year. >> Yeah, absolutely. I I I mean, the biggest thing is quarterbacks in this league and coordinators in this league are too good that if you know or if an offense knows like, "Hey, this is cover two. These are your known rushers. This is I mean, you're going to get diced." Uh and that's why, you know, defenses are always trying to look for advantages of uh you know, how can we make that quarterback get off his first read? How can we make him hold the ball in the pocket just a little bit longer? Um and that's, you know, when you have five guys, uh you can either rush all five and you have five one-on-ones with the offensive lineman or you can drop one, you can drop two, you can bring a lot of different multiple looks at quarterbacks to hopefully get them to their second lead or second read and hold the ball and create negative plays. Um and yeah, I mean, our outside linebacker group has done a really, really good job about, you know, learning the new terminology and you know, playing in space, uh you know, not necessarily as much um thinking more defensive end sort of jetting, but more that outside linebacker where uh I was always told that you really have to play in the gray because it's not always an exact perfect look and you have to be able to figure out what tools can I use at different times, uh you know, more like in the run game. Yeah. >> Calling pass rush games is not something that's foreign to you. I mean, you were assigned that duty last year, even though your time on the field unfortunately was brief. Did you do that in LA and and if so, what makes you comfortable kind of taking on that added responsibility? >> Yeah, I I mean, I think I'm just a football junkie. Uh you know, I love talking ball and understanding how the pieces all sort of come together. Um and you know, I kind of take that as my responsibility where I need to know what every guy is doing. So, if anybody has a question, you know, I can tell them the same way, you know, if offenses know uh on you know, first or second down exactly what's coming, you know, they're going to dice you up. If a defense gets to third down and every single person knows this is pass, we're about to pin our ears back and go pass rush, like that's advantage defense. And I never want to be, you know, you only get so many third downs throughout a game, and I never want somebody to be out there with me not knowing necessarily what they're doing and I can't give them that answer because it's also going to mess my rush up. Uh you know, so we're all, you know, we need all 11 guys on every single snap to be right in order for one person to get the production. >> How much freedom inside a call do you have to like make the guy and and how much of it's art and how much of it is science? I mean, you watch film and you get to know that offensive line. You have a pretty good key on what their protection's going to be. How much freedom do you have within that and you know, with and the relationship between you and Ed and Rousseau, the whole gang? How much freedom do you have to say, "No, no, we're going to do this instead of that up front on the rush?" >> Yeah, I I mean, I would say uh that sort of freedom uh is earned and you know, we earn it out in training camp where you know, coaches are absolutely they give us, you know, all the freedom in the world to um work together as like a rush group and learn who how do how does this three-tech rush and how do I play with this guy? What's his get-off like? You know, if you're rushing very different than Ed Oliver. And uh so, the more, you know, you rep that, the more coaches trust you to be able to you know if they make a call you can override some stuff cuz ultimately we're the ones out there. But that leash you know if you start to mess things up or you you know if you have two guys on top of the quarterback and Josh like takes off through that leash starts get reeled in pretty quickly. So uh yeah I mean football like anything like you know the trust is earned and the players on the field the coaches have to trust that they know what they're doing. >> There are a fair number of vets at your position on this roster but a lot of the other positions on defense this this coaching staff and the personnel department kind of made a conscious decision that you were going to go considerably younger on your side of the ball at a lot of other positions more athletic perhaps as well. Um who in these first few days whether you've noticed it on the practice field or even reviewing practice film has kind of caught your eye from that young group of people you know that's just getting their legs under him here in the league. >> Yeah I I mean Zane Durant's had a couple good days on the defensive line. I mean you can look at him uh and you can tell that he's going to be uh a good run player in the middle and that's the hardest part I think you know cuz I came in as a three tech too and they always say the hardest uh test for young defensive lineman is how well you handle double teams and he's done a pretty good job on that. Um Caleb at middle linebacker has done a uh really good job both special teams and uh defense so he's definitely popped on tape but yeah I mean we've got like a young group um and a lot of guys uh are you know taking the right steps but the real test will be tomorrow when we have full pads on because you know offenses start to be able to run full schemes and do some of the uh more fun parts of football that uh you know I'm sure there'll be a couple welcome to the NFL moments out tomorrow. >> Yeah you were here last year this is a much shorter training camp. You got like three more practices here uh St. John Fisher and then you're going to be back in the new building and it's going to be all bells and whistles. How much work did you not get done because of the rain? >> Honestly, I don't think we missed a beat. Uh you know, I think our philosophy through this year and I'm sure you'll see it all around the building as we put the ball down. It doesn't matter sunshine, rain, snow, wind. You know, we're putting the ball down. You don't pick and choose when you want to compete. You just go out and compete. Uh so, that's you know, our mentality. You walk out there and uh you know, it's lightly raining. You're like, all right, it's not so bad. It starts pouring down raining. It's like, doesn't matter. We put the ball down. We go compete. Especially in the red zone. Got to be able to throw. Got to be able to catch and we live in Western New York. You're going to have to play in rain. You're going to have to play in snow and if we can't practice in it, we can't play in it. So, we're not going to let uh an advantage of we get to be here the entire year. Uh we're not going to lose that by, you know, going inside and being scared of the elements. >> Well, I mean, the pads go on. I hope we see a blitz period soon here. We're kind of we're kind of chomping at the bit for one of those. I imagine you guys are, too. Uh we were talking to Josh the other day. He goes, we got to get ready. I know it's coming. It's coming soon. So, good luck with that. Good luck this season. Stay in one piece. And uh great to see you back out there. That's Michael Hurl joining us here.

title: Dalton Kincaid Speaks To The Media | Buffalo Bills
text: Saw you go down for a little bit today. How are you doing? How's your knee? >> Doing good. Uh it was a family jewels shot, so Yeah, knee is all good. >> [laughter] >> It was a knee It was a knee to the family jewels. >> Got it. Glad to hear. >> Genitals are better than the knee, right? I guess. >> Oh, yeah. >> Kevin, what's your thoughts on that? >> Oh, 100% yeah. I was just uh a few minutes of pain. >> How do you see today otherwise? Obviously a little chaotic weather. Um obviously every year you kind of have to evolve and change just with the league, you know. Year four, how do you feel like you've matured as a player and just as as a man? >> Yeah, I mean it it it flies by. The vets tell you that when you come in as a rookie and you don't really believe them and then next thing you know, you you blink and it's going into your four. Um I think a lot of things just kind of slow down. You you know you have more of an idea of what's going on. You you have more experience on the field and and seeing defenses and coverage and alignments and I think you just Rob talks a lot about vision and it's kind of an understanding of what's going to happen. Um so, I think kind of having better vision as years go on and and seeing defenses better and understanding concepts better and and knowing where you need to be against what coverage. So, um obviously we have a few weeks to kind of work on that and and try new things, but um I think it's just a little bit more confidence going into your four. >> When you talk about attacking the off season, did you have like particular things you were focusing on or was it more of just all kind of time on task? >> Um the main focus was probably just strength. Um a lot of load early on in the off season and just kind of working on that. Um I have a a trainer I've been working with in in California who I feel really confident in and in the plan we had in place and him communicating with the strength staff and training staff here about, you know, what I need and and what's been working. So, um I feel like everybody kind of working together just to kind of formulate the best plan, you know, to have now and then as we go into the season. So, um feel really good. >> How tough is that to focus on load? I mean you go into an off season, you probably have have bit of a break, but then ramping up like you would if you're loading. How tough is that? Like just to go into a mindset like we're going to work really hard. >> Yeah. Um I mean it's a choice you make, you know, you can choose to have more time off or choose to uh attack it earlier and um I think that was the kind of the plan this year was just to attack it earlier and get a head start on it. Um I think I needed it physically um and uh you know, I feel like it's it's paying off and hopefully it pays off, you know, later into the season as well. >> What do you What do you expect to see out of Dawson Knox in year two? We saw a lot last year, but what do you think is going to happen with him this season? >> Um you know, I'm just hoping that confidence grows. I think that's a a big part of success in this league is having confidence out in the field. Um and just, you know, more knowledge, more experience, um understanding looks better in in defenses. Um I think he's a a tremendous blocker. You know, I think we saw that as his rookie year and and going into year two, you you know, you expect it to to get better. Um you know, it's hard to get better because he had such a good rookie year, but um I think, you know, you can expect him to have the same impact if not if not more of an impact. >> What have you seen from Keith Carter Michael? Has he brought in some little nuances, differences to this offense? >> Yeah, Keith's been great. Um I think he has plenty of knowledge, um plenty of experience in this league. He's he's lived through so many phases of this league. Um so just kind of picking his ear and picking his brain about, you know, what he sees and what he likes out there and and his experience with um the tight end position uh throughout his time in the league. >> What does going against a Jim Schwartz defense in camp do for you? After your first few years in the league, you've now gone against first couple against Sean McDermott's defense um every day for two weeks, basically. >> Yeah. I mean it's a it's a lot of different looks. You know, we're going up against a completely different front. Um and then coverage, you know, it it it plays out a little differently. So, um I think going against, you know, our our defense we've had the last few years, you you know, you get accustomed to that look and you're used to that look. And then now going against this this defense, um you got a whole new look and you're working different combos, you're working different blocks, um you know, routes adjust uh accordingly to coverage. So, I think it's it's good to get that experience, especially going against them every day. >> Dion, can you say how you Are you Are you re-did the way you approach the break between OTAs and mini camp and here? Are you altering anything now that you are here at camp and how you're day you're approaching your body? >> Yeah. Um I probably probably not so much during camp. I think during season it'll look a little different. Um you know, in in lifting, in loading at certain points during the week. Um in camp, the schedule's been great to to where we can load pretty well um before off days and and get a good day of rest before then. but I think last year, you know, I tried to do a few different things during camp and and probably didn't work out as well for me. So, um I think the schedule we have in place right now has been in really good for me and for everyone on the team. >> To go back to going up against this defense, is there anyone I know the look is different, but is there any player who's standing out to you right now as you kind of have those back and forth from day to day? >> Um I mean, obviously a lot of guys have talked about, you know, Caleb coming in and and his confidence and it does look like he belongs and um like he isn't a rookie out there. Um Bradley Chubb and Greg, you know, we're seeing a lot of them on the edge. So, getting good looks against them. Um I remember my rookie year, Bradley Chubb lining up opposed opposing me and he was like, "Do you like it here in Buffalo?" And it was like >> the oddest question to be asked as a rookie. And then you flash forward, you know, 3 4 years later and he's on our team. So, I think it's pretty cool. Um just him to come in and just seamlessly become a a leader on this team. Um you know, both on the offense and defense side of the ball. Um But, yeah, I think Caleb has been flashing a lot and then the those guys in the end are looking pretty good. >> You did that in the game? >> Yeah, at home my rookie year. I think it was pretty early on on in the season. And I was just kind of like taken back by it cuz it's usually trash talk coming from those guys. And you know, obviously I knew who Bradley Chubb was coming in as a rookie. So, it was like I was like, that's pretty cool coming from that guy. It's like a sportsmanship award. >> Maybe he was doing a little future planning. >> Yeah, you know, you know, it worked out. Oh, I told him I loved it. You know, I think it's the same answer everybody gives. So, it was a little recruiting pitch. >> It's an invisible string. >> Yeah. >> Last year you were on a little bit of a pitch count because you were never fully healthy. Now that you feel better, do you see yourself hitting the ground running with more snaps like week one or do you think it'll be more of hey, let's keep the pitch count kind of where it was last year so December and January you feel more like 100% >> Um you know, I hope it's hitting the ground running in full full speed. Um ultimately that's not really up to me. It's you know, I I just go in when my number's called. But, um given kind of where I was at physically last year, we were kind of put in a position where I had to be on a pitch count unfortunately. And um you know, that kind of wears on you just not being able to be out there, you know, in in certain situations and be there for your teammates. Um So, you know, this year I feel really good where I'm at right now. Um and hoping to to continue to feel really good.

title: Edgerrin Cooper: 'We need everybody on the same page'
text: Yeah, for sure. Uh, you know, season coming on, coming along, so it's good, you know, to get get that feeling back. Uh, so right now I just get to go out, look at them, and have fun with them. >> You're not bringing them to family night? >> I [laughter] am. >> Not going to ride in on >> Like I said, you never know with me. Does it is it different compared to a normal practice? >> Uh yeah, but no it's it's it's going to be packed in there, so it's going to be you know, game like energy. title: Chris McClellan on fans at training camp: 'Shows the love and support the community has for us'
text: How do you go about it to like let up around the quarterback? It seems like >> It's very difficult. I It's a major point of emphasis obviously with this being the pros, you know, stay off the quarterback is, you know, that's that's the strength of our team, the heart of our team, so you want to stay off of him as much as possible, but also you want to simulate and replicate getting close to the game as possible. In the game you want to finish on the quarterback, so you know, it's been difficult these last few days, but I feel like we've been doing better as far as just kind of getting to the spot and veering off. >> Were you disappointed there was no one-on-one today? >> A little bit, yes, I was. I was I was looking forward to kind of go out there and and have like a for sure rush one-on-one and and get the opportunity, but I think we have it tomorrow, so I'm excited for that for sure. You get you. >> How was music able to really ramp up the intensity of practice? It was really loud in the beginning, so how was it able to really get you in the groove? >> mean, honestly, for me I I block I try to block out all the noise, you know, so if if anything, for me it's more of like a distraction, but I like to go out there and kind of focus on the man in front of me, my job, my timing and you know, I like to visualize what what I'm going to do during the play, so that's how I've always been. The music, crowd really don't affect me. I just kind of I'm one track minded when I get on the field. >> How does it feel getting reps with the ones? >> Uh it's a great feeling, man, especially now that we're in pads and trying to, you know, getting deeper into camp, to still have the opportunity to go out there and play with the one defense and just be with the pros, guys like Z'Darius out there playing the defense is awesome. >> What's your excitement level for family night on Friday? >> I'm super excited, you know, so my family has not came up here yet since I got drafted, so everybody will be here. I think coming Thursday night, so I'll get to see them Friday and obviously they get to see the stadium, but I'm excited to see their reaction, so I'm just excited to have everybody down here and to [snorts] I heard they said it's supposed to be like 60,000 to 70,000 people there, so just to get that full experience in Lambeau and get those jitters out before, you know, we get to our real first home game against the Falcons, like that's going to be exciting for sure. >> Did you have fans watch in college? >> Excuse me. >> Did you have fans watching in college at so >> we had a few open practices at Mizzou, but not really nothing like this. Like this is almost like a mini game every every day. So and I think that really adds to the intensity of practice just with the fans being there. You know, everybody's always going to show out when it's a crowd. So it's it's kind of like that added hype to every practice. >> What do you think of the fans so far? >> They've been awesome. You know, like of course everybody is just more excited for the offense every time they get a big catch or something. You know, I wish they would cheer when we got those sacks and TFLs, but it's a part of it. You know, but it it's a good thing to have those people out there and it really just shows the love support that the community has for us. You know, it just like I thought it would die down from the first day with like the bikes and people come to practices. It's almost like it's ramped up. So it's just been awesome to be a part of that every day. >> Are you a goal setter? Like do you write down individual goals? >> Yeah, so every day is just kind of we we say something to you in the D-line room. Just you know, what are you working on today? Like KB will come up to me every day and be like, "What are you working on?" Like just for today I'm trying to work on keeping pads lower and just getting knocked back. You know, first day of pads so I'm always thinking I want to be the most physical guy out there. So that's just kind of I set daily goals to accomplish and after we go back every day watch the tape I see what I did, see what I didn't do and go back and kind of see what okay, what are my what are my goals tomorrow? What I need to keep working on? What I need to what I get better at? You know, just always picking apart parts of my game. You know, and I'm always asking guys like every day like Hargrave especially like man, watch me on these reps. Like what do I look like? What do I need to work on? What can I improve on? Just trying to see like learn from guys that have done it at a high level for such a long time and get the best parts of their game and kind of take everything I can from them. While I have that opportunity to be out there going against the one offense. >> So then you like on a day-to-day basis you have goals but does that become like week-to-week and then have you thought about your season-long individual goals at all? >> Yeah, yeah, I mean there's certain goals I've set for myself for the season that will come once the season get here. But right now I'm just focused on the day-to-day between these practices and trying to grind it out and get better while I'm in camp.

title: Head Coach Matt LaFleur Press Conference
text: Mhm. >> [music] [music] >> Mhm. >> [snorts] >> What's the message to the guys heading off there for the day? >> So I mean, it's always team first and you got to protect each other, but obviously this is our first opportunity to come together in pads and just went over the rules of engagement in terms of how we thud and and what that looks like. >> Are the addresses allowed to bull rush now? >> They are. One thing that we just to try to eliminate as much gray for our players in terms of studying in the [snorts] core versus when you're outside of that tight end box if you will. Carrington >> He hurt his leg. >> Back today? >> No, he won't be he'll be out. >> Matt, I know you love it when we ask you scheme questions. Like, we'll continue to get more of that good-on-good work uh as we get the pads on and and are in pads more consistently. >> Thank you. >> When the pads came on, first Rodriguez with the start of the top, what are your initial impressions today? >> Yeah, I mean, he did kind of what he you you you think he's going to do, in a way, right? I mean, I don't think he meant to necessarily like I don't think he even really lowered his shoulder on Caleb. It just was one of those hits. And um yeah, he showed up, which is kind of what you're hoping. And I think, you know, he was feeling better. He's continuously getting better. And we're just trying to be smart with all right, getting him the work, getting him acclimated while not trying to aggravate it, knowing that we're so early on. And uh I know he was excited about getting the pads on. >> Is there any part of that likes working in the rain a little bit? >> Yeah. Yeah, I mean, it's like it's football, right? And we are it has to be an edge for us here in Florida. And um knowing that, shoot, last year, right? We had a delay and all that, you know, week one. And um just we we got to get that work in. Now, with some of the other like the one-on-one pass game, like that that would have been a a waste of time to do out here. So, we wanted to make sure we got clean work in there. Uh which I I, you know, it was some good work. And then, you know, these guys they don't care, right? And they want to just play. And they prefer to stay outside on the grass than go inside. So, um I just typically, you know, you're concerned just a anchoring, guys anchoring and slipping out, whatever. But, it's football. I mean, stuff happens. >> How have you seen Anton kind of adapt to different things he's done in >> Yeah, I think he's done a nice job. I mean, it's it's part of what we've done, moving those guys around and and seeing what sticks and if um if that ends up sticking, you know, hopefully that's a good thing for us and um I think he's put together uh you know, five good practices so far that you're pleased with seeing the consistency. That's something that we're continuously challenging, not just Anton with, but that entire unit and and group is just consistency, consistent effort, consistent technique, consistent finish. Um but I've been pleased with him just handling it pretty seamlessly so far. Yeah, I thought Rook did a nice job today. I thought he flashed um you know, more today than maybe in some of the previous days. I think he might have two sacks in the Mamba period on the first two plays of of his rack. So, nice to see him flash. It's It's always a little bit more realistic when you get the pads on. I mean, the whole thing is like pass pro sucks with no pads on. It just does. Um so, it's nice to see him win when you're expecting the pass rush to maybe be a little less than it's been because of the pads being on. So, that was nice to see him flash and I mean, you know, we talked about B.J. flashing and some of those I thought Danny flashed a little bit today as well. So, um we need those guys to continuously give us meaningful reps. >> Brian looked good in one-on-ones and then he had the 100 yard catch. >> Yeah. >> Just where do these days stack up for him? What is that going to do for him? >> The connection, man. The chemistry between not just he and Trevor, but us, right? Me as as a coach, as a play caller, um the rest of the group, the the entire team's confidence and um swagger that that brings. When when you can throw the ball over somebody's head, it's just a it's a threat, man. And and it's something that uh we need. We need not just him to be able to do that, but when on some of the other reps that I mean, he's run a lot of routes out here that maybe weren't getting targeted to him that he's won as well that I've been pleased with. So it's just I think it brings everybody up. It elevates everybody's game when when BT's playing at his highest level. >> We didn't get to talk to you yesterday, but what did you think about Travis making those splash plays on both sides of the ball? >> Yeah, that was good. I mean, just coming off of what he what he's gone gone through to come out and and make an impact fairly early on, right? And for the first time probably since we've sorry, since we've all been together was like back-to-back, right? Like making a play on offense, then on defense, then back on offense. That was really just I think great for everybody to see, not just, you know, the fans and the exposure, all that. That's great. It's more just for his confidence and his comfort level getting back out on the grass with his teammates, competing, and for for them to all see him compete like that. Go ahead. >> Liam, I know you could probably talk about the receivers all day and the supply and the talent level. What are you finding out with each of these practices, something new about them? Is something surprising you about these guys maybe? >> Um you know, I think we're at a point where we are getting to know each other more. I mean, today Jacoby had a really good one-on-one fade down the sideline. And so it's like, okay, he won we got to get him going more on some of those vertical routes and not just, you know, keep limiting his tree to some of those in-breakers that we all know that he's really good at. We've got to make sure that we're giving him complimentary cuts, whether it's out or vertical, so that he can you know, when you're playing the game within the game, you're not feeling like people are leaning on you one way or another based on your strengths or your weaknesses. So, yeah, we are learning stuff about these guys on a day-to-day basis and um you know, just I what I've been pleased is with and I told them this before we got going was we threw the ball a lot in the spring. I mean, that was the intent. That was what we were trying to do. So, you're just limiting the amount of reps. I think what they've done is is maximize the reps that they're getting and being very intentional about the connection and chemistry that they have. No, go ahead. Finish. Finish. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. For sure. Yeah, the combination just being thicker on combinations a little bit. Um sometimes based on the scheme sometimes the O-line will think they have to maybe get on an angle because of where the ball's going. Like say it's outside zone, they feel like they just have to run because it's outside. Well, don't No, let's let's take care of the down first and be a little bit thicker through combinations so that uh we're moving the line of scrimmage. I think that's something that we've been very intentional about whether it's with wide zone, mid zone, duo. That Those are the only three plays we have in right now. Um just being more intentional about like chipping on our combinations and being a little bit more vertical so that we're not just running, all right, sideline to sideline and getting thinned out on the you know, at the line of scrimmage in the point of attack. So, I think that that's something that those guys have worked diligently on since the spring and once you get into the camp, you're able to see it a little bit more. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I've actually been pleased with him. Um running routes that like yeah, he doesn't get a target on, or he's not the primary route runner on. He's going to be more than fine in terms of like what he's going to be able to do, whether it's targeting him or not, fitting in the progressions, and being there. Um you know, I'm I'm going to be he'll be more than fine with us being able to go whether he's in an 11 or 12, and he's the Y, and he's opposite Brandon, or whatever it is, and you're able to be able to mix those things up. I'm I'm more than pleased with what he's able to do from a route tree standpoint. >> What's your thought on how last off season was about finding your edge, and this off season has been about attacking that edge? >> Now that you've acknowledged that there's an edge present, does that help with the intentionality and the fluidity of these practice periods? >> That's right. Um you know, defensively there's some uh disguises and things that we're experimenting with as well. I think there's so much more in right now with especially with the first group um and we've definitely experimented with some schemes and concepts and some fundamentals that when you watch the off season, you self scout yourself and then you look around the league and we do that exactly back-to-back. So, like when we watch all of our wide zones, we watch let's call it 100 of them. Directly underneath are the top, let's call it three to five teams around the league that we felt like ran wide zone the best and then they're cut up and exactly underneath that as well. So, it's like you get to see you and you get to see the best that are doing that exact concept. So, whether it's scheme, truly the concept, or a fundamental, you know, of how they're doing it, well, hey, does that fit us? And we're trying some of those things now, yeah. >> I was told you have a competition with Chris Manhertz. Can you elaborate more on the competition? >> You want to nail it. Oh.
