Um, you talk about too, I mean, world class DTS. I mean, that that really sets the tone um, for any defense. you know, the linebackers are flying around. You know, secondary, you know, you just see great communication out there. Dudes knowing what's going on. So, it's definitely a huge step up and it's definitely been tough on us. Um, you know, when you go against that that kind of D line, it gets tough, but you know, we've been a able to throw in a little wrinkle here and there, but no, it's definitely exciting to see just the progress they've made and it's definitely made our jobs a lot harder. >> Tell me the how how much you've been impressed by Tyler Booker. >> Oh, I mean, he's just a I mean, a worldass player. Um, world class athlete. I mean, he's so smart, too. And that's one of the things, you know, I enjoy the most. You know, we get to pick each other's brains, and, you know, yeah, we're both young guys, but I mean, he's just a true professional. I mean, he's a phenomenal guard, and I'm I'm so glad I get to play next to him. >> And then, how much does it benefit y'all now that you've been able to not not only just you and Tyler, but Tyler on the other side as well, and the whole offensive line getting in sync and having played together now for a little bit? >> Yeah, absolutely. That's huge. Um, obviously, we all know, you know, team chemistry, especially in the O line's huge. So just continuing getting those continuous reps, you know, hey, you know, and communicating with each other after the play. Hey, did I give you enough there or you know, what could I have done better? I think it's just we're take we're continuing to take big steps up and you know, I'm excited for what this group could do. >> Appreciate Cooper. Absolutely. >> Thank you. >> So, uh, how was your first NFL practice in pads? >> Well, it was great. Shoot, we got to got the hit finally, but it was fun. I had fun out there competing. >> Have you been looking forward to this day? >> Yes, sir. Definitely. Shoot. It's real football now. Yeah. So, what's what's the biggest difference for you when you put the pads on? >> Uh, just the contact. Like we can finally hit each other uh without like trying to like keep take care like you're going to take care of your teammates, but it's kind of some carelessness into hitting, you know, but still being smart. >> Yeah. Uh, how are things going so far for you? You got one week down, just getting started here, but how's the transition been like for you? >> It's been good. I'm getting better every day. Um, seeing my steps and my progress, um, how I'm approaching things. So yeah, I'll say that. >> So who are uh some of the veterans who have kind of helped you along in this? >> Yeah, Rashan Gary definitely uh just working out with him over the offseason with uh BMAC, one of uh our trainers. So that was real good. Just building a bond, building a brotherhood. >> What uh what are the biggest things that you're working on at this point to try to make an impact your rookie year? >> Right. Um just making every one of my pass rushers look the same. um getting off the ball, just using my speed, using my explosiveness to the full potential. >> Yep. Um when you uh look at your expectations for this year, what what are they now? >> Right. Um getting on the field and making an impact. Um whether it's pass rush, run, defense, anything. Just getting on the field and helping the team out to uh get to the ultimate goal, which was a Super Bowl. >> How about Christian Parker's defense? Uh how does it compare with what you've what you've been exposed to before? Right. Um, shoot. Now I'm just like basically a wide nine. So I get to play uh to my liking, to my speed. Sometimes like at UCF I be in a four eye a little bit and 250 260 lb 4 is a little hard, but now uh I love being on the edge. So yes, >> appreciate it, Malachi. Thank you. >> They just narrowly got the best of you yesterday. Uh well last practice, but then today you had the best practice. You know, few PBUs. Just how was you coming along development wise? >> Yeah, man. Um keep it brief, man. Hey, it's a reason them boys top five >> for real. And yeah, you could tell from, you know, last week, watching last week and, you know, started this week is they kind of made me better, you know, I mean, going against them boys and competing against them boys every day, even our backups, you know, Florida. Um, they just sharpen my skills each and every day. And I go go back and watch film, see what I need to do, see what they see how they move, you know what I mean? And fix it in practice. But them boys, man, y'all know, y'all see, that's that's just who they is. And and what does it do for you mentally to be out here this time of year fully healthy and and going toe- to- toe with these guys? >> Uh mentally, man, you just got to take it one at a time. You know what I mean? At the end of the day, you know, they're trying to achieve we all trying to achieve a goal. You know, I'm trying to be the best player that I can be every day. And to have the top five receivers on the team, you know what I mean? That that also helps me along this journey. So, I mean, it's it's a blessing definitely. >> What it mean for you being back in full pads as you continue to try and get back to where you want to be? >> Oh, man. Like I said, take it day by day. I mean, 1% every day. You know what I mean? Just get better in my skills and the areas that I need to fix in the rooms that I need to need to come in. You know what I mean? Watch film, fix what I need to fix, you know? >> You guys only have 10 of those full fully padded practices in camp. What's the sense of urgency like as you go through? >> Compete every day, man. You know what I mean? Got to have that intent to come and get better every day. I mean, at the end of the day, these your teammates, but you trying to achieve your own personal goal, and that's just how I come out every day. You know what I mean? take a deep breath before I come out here and just blow it out. It's time to practice, time to go. >> Talk about your health. Simple as that. >> Your health and confidence compared to last year. >> Health and confidence, I say. I mean, obviously my health is 10 times better. Confidence is always there, man. It's always that heart and that grit to go out there and like perform for your team. I mean, it's no excuse to why, you know, mean once you get on that field, there's no excuse to, oh, my knee or this and that. You on that field. Hey, attack each play with intent to get better. You know what I mean? That's just how I look at it. Yeah. >> You had tight coverage against George Pickins. He caught that really tight touchdown the other day. How thin is the margin going against George and CD between like a touchdown and a pass breakup. >> Uh shoot. Well, I wish I could answer that question, but hey, just just be locked in. Be locked in cuz them them guys is no joke. Seriously, it's just one slip up and y'all seen it. Just to stay focused, you know what I mean? >> You have to have a short memory. Clearly today with CD, you had a couple of good players on the sideline. Just talk about that. And you talk about iron shot and iron and they making you better. >> Yeah. I mean, going against these guys, you see how they move, you know what I mean? You go back, watch film, come back out here, you know, get a little fail at first first couple of plays, you know, you try to learn that player. At the end of the day, you know, how I look at it, I just compete, man. I just I don't I don't think I don't overthink. I don't think too much, you know. I just go out there, do what I do what I can do. I know my skill. I know my abilities, so when I go against them guys, I know it's iron sharp iron. >> When Pickkins made that touchdown catch, obviously it was really tight coverage. Great catch by him. When you watch film of that, how do you say like, okay, how do I improve or how do I stop that next time? How did you how did you kind of watch film about that play? >> I was just kind of I was being a little too aggressive, you know what I mean? Sometimes my arms and my hands get me in trouble because, you know, I also got long arms and I kind of push myself away from them. You know what I mean? At the end of the day, he used me against myself and that's what he did. And Dak knew I was tall and I have I was length lengthy. So, he threw a ball short and I just just played it today. I was like, okay, let's approach it differently. >> That's some next level stuff, right? >> Definitely. >> Talking to your confidence, you uh you broke out the finger wag today. That's the kind of great day that you had at practice today. Just talk about just physically and and mentally. Do you feel like you're close to being back to, you know, quote unquote ECU Savone? Like where are you? >> Most definitely. Definitely feel like I'm getting close to my ECU self. And I say that every single day. I watch film myself every single day. I do go back and watch my ECU film [laughter] and see what I what I used to do. You know what I mean? There's a few errors. I was always I wasn't always perfect back then. So, I take that, you know, kind of give myself some confidence when I come into practice to prove to who who I used to be. You know what I mean? I take that. Okay, let's let's lock in. You know what I mean? I know who we going against each day. >> How different is Christian Parker and what are the differences, >> man? The intentionality, bro. Like the way he wants to come out here and perform, you know? He tell me every day, you know what I mean? Use your abilities, use your skills, man. You 1% out of the league, man. You lengthy, you fast, got long arms, you strong, you know what I mean? I And I take it's me. It's my responsibility to like be there for myself and believe in myself at the end of the day because I have the coaches that believe in me. So I also got to believe in myself. So that's exactly what he do for me. >> How young he is, does he bring more of a player mentality than maybe >> Oh yeah, he definitely brings. >> I mean he he's very intentional with what he do, you know what I mean? Coaching wise and also like he know his players. He know what you can do. I mean you feel down on yourself, he'll pick you back up, you know? I mean, hey, next play, next play. Error is going to come. I mean also like as an offense, you know, drop a ball, see drop a ball, next play as in corner, you know what I mean? You gonna give you give up a couple passes, but next play short memory. >> How critical are you of your own game? >> How crit? Hey, I'm most confident in myself to anybody else, man. I just, you know, I mean, be there. You got to be available for yourself each day. I mean, you can't move how everybody else want you to move. You also just got to have that short memory and approach each day like you want to get better. You know what I mean? Ain't no excuse to to having a bad day. You going to have bad days the next day. You just got to approach it differently. Don't look back in the past cuz that's going to also mess up, you know, your head. You don't want that to mess up your mental. But so I just move forward, man. >> Shotty Shotti's talked about your man coverage ability being elite and he said, "But we want to get him also the zone coverage to be kind of on the same level." How has the learning process been for the zone coverage aspect of things with >> I'm in I've been in there with Yeah. CP, um, DA, Smitty, they all, you know, coaching me up with the with the zone coverage cuz I wasn't always perfect in that part of of the game. I mean, I'm starting to catch up with that as you can see. You know what I mean? I've been progressing each each week. Even during OTAAS, I progress each week and trying to understand the formations and the um what they trying to run and stuff like that. So, yeah. >> In those instances where CP is needed elsewhere that you getting the same message, same juice from DA and from Ryan Smith. >> Yeah, I mean, everybody got their own say so and things, you know what I mean? DA, you know, the quarterback coach, Smitty, safety coach, and we all in the same room. You know, I mean, CP runs the whole thing. But, you know, you dealt with DA, you dealt with Smitty, and they they they know what you got. You know what I mean? I had a visit with DA when he was at Green Bay. I had a visit with Schmidy when he was at the Cardinals. So, they they seen what they had in me. They they for me, you know what I mean? When I have my head down, you know, everybody had their ups and downs, but no, >> how I look at it, man, each coach has like come they come together as one. I mean, they going to tell you this, this, this, and that, but put it together, you're going to be a great player. >> Did they bring that up? The fact that, hey, we couldn't get you in the draft when we were in Arizona and Green Bay, but now we got you here. >> Maybe. I don't remember, but if they did, I don't know. I don't know what to say. I'm with the Cowboys now, so [laughter] it >> all worked out then. >> Yeah, definitely. >> Thanks. >> I appreciate y'all.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: “We Have to Go Out and Do It” | Press Conference
text: might be. I don't know. I don't know. See where Calvin wants to go with this thing. I'm just saying. >> Calvin Todd Archer. >> Calvin Watkins, Dallas Morning News. Your thoughts today? What you want to see in your team the first day at pass? >> Um, you know, I want to see physical play. I want to see pad level. Uh, I want to see us work together. still stay off the ground. Um, you know, this is still a ramp up mentality. It's our first time in pads. You know, it's a review day. The way we do it, it Calvin is, you know, first three days the installs were in, but you know, there's no mistaking why you would do a review day the first day of pads because you don't want any guys going the wrong way, bumping into each other, stuff like that. So, uh, the normal play style that we're looking for, but really the competition piece, playing to the edge without going over the edge. to say we go hour and a half, two hours, that kind of thing. >> It's hour 45 today with an hour 45 max. Yep. >> Healthwise, what where you stand? Thompson back. >> Uh, no. Uh, PJ Lock should be close to getting back. JT's doing great. Uh, Zion's going to probably be a little bit longer. Um, but again, all three of those guys are working really, really hard. >> Clam DLS Cowboys, couple questions. Um, what what's the message? I mean, obviously there's no tackling. But how do you want them performing at pads? >> Yeah, again I think you know we want to get our pads down. We want to be able to strike. Uh there's things that you teach, you know, in terms of we're a leverage tackling team. So the way you work and get your leverage. The difference is from going from a tag off thing, you know, Clarence, now we're actually going to wrap. We call it wrap and release. So you get down low, you strike, you wrap your arms, and then you release. Because if you don't have the ball carrier running, you can't get the conditioning and training the pursuit angles and things like that. But um yeah, the guys working together. You know, the big thing we say is, hey, stay off the ground, protect your teammates, but but play with great pad level and urgency. >> Not just studing up, studing and wrapping. >> It's going to be a little bit more of a wrap. Yep. >> And will you do any Last week was a lot of team work where you do any pass rush drills, one-on-one drills, any of that sort of stuff. >> That's coming tomorrow. Yep. That's coming tomorrow. So, today again, first day in pads, you want to get these guys used to carrying their pads. You know, they're all probably making sure they they fit right and things like that. But uh uh tomorrow we'll get into some of that. >> Brian Todd Arth with ESPN. >> Welcome back. >> Thank you. Appreciate it. Um there's a lot of talk about Gotti greatest offense there is and things like that. What in your mind? What has to happen for that to become a reality? >> One, we got to evolve. I mean, we have to change the things that we didn't like last year that we didn't do very well. We got to find ways to complement the things that we did well. Uh we need, you know, a couple more guys to continue to step up. You know, not name Pickins and Lamb. And that's the floor noise of the world. It's some young tight ends, Jaden Blue, things like that. And then, you know, I've been very open and honest. I really do believe that this offense is going to be driven by our offensive line, our ability to move people, our ability to knock people back in the run game, our ability to pass protect. I think that's incredibly critical, and we've got a few position battles going there. So, um, I love it. I love the confidence. Um, but, uh, we have to go out and do it. How do you go about anticipating what opposing defenses might try and do? Is that an offseason study for your guys? You're like, "All right, they this what they did this now. They've seen this. They have a book a little bit. You got to anticipate." >> Yeah. I mean, what you do is you study. I mean, we all do it. There's no secret. All 32 of us look at, "Okay, who are the great offenses? Who are the great defenses?" You study them. Everybody does it and everybody's got their plans of, okay, hey, here's how we want to play the Cowboys, here's how we want to attack, you know, the Eagles, whatever. um you look at people that have had success against them, you know, and so um you know, we do it, we know teams do it to us, and that's why we're constantly looking at ways of evolving. And part of the way to evolve is to have great marriage with your runs and passes on offense. And the disguise element on defense is a huge part of that in terms of keeping the offense guessing. >> Jeez, getting them all in. >> He's back. >> Red zone. Um last year you were 16th in the league in touchdown percentage. Do you do more in practice than you get up to speed? How do you address the red zone? >> Yeah, it was a big empis for us in the offseason. Um we did a bunch in phase one and phase two. We really did a deep study into it. We spent more time on it. The guys have been doing some of that. They did that out in Park City, more of the red zone throws. Um you know, we know where we came up short. A lot of it was things that we hurt ourselves with, you know, penalties and self-inflicted wounds down there. Uh, but, you know, we're too good to be kicking the field goals that we were kicking. And I think that's part of the Gotti, you know. I mean, if we're going to truly be that, then we have to score touchdowns in the red zone. >> Scott Michet uh making that roster move, adding Gutierrez and moving on from Snowden. Can you just take us behind that? Yeah, >> you know, um again, the end of the day, um you know, Charles, um injury going to be out a while. Uh and um so we decided to get another guy in here that can come and work and I thought Charles is great and uh you know, we'll we'll see how things play out, but it's really this time of year going into pads, you need as many healthy bodies as you can get. And um you know, so we're excited to see how Sebastian does. >> And uh it looked like Tyler Gayton got some work, the second team at at right tackle. What did you think of that? What's the thought process? Yeah, actually you guys are wrong. Whoever reported that is wrong. And don't worry, I make mistakes all the time. Uh but he was playing jumbo tight end. So, uh when the twos are up, we try not to move the the tackles around. So, we played him on the right. He was on the right, but he was playing tight end. So, um again, just things we're trying to trying out with. Did you report it? Was it you? Dang it. No. Literally, I make mistakes all the time, so it's no big deal. >> Yeah. >> Until I see it. I told the I told the O line the other day, especially Terrence Steel, I said, "Uh, hey, Kell Moore is a way cooler coordinator than you, Clayton. He throws the ball to the tackles." Terrence Steel's like, "Yeah." So, but uh guy catch probably he's a pretty good athlete. >> Catch in college. >> Did he? Okay. I'll tell I'll tell Kellen and Clayton. >> Harris for Star Telegram. Uh these young safeties obviously getting a lot more opportunities with the injuries. What have you seen from these guys and specifically Caleb Downs getting some work out deep as well? Yeah, you know, I mean, that's what the the one, you know, positive that you get when you get guys that are slowed by injuries is you get to, you know, find out some of your young players. Uh, big shout out to Julius Wood. You know, he and Elijah Clark have been flying around, you know, in this defense. The ability to come out of the shell the second half of the defense and fit the B gap, I think, is really, really important. Those guys are showing a quick, you know, quick trigger and getting up there and getting set fast. Um, shout out to Ready Stewart. I mean, he got moved to safety the other day and um you know, that's the versatility he gives you. You know, here's a guy that's really a nickel, but he's going back there and playing uh there. But um what I really do like is also the guys that have been out. I mean, you watch him in practice. They're watching, they're communicating, they're coaching, and that's part of the deal as well. But uh it's a deep position for us. Maris Bell, you he's played a lot of great football for us. Um and uh you know, we feel really really fortunate to have that type of depth at that position. going back and watching the film from these first three days. Is there a specific one-on-one battle that's been really fun for you guys to watch and that you're excited to see in pass? >> Um, there's been a lot. Uh, it's been fun for me, maybe not Bibbs, uh, Cooper going against Kenny and Quinnon every time, but, uh, I would pay money to watch Quinnon Williams and Tyler Smith play football. Uh, if it's just the two of them on a field, you know, run blocking, pass blocking, uh, I would I would I would pay admission for that. So, uh, but really all of them, you know, it's been fun to watch CD and George go up against, you know, Kobe Durant and Bon and and, you know, uh, Kalin. So, a lot of match ups that we look forward to seeing. >> Tommy Rish Dallas Cowboys.com. Brian kind of mentioned it a little bit, but offensive defensive line when you put the pads on, it's very different. What's telling for you when you watch them with them on versus when they're not on? >> Yeah, again, I think the biggest thing is just the pad level. you know, the ability to sustain blocks, combinations get a little bit, you know, thinner because linebackers are coming downhill. And um when you put pads on, Tommy, you want to make sure you keep your fundamentals. You can't just, you know, start flopping around and and going and losing technique because at the end of the day, it's going to be the technique that allows you to get your pads down, get your feet in the ground, lift your, you know, lift the opponent up by getting with your pad level and hit with a 6- in rising blow. So, I want to see these guys still continue to use their fundamentals even though the pads are on. The pads just really give you a chance to um you know, be a little bit more physical and uh and and we've been really big this off season and even early in camp using our hands. You'll see more shoulder blocks and things like that today, but uh the thing we're trying to prevent is side shots. You know, we don't want any side shots because it usually puts guys on the ground and uh we don't want that. >> You said last year at this time that Sam Williams was barking when you told him the pads were coming on. Is there a player you've seen? >> There's not been any barking yet. They might be waiting for you guys to be out there, but uh >> is there someone you're excited to see in specifically? >> Uh I think all the guys I I love this day. Uh but it's the first step of a long journey and uh you know, it's uh it's going to be a fun practice. Like I said, it's uh going to be um two scripted periods and then two competitive periods uh where we let the coordinators call it. You know, I'm just going to be the head coach and let CP and Clayton call it. and you'll see the threes get some more work today. I think that's important. Get those guys some some reps. They'll be playing, you know, real football here in in uh couple two weeks or whatever. Uh so it should be a fun day. >> Joe Hoy, Dallas Morning News. Um Malachi Lawrence made it a big emphasis during mini camp to work on his fall stepping to make sure he was going forward first. Seems like that's still a little bit out there with him. How hard is it to break just kind of the, you know, muscle memory of a fall step and how has he been progressing? >> It is. It's very hard. You know, we have some receivers that are elite and they still fall step. You know, uh have a few other, you know, skilled players on offense that again, you would love them to eliminate the false step. Um but when you're a pass rusher and every inch counts, I think it's really important, but he works tirelessly at it. He actually had a rush the other day, uh I think it was against T Steel where it was an edge rush. T Steel had a really good set and he had a sweet hand swipe where he beat T Steel inside and that was one of the things that I'm excited to see Malachi but it was a really cool counter. You know part of pass rushing is you know your initial move but what's your counter and what's your toolbox that you use to to defeat the blocker and um he's learning all those from Chedera and uh and BT >> extra conditioning. Uh Tyler Gen was talking about how when you're that tired and you have to run again it almost makes your mind lock in a little bit more. or it helps with the end of game and keeping your fundamentals for a guy like that specifically and just in general. How much does that help with the discipline, late game discipline and the extra condition? >> Yeah, you know, I think it's important. I think it's good when the players are saying that. I think they understand. You know, my big thing from them is I wanted them from the very beginning to understand that it was not punishment. This was the plan all along. We're going to, you know, plan on doing some running today. Everything we do though is based off of the science and the catapult numbers and things like that. we know exactly what type of practice output we want to have today and um there'll [clears throat] be times that they reach that output and I might take conditioning off or I might add conditioning based on the numbers and um it's all done for a purpose and it's something that we studied uh at length uh during the offseason to give us an advantage going into not just the start of the season but the latter part of the season and into the playoffs. Joe Treyan. >> Joe Trean, WFAA TV. Coach, while this is the first step of the long journey, as you mentioned, it's also, by my count, one of only 10 fully padded practices, including uh the working with the Rams and the Saints. What's the message to your team about the urgency that they need to work with as well? >> Yeah, I mean, maximize it for sure, Joe. I mean, that's that's really important. But again, I think you I use the word here a lot. Some of it's mandated by the league, some of it's mandated by us as a staff, but like the ramp up, you know, why do you not do one-on- ones today? Well, they're just getting to kind of feel for their pads. Um, but we'll have a few more two twohour practices, the joints against, you know, uh, you know, the Rams and Saints will be really important for us, but today is just one step. And again, these guys put these pads on, they don't think twice about it. I mean, they've been doing this since they were 5 years old, six years old. You know, they look forward to it. And uh you know it'll be our our job to uh like I said make sure they're playing to the edge without going over the the edge. >> Is there anything you have to reaffirm with some of the younger players on this day? >> They're actually the ones that you you do keep an eye on. You got to communicate more too just because they're excited and you know they they they're looking for their ops whereas the vets kind of know how to practice but uh I do think we do a good job of explaining the tempo, what's expected. Um, for example, when your linebackers and running backs are in a blitz pickup situation, you know, the linebackers want to beat the backs, the backs want to beat the the running backs, but they also have to have some awareness. There's a three-y halo around the quarterbacks. That's why they have red jerseys on. So, it's not just uh, you know, do whatever you want out there. You got to work together with your teammates, and um, the time will come for us to be able to do that, whether that's one-on- ones or in, you know, competitive preseason games. Uh, hey coach Nicole just in Dallascowboys.com. This is year three for Maris Le foul. He's kind of been under three different DCs. What did you kind of notice from him and how has he taken on the different changes? >> Yeah, I I I love Maris versatility. You know, unfortunately for Maris, I mean, that is what it is, you know. And what spot are you playing? Well, you're a linebacker. I know you're on the ball. We know he knows how to take away the ball. We know he's physical. We know he's got great length. I actually think that his versatility to play on and off the ball will be a huge, you know, uh, advantage for us. And, um, again, you never have to worry about his wiring and the play style. And, um, you know, it takes guys, you know, a couple years. And then you factor into what you said about the different coordinators and changes and position changes and, uh, but he's done a really good job with his weight and, you know, managing that and, um, you know, he, uh, continues to thrive on special teams. So, he's a guy that we're thrilled to see take the next step in this system. >> Mike Ducey, Fox 4. I know you've been around long enough to remember where when there were not the restrictions on padded practices the way there are now, and it is what it is. I understand. But how much more challenging does it make it as a coach and a coaching staff to evaluate your team and your players with these restrictions in place? >> You know, D, I actually kind of like it. I I I really do. I mean, I think you have to be more organized. I think you have to do a really good job of of explaining to the guys what you want. I mean, if you would let my dad practice four times a day, he would have probably did. Uh self-report. [snorts] Love you, Pops. Uh but uh Dick Vermile was that way. Coach Vermile text me the other day and I remembering, you know, three of days in St. Louis, whether it was legal or not, I was just a QC running to get water for people and running cards and things like that. But I remember three. So, um I I think at the end of the day now we can get the work done, but you got to be organized. These guys have to understand what's expected. And uh I I like the rules. Cindy Steel, D210 Sports. So, when you look at position groups, do you think it's more important for some over others to evaluate them with the pads on? >> Uh, yeah. I mean, probably honestly, like, you know, I'm not evaluating the quarterbacks and pads. Uh, whereas offensive defensive line as you are evaluating them a little bit more. Uh, we've talked about the edge rushers versus the tackles. We've talked about the matchups inside. Um, but I do think Sydney that there's a point where these guys do still have to work together uh to get done what we want to get done. The fans, since you opened the door to talking about preseason playing time. >> Why did I figure you would take that, Brad? Yeah. >> I don't write them. I just read >> Okay. Yeah. Uh, but you got to have your depth chart. I get it. You got to be able to speak about this stuff. >> How do you as a staff balance rookies who you think are going to be starters who you don't want to overexpose but have to play some? And in that group, um, that tells us whether they're playing zero snaps in the preseason, whether they're playing 10 to 15 snaps in the preseason. Um, you know, 25 to 35 for the B minus and kind of unlimited for the C's. Um, I have a list in my mind, the the coaches get with the coordinators and they debate those things. Um, you know, Caleb DS for example, you know, do you play him, do you not play him? We're having those discussions and um good news is we don't have to make those decisions for a while, but there's something to the young guys playing a little bit and you know, we do it in the first two games. I think that's part of it. You know, usually don't play many of those guys in the third preseason game, but uh it's something that, you know, we're we're very serious about. >> Coach Charles Robinson from Front Office Sports. Um once you put the pads on, how long does it take to tangibly really understand where the roster deficits are? Charles, that's that's a good question. I I think it's different every year. I think, you know, we have an idea right now of where we feel we're strong and maybe where we feel like we've got great depth and then, hey, we're a little thin here. Um, but I would say it's after that second preseason game. I mean, we got to see these guys play real football and even out here, it's the closest thing that we can do to real football, but like we're not tackling, taking guys to the ground and stuff like that. So, I think you got to probably get through the two joints, the two preseason games. Once we break camp, head back to to uh, you know, the star after the Arizona game. Yeah, I mean I think you know you mentioned a couple names, Mike, but again you know I like a lot of things from really a lot of the guys. I think you know Demo's doing an awesome job. Uh green dot not you know I can spin you know Clarence around with that conversation for the next 20 minutes if we want. Who's the green dot? Who's not? But um you know Dwinners the speed shows up on film for sure. J Sean's been really really good. Uh Shamar James uh is standing out and then you know there's some other guys. I mean, you know, Justin Baron's doing awesome. Curtis Robinson, you know, he's a a guy we brought in that we're really excited about. And uh Vet and then uh Langston Patterson as well. >> All righty. >> Thanks, guys.

Yeah. No, it's the biggest um I I think I've said this multiple times. Uh I don't take anything for granted and I don't take those matchups for granted because not everyone's able to go against someone like that in practice. Every day, day in and day out, just battling. So once we get all those those two things down I think everything else will follow nicely. >> Dan has kind of also talked about potentially playing some starters in the preseason. Do you think because there's so many moving parts on the offensive line that's something that that would help you guys? >> N I mean whatever Dan says, I think it'll help us. So if we go, we go. If we don't, we don't. So >> Well, obviously this a kind of a system that's been in place for a number of years. Jared's pretty familiar where they come in. So, >> how much easier does that make your job, you know, just with a guy a veteran guy like who's >> Yeah. Yeah. It makes my job easy. Um you know, we got a we got a good team here. >> Besides the vocal communication, are you starting to like notice some of the stuff that you you don't say out loud that you like you notice Tate's over here doing this? title: Kelvin Sheppard Press Conference | 2026 Training Camp Day 4
text: I wanted to ask you about two of your young uh defensive linemen, uh Hassan and and Moore. Uh we see Moore out there yesterday having some some pretty good success as a pass rusher. Uh just kind of your early impressions of him. And then Hassan, you you >> changed his role a little bit. Uh that the effort that he put in to to get ready for that and kind of your early impressions on how he's handling that transition. >> Yep. Well, first I'll start kind of summarizing for both of them. I don't want to jump the gun because they play defensive line and we've yet to have a um a padded practice yet. So, I don't want to get too high, too low on anybody, especially the front seven guys. Uh but dating back to the spring, ever since we drafted and acquired Derek Moore since the day he showed up, he just has the presence of an older guy. Just being around him, he doesn't feel like a rookie. You know, I kind of say that to the staff all the time. He's very mature. He's kind of introverted, but once you get to know him, he's just a man's man. And he just comes to work every day with his head down. Coach, what do you need of me? What are you expecting of me? What is the standard? And he goes out and tries to meet that. Uh he's shown things. Absolutely. Um the thing that I've seen more here in person that I keep saying has kind of jumped off to me that didn't jump off so much on the tape is his athleticism. And I think you don't see it as much on tape because he plays like this hard no style um speed to power rush, but when you get around him, he has very uh good um efficient movement. Um he covers a lot of ground, no wasted steps and things like that. Things is going to transition we feel like to this level um of play. And then transitioning, talking about our med, man, I absolutely love that guy. Like I told you guys before last year, um we took our med on and you all know our med only knows one way and that's full tilt and sometimes the offense doesn't like that especially when we don't have on pass, but they appreciate it because they know it's real. It's not fake. It's not phony. It's not fabricated. Energy is real. Um, and we did we kind of switched his role a little bit and I think it's been to his advantage um to more of the bigger end type position um and seeing what he could provide for us there as far as potentially starter depth player or whatever that may come from. But like I said, the real tale on those guys that come starting tomorrow's practice when we add the pads. >> What uh what sort of growth did you see from Jimmy Roler from when you got him until, you know, Friday and then the injury? How much does that set him back? Yeah. not, you know, for however long he's going to be out there. >> Absolutely. I mean, Jimmy, I mean, the trajectory was clear and you saw it. Came in in the spring like anybody, a veteran linebacker we acquire. Uh, where we've took this system now with the with with the adjustments, the checks, the things like that, especially at the linebacker position. It's a lot. So, he came in in the spring, he's like, whoa. Kind of, you know, that. But as soon as he showed up day one, you saw two things. He put work in this summer. He applied himself and then he's trusting the coaching. What's what Ham's asking him to do is a tick different than things that he did at Michigan and he's met that challenge and and I tell you that that kid was getting better every day each and every day. Um hopefully, you know, we have a tremendous athletic training room staff in there and they'll try to get them back to speed as far as return to play as soon as possible. >> Still contribute at some point this year. >> Oh, absolutely. Absolutely. as far as the mental and all that, he'll still be engaged in meetings and all that with us. So, I absolutely see him contributing at some point. >> You haven't seen Devin yet, obviously, but just when you add a guy with that much experience, but a guy [clears throat] that had 174 tackles, you know, last year's won a Super Bowl, just what might that mean to to the room adding a veteran presence like that? >> Uh, it just backs up everything Dan spoke of this off season that we are going to find the best 90 to come in here and compete. It's all about competition. uh if we have the chance to acquire somebody that we feel like can come in whether that's push to start or push guys in the room to make them, you know, that the urgency is real this year. It's not just lip service. Uh and that's what we've did. Uh the front office and Dan do a great job going out and it's non-stop. It's always evolving. How can we get better? How can we improve? And like I said, it's not just, oh, go out and get this flash guy. know how can we improve the competitive depth situation right now as far as training camp is concerned and Devin definitely does that with his championship pedigree. >> It's always good to add an LSU linebacker to the room, right? >> Absolutely. >> Chev, I think um Hutch led all NFL defensive ends last year in snaps, the only one to play over a thousand. Obviously, you want your best players out there as much as possible, but some fresh legs on the edge and and more and and want them. Could it benefit Hutch to get a few extra breathers per game this year over the course of the season or do you want to see him still playing that huge line? >> Like I said, you guys come down on game day and try to tell him he's off the field. Uh but I mean you appreciate it. But yeah, like with all jokes aside, seriously, absolutely. like the wear and tear the duration of a season talking 21 22 weeks you try to push to February 14th asking a guy to go out and play 90% 95 percentile at that position where it's shock and shed every play his hands people leaning on him every play so obviously we'll like to find the spots the right spots where we feel and like I said the front office tremendous job making sure when we want to do that there's no drop off where you go from hutch and now it's like oh I can't call this. I can't do this. Now you have a veteran like DJ won. Let's go. And he's not batting eye. You got a guy like Derek Moore. Let's go. He's not batting eye. Uh guy like PT, he's not batting eye. So, you know, it goes on and on and on and on now to where Hutch doesn't feel like I got to carry this load. I got to do this. All right, I'm tired. Let me tap my head and let my brother come get some. >> I think for years we we've uh you know, talked about pass rush. Did you have enough? You know, did you guys do enough? Whatever. this year the the concern from the outside at least seems to be on the secondary. What level of concern if any do you have right now about you know health at safety depth at quarterback those those sort of >> again we've brought in a good group we feel of veteran players who done it before. That's the thing that I think is the biggest difference this year is that say we go into this season, we go into this thing with the room as it sits right now, Chuck Clark, Avante Maddox, even Thomas Harper, these guys have time on task in the NFL with NFL snaps. They've seen these formations. They've done it. And then they can also there's there's a lot of young guys in the room that could lean on these guys. So, I just love the way the room's set up right now. the way it's structured and we've built a system. We feel like that's adaptable and that it's not just, oh, you have to have this player to run this play. We're trying to build this thing to where it's just plug and play as we go. And that's what this has allowed us and allotted us. Not that we don't want to have these guys in there, but not having them in the spring, we knew what we needed to attack right right then and there. So, we're able to go into training camp with the mentality as far as midseason trying to bring guys in, get them caught up to speed. They've been with us all spring now. >> Cornerback. Was that a setback losing Terion? How big a setback was that? >> Listen, I'm I'm not going to say it was a setback, so to say, because to me, honestly, that's disrespectful to the guys that's still in this locker room. What I'll say is Terry Noral had number one quarterback potential, but it was still untapped. You know what I mean? And that's and I kind of leave that at that. >> Big camp for Andis, you know, he's he's gained a little bit of weight, looks a little bit bigger. Just what have you seen from him early on? I know without pads, but do you like where kind of he's training? Obviously, you know, he's got a chance, a big opportunity to to to earn a role here. >> Absolutely, Tim. And I'll say with Inis, the talent was all was always there, but you just hit it as far as getting his body ready to take on and endure what he's about to have to endure this year. Again, the stretch of 21 22 weeks. And then mentally, that's where I think you guys going to see him take the biggest jump. understanding, recognizing formations. What do we need him to do on this call? Not just going out thinking, I got this guy, I got my man. No, learn to play with leverage. Understand where the safeties at. Understand where your help is. That's where I've seen the biggest jump within it so far as we've started off in camp. >> What are some of the core basics you're looking for when the pads go on to know that a guy might be for real to maybe what you've seen the last five days is going to continue on? Like what are those core? >> Well, it flashed it on the board. It's a quote I got from the late great Kevin Green by way of Dom Capers. We're going to establish the violent physical nature of the game. And and and that's non-negotiable. That's literally non-negotiable. So guys are going to go in and they've already been told we will get back to playing elite run defense here and it starts with the front seven. It starts when the pads come on and it starts there. So if you can't do that, it's it's called earning the right to rush the passer, the flash and all that. Yes, a time and place, but the brunt of a game, the bulk of a game is played within the trenches on first and second down, early downs and earning them right. >> Watching Chuck Clark last year with the Steelers, you know, you saw I came away impressed with pre- snap him playing too high and then post [clears throat] snap buzzing down, getting that curl hook area. What are some of the things on the field you hope to utilize with Clark and Maddox and Izzian and Harper? What are some of the strength they display? That's literally what I was just speaking upon as far as bringing in veteran guys who understand what we're looking for as far as disguising. That's where we're trying to get to now as a defense. I told him it's time to go to the next level, guys. The quarterbacks in this league is too good now. So, it's all about lying to him. You got to be liars on defense. You got a lot of that guy with the green dot on offense. Pre- snap, he has to see something and then post snap, that picture has to change or else you're a sitting duck. And these guys have done these things. They understand the why behind it because you take these young pups, you get them in here, we want to disguise. It's no rhyme or reason why guy down on the edge and he's supposed to have the post. Well, how you going to get your job done? So these guys understand not only let's disguise but why I'm disguising where can I cheat to? Where can I lean to? So the neck up I think we've taken a step as far as the DB room and the secondary rooms is concerned. Christian >> with with Christianizian Shep. Um, obviously he had to start on NFI with this bug he he contracted, but Dan said you were hoping to come into camp getting him some some look at Nickel. And I'm just curious as you're >> you've got a lot of versatile guys back there, right? Like they can do a lot of different things. How much are you still kind of putting together the the puzzle in your mind of best fits and when do you kind of maybe need to I want to say lock in because the versatility remains but really come together with the plan of what you want the the fits to be for your defense. >> Absolutely. Just I mean the faster we could figure out those 11. I mean that's the best for everybody. But we're going to let this competition ride as long as it need to. We're not going to force we're not going to force anything. I told them we got a lot of new guys. It's all about progression learning and conceptual learning. And that's that's when it comes to chess pieces. Now you're out there. All right, Izzy, you got to know safety and nickel. All right, Devonte, you got to know safety, nickel, dime, corner. And it's just a matter of how much can a guy take on. And then understanding we get in game. You might see him one play at nickel. You might see him one play at safety. You might see him one play at corner. But this is all things that Izzy did in Tampa. just going back and I did my due diligence, studying, talking to people that's coached him, been close to him, understanding how to utilize this player, where where where does he thrive, where does he want to play, having conversations with him, and then him understanding my vision for him and him meeting me halfway. So, it'll be great getting him back out there today, taking these reps, seeing what's the truly best fit for him in our system. But, it's definitely a place for Izzy. >> Last one day, last one day we got to go. >> You said uh get back to playing elite run defense. That's a big thing. You guys were still top half of the NFL last year. So, how do you how do you assess what you guys did on run defense and beyond just that mentality, why do you think you're better equipped to, you know, be a top five run defensive team or whatever you want to be?
