title: Head coach Shane Steichen on first day of padded practice
text: What's up guys? Good to see you. Obviously first day in pads today. I thought it went really well. A lot of physicality. Good back and forth. You know, defense made some plays, offense made some plays, but it's good to get get out here in pads. Banging around a little bit. We go from there. So whenever you're ready. >> How does the energy shift once you put on these pads? >> Yeah, a lot. A big time. I think the guys feel that when you come out here with the pads on. Obviously it's a lot more physical. Obviously we're taking care of each other too at the same time. It's a long season, but we got to be physical at the point of attack and I thought the guys brought that today. >> Anthony and Riley had been rotating pretty evenly for most of the week, but Saturday it felt like Riley got quite a bit more action than >> Yeah, I think I think that was just the way the reps played out. We had a little long drive drill there and he got that long drive drill which got more of the reps. Obviously if they would have rotated the other day that would have been Anthony's reps. So we just rotate those guys. >> Going back on Friday, we saw Anthony bobble a handful of snaps in that one practice. What did you Was there anything to that from him or from the center or what was >> Yeah, I think that's just concentration. You know, just getting the snaps, seeing it in and go from there. >> What are your impressions early on in the kicking competition? Is there anything that went into Spencer or Chase today? >> Yeah, we're going to rotate those guys in kicking, but that's that's going to be a good battle for sure. Both those guys are starting kickers in this league, so that'll be very interesting to see how that plays out cuz I love both those guys. >> Shaq, we've seen work come out and he's getting some work in. >> Yeah. >> What does he mean to this defense? >> He means everything to this defense. He's been a pillar here for so long. 10 year plus vet. He leads the right way, works the right way. To so to see him out there and get some reps is huge and obviously that's an ongoing conversation that he'll have with you know, myself and the trainers and just make sure his body's right and whatever he needs to get from a team standpoint he'll get throughout training camp. >> Can you say what Hunter's dealing with? >> He's got a hamstring right now, so yeah. >> What have you seen from McGowan? He looks like he's got some power there. >> Yeah, there's no doubt. It's good to just get the pads on with him. We were excited to see him in pads. I think he brings a lot of physicality you know, to the football field and so we're really excited about that. He's a downhill runner. When I watched his tape at Kentucky, uh the physicality he ran with, you know, when he gets hit at the line of scrimmage, he usually falls forward for a couple extra yards, which is huge. Um you know, in short-yardage situations or just in the middle of the game, uh it's big. So, good to see his growth and, you know, see how training camp plays out for him. >> Is there a little Zach Moss to his game with Is this where he kind of cuts? >> Yeah, I think that's a fair assessment. Um yeah, he he's got some good stretch-cut stuff ability to him. Um and again, he's not scared of contact, which is awesome at the running back position. You need that physicality um at that position. He brings that. He's been good. Obviously, that's a work in progress. Um we'll keep working through that. Um as many touches as we can get those backs out of the backfield, you know, in team situations, even seven-on-seven, routes on air, it doesn't matter, you know, I think you just keep working through that uh and see where it goes, but um excited about all those guys. Yeah, I think there's a good competition going on, especially for that third spot with Duellin and Westbrook and Tread, you know, both those guys are battling like crazy, um but they're pulling for each other, too, which is awesome to see. That's that team, you know, not me mentality, and uh it's good to see that. It'll be interesting to see how that all plays out. >> They match up obviously against a really tough DB squad with Mooney and Sauce. Um I know um you guys know that you'll get Pierce back eventually. Does that make it even a little bit tougher when they're going up against some of the best cornerbacks in the league when they're also trying to >> No, I think that's great. When you can go up against two of the best in the league uh in practice every day, it's going to make everybody better. So, you know, to have those two guys out there, um tight coverage, you know, every single play, especially when it's man coverage, um it's going to make those guys better. >> So, do you have any better sense on on Pierce's timeline? >> I don't. I know that he's working. He's heading in the right direction, for sure. Um so, I feel really good about that um moving forward. >> Obviously, Daniel's not taking any hits, but first day in pads for him, as well. How how'd you like what you saw the whole team in pads and how it went? >> Yeah, good. I think he's been doing a great job. He's progressing every day, um making plays, getting us in and out of the right play, which is huge, Completing passes, moving the offense down the field, making good decisions. Um and so we just got to continue that through camp. >> Uh Nadi has been missing the last couple of days of practice. What's he dealing with? >> Uh he's got a toe right now. >> Shame with this tight end group. Seems like you got guys who do a lot of things. Tyler does everything. But do you like the makeup of this group? >> I do. I think uh obviously, you know, Tree and Mo are really good blockers for us um that we can use in the pass game as well. Obviously, Tyler's a guy that can do it all. Um and so I think there's some versatility there with that and how we use those guys. And that's up as up to us as coaches to put those guys in position to be successful. So, we work that, you know, through camp on how we use those guys and obviously throughout the season. >> What about Mo? I mean, he's still here. You just He just feels like he can't be without him. >> And there's no doubt. Obviously, every year, you know, Mo, you know, maybe a one-year contract, whatever it is over the past couple of years, but he's a guy that's just reliable. He's consistent. He does everything right. Um and we love him on this football team. >> You guys have rotated through like six or one backers in one of the first couple of days of camp. What um are you guys looking for in that battle? And is there anyone that stood out to you? >> Yeah, I think that's an ongoing battle with all those guys. You know, we're doing a great job. Lou's doing a great job. Batcher's doing a great job of rotating those guys. The communication piece of it's going to be huge and then making plays inside the box, you know, making tackles, being great in coverage. Um and that's a process that we're going through and I'm looking forward to seeing that competition throughout camp. >> Without Hunter out on the field today, it seemed like AJ kind of slid in and took over his first reps. What did you see out of him today? >> Um you know, I thought he made some good plays. I thought he was in position a lot of plays. You know, he's a smart guy for a young guy. I think he's got really good instincts. You know, he's always around the ball and you need that at that position. So, it's going to be good to see his growth throughout training camp and obviously throughout the season as well. >> I know Mark Westbrook-Keenan and those guys that you are challenging for that wide right receiver three spot has gotten the most reps over the last couple of seasons. He's had a couple of good plays, especially late last week. Has he stood out to you or what have you noticed from him so far? >> Yeah, I think he's made some big plays for us. Obviously, guy, you know, when he was at Tennessee two years ago, you know, I think he had I don't I want to say seven or eight touchdowns. So, he's made some plays in this league. A veteran guy that can play special teams as well. So, really excited about him. And uh like I said, we'll see how the competition goes. >> Someone who's carried that level of volume recently, maybe more recently than Treadwell or Duvernay. Is that important or does that matter when you guys are looking at >> We're just doing I think Reggie's doing a good job of rotating those guys right now. That's really what camp's for is rotating those guys and see who's going to step up and make the most plays. >> Okay. >> All right. Thanks, guys. Appreciate it.

title: Colts players on first week of training camp, what they expect with pads Monday
text: Quentin. Quentin, just what are your impressions of Daniel, just his growth, his bounce back, and the way he looks so far? >> Yeah, I mean, he's been incredible. He's back like he's never left. Um and he just worked so so hard to get here and uh it's uh been awesome to see. >> How much more different or I guess better does it feel this going to year or two knowing you already know who he is personality-wise, work-wise? Compared to last year. >> Feels great. >> Quentin, it's been noted and it's evident from the work that he had to put in in the last 8 months to get to this point. What's something you maybe learned about like the attacking process that maybe you didn't know when you were working with him before? >> Yeah, I mean, he he's always been a hard worker. Um first one in, last one out. But, I think he really enjoys the work that he does to be the best quarterback he can be. Um this was a totally new challenge for him where you know, it's work that you don't want to do. He He's waking up super early, rehabbing, and then late at night rehabbing. Um and it's it's tedious work that you got to do every day that he did. Um and we just appreciate him a ton. >> How much have you guys benefited from another year of continuity with that offensive line? You obviously have one change, but I mean, you you've been here before where you had that continuity and grew together. Um what what is that doing for you guys right now? >> Yeah, um it's been awesome. Uh feel like we've had a good 4 days and stuff to improve on. Um but Ford's adding a year, um Gon is adding a year, you know, obviously Bernie's been doing it for a long time, but even he's finding ways to get better. And then adding Jaylen Samuels into the mix, um it's been really fun to see these young players growing uh and working so hard to get better. >> From the coaching staff too, I think nine of the 11 starters on the offense. When you have that continuity, what does that do for a team that kind of helps you guys hit the ground running when it comes to starting the season off? >> Yeah, it helps us a bunch. >> What have you seen from Jaylen so far in camp? He's been a lot more vocal. >> Who's Jaylen? >> Travis. >> Trav- Travis? Um Got to be honest, I'm pretty focused on myself uh and like the left side and board next to me like working with him and working with him that I don't really pay that much attention to Gons and uh Jaylen, but I mean I I saw all I needed to see like last year um and this off season and in camp with the way they work and how much it matters to them and how much they care. and then also obviously how talented they uh he is as well. Um so you add hard work to talent, that's that's awesome. >> What kind of growth have you seen What kind of growth have you seen from uh Boardlini just being the guy who snaps the ball every snap and doing well next to you? >> Yeah. Uh he's been great since day one um and it's not easy. Uh the center has a tremendous responsibility in our offense with having to make all the calls, read the defenses, see the safety rotation, everything. And I mean he's just taken the bull by the horns and he's gotten better every year when it comes to that um to the point where he's able to check protections and having a center like that who's that smart and then also again that talented and able to run the way he can and also get movement uh awesome. >> Dude, I mean that I mean I know you're a very diligent worker and like a lot of the work is not always physical, right? It's the mental part of the game. How have you sort of um maybe grown in that regard over the years just kind of learned to work smarter or I don't know, just kind of prepare better? >> Yeah. Um it's definitely important to work as efficient as you can and like work smarter while also working hard. But that's just something you grow at as a player and you learn from older guys from a young age. So lucky enough to play with some great players that were able to teach me how to do that. So >> I know when you mentioned in the spring that you wanted to leave the contract stuff to your agent, but have you had any more discussions about your contract? Did you want to get something done before the season starts? >> I haven't had any discussions. That's not up to me and um yeah, I'm just really thankful to be here. Excited for this year and uh love this team, love my teammates. >> One last one. >> How different will Monday be just putting the pads on when you compare that to week one versus now in terms of the full padded practices? >> Compared to week one, this week this that we just had? Um yeah, it'll be more physical. When you put the pads on, you'll be you're a lot more banging out there. And it's just even more like football. Being able to grab on to those shoulder blades. Alignment never grab. Uh we just put our hands on. And uh >> [laughter] >> yeah. but uh we we love it when the pads come on. You callus your body, you get sore from all the hits you take and all the hits you give. And uh it it's fun. Uh having those shoulder pads on, these helmets on, I feel like it's what makes the game fun cuz you could just play with a reckless abandon and come off the ball hard and >> All right. >> Thanks for the visit, man. >> How y'all doing? >> Good. >> Had a nice bomb today. What's what's that like when you're kind of in the thick of this competition here when you establish yourself and you make a play like that? >> Yeah, it always feels good. I mean, whenever the ball gets thrown your way, especially a deep one, you just you see it in the air, try to run under it, come down with it. It's a great throw by Riley, obviously great protection to be able to get it off. So just happy with it. >> And had one yesterday on I contested catch had to come back for it, go up for it. What do you remember about that play too? If that one stood >> Um Oh, yeah, yeah, I remember the one Daniel threw. Yeah, kind of similar thing. Running my route. I knew I wasn't the primary look, but just ran the route to win it. I necessarily didn't like kill him on the on the release or anything, but saw that DJ gave me a chance. So, he tried to establish establish that trust and come down with the play. >> What have been the different situations in your career where you got sometimes a lot of opportunities, other times not many at all. How's that prepared you for maybe this position you're in here, which is kind of just be ready and see where you fit in? >> Yeah, I think you could say that. You know, looking at it like that you know, there's a bunch of different things that I've gone through that have led to me being here right now and try to learn from all of it. Like you said, I've had you know, years where felt like everything was going right and years where it felt like everything was going wrong. And so, I just try to learn from that and just understand that it is a game going against, you know, professional players every day. I just try to win all the reps that you can and see what comes of it. >> When you look at last year and maybe winter this time with the Colts, was there any specific thing you thought this is where I really want to get better to get back to where I was in Tennessee and playing and getting production and stuff like that? >> Uh I mean, that wasn't really the motivation. It was just I saw it was a good team. You know, I I played against them, you know, week one and got got kind of walloped when I was in Miami. So, I saw that and then watched, you know, that those first eight weeks and was watching throughout the season. And just understanding, you know, the the organization I always had respect for. So, that was kind of more of the motivation. >> Did Did you learn anything about what they do from just in the spring and maybe with OTAs and everything? >> Oh, a little bit. I mean, that's understanding I'm a bigger body receiver, you know, just go go out, play big, you know, establish yourself in the run game, do the dirty work. That's kind of what I've always hung my hat on and how I've carved out a career so far in the NFL. So, you know, my thought is, you know, if that's what's gotten me to this position, just continue to try to do that well. >> When you look at the wide receiver room as a whole, obviously there's some opportunity there. How have you all pushed each other, but also maintained like that camaraderie? >> Yeah, it's been a great group so far. I love I love being in that room. I feel like everybody um is competing, but, you know, everybody's quick to help and offer advice or, you know, whatever it might be. Um lend an extra hand, extra time, you know, studying, whatever it might be uh to to push each other to get better. So, it's been a great great room so far. >> You've been in the league a while now, but how is going to a coach like Reggie Wayne? How how has he kind of helped you take your game up to another level as >> Yeah, I mean, I just appreciate how, you know, he shoots it straight. Um and obviously I have all the respect for him, understanding watching him, you know, when I was growing up and the type of player that he is. You know, I take everything that he everything that he has to say coaching-wise um to heart cuz I know that, you know, it works. Um so, it's huge just having that having that um you know, veteran presence and a guy that's done it before. >> And makes you feel >> more that you're around talent-wise, skill set-wise in your wide receiver room. Who have you benefited or who have you benefited the most benefited the most from the guys in your room? >> Yeah, honestly, Alex has been a a huge huge guy for me so far. You know, obviously he's not out there, but you know, usually, you know, on the sideline watching practice, he's in my ear whether it's with, you know, a coaching point or encouragement. Um he's been a guy that, you know, with what he can do right now, he's making the most of it. >> And there's such a wide open column >> this versatile and doing I mean, how did you get that mentality pretty early on and how has that served you well? But particularly the blocking in place like this with JT. >> Yeah, I mean, early on, you know, my first few years we had Derrick, so you hand him the ball 30, 40 times and something good's going to happen. And it's the same thing here with JT, so that's something you definitely got to take pride in. I've kind of always have as a receiver try to take pride in blocking. >> Knowing there's so much competition in this group for that number three spot right now and with Alec not yet on the field and if there might be some more reps for you at the moment. Is there like an added sense of urgency to take advantage of the the reps and the times that you're getting to see ball in this first week or week and a half of camp before he comes back? >> I don't I'm not really putting that on myself. You know, I can't really focus on that. It's not anything I can control. And so right now I'm just trying to take advantage of the reps that I am getting. Been blessed that Reggie's been giving me some some good reps and reps with the ones and so I'm just trying to be out there be in the right spot when those opportunities do come. But I feel like if I try to put that urgency on myself, you know, I feel like I'm squeezing too tight and trying to hold on to something. Just let it let it come and if it happens great. You know, if not, you know, oh well. I'm just going to give my all and try to get it. >> Yep. >> Thanks guys. Appreciate it. >> So different much different camp for you this year obviously. >> Year two. How how different how can you can you can contrast last year versus this year in terms of like your preparation? >> Yeah, I feel like last year training camp it was just you know, I was a rookie trying find my footing and and routine and also just learning the playbook and and putting on you know, kind of just I wanted to show something of myself. But I feel like this year man, I've been around group of guys that have showed me how to do it and man just getting right with my faith. I think the Lord has blessed all of us with these amazing talents and I think it's it's for us to just go out there and be us the person he made us to be and you know, just taking all the advice that I got from all my vets even outside of my room. Just knowing what they did to keep their body healthy and what to expect especially in year two and and I feel like I've applied that and and it's been helping me a lot. >> Tell us about some of the physical and athletic changes you made in the off season. Are you seeing that translate to the field now? >> Oh yeah, definitely. I just feel a lot lighter on my feet. Just feel more explosive. Man, just feeling great shape. Feel like I I got a lot of fat off of me which it very needed. But I feel amazing man. >> What do you think of the opportunity ahead of you because of the opportunity you have opposite of watching the film? >> Yeah, man. I'm excited. Uh excited just to just uh I lived here for the last year. I feel like I showed some some splashes and some uh you know, some little clips of of what I'm capable of doing last year, but I just want to build off of that and you know, just take it day by day and just get every get better every day, you know, learn from the mistakes I made yesterday and the mistakes I make today and just continue to just critique every part of my game. >> This is one of those positions on the roster where there's maybe just about as much competition as anywhere. How have you experienced that and what is that um competition and the opportunity uh potential that you have there in light of the performance in the game? >> Uh it's man, it's been amazing. I think uh you know, going in knowing me, I I love competing. I love competing against, you know, great players who are around me, great players that, you know, offense side. So, I feel like that's always something that I love and and you know, I feel right at home. >> Watkins has acknowledged that there was a lot of pressure on him to kind of take over and be the guy last year. Have you noticed any changes in him this year compared to last? Like kind of taking ownership of things? >> Yeah, I mean I mean, me and Watkins have been home every day together. So, you know, while we're just sharing uh stuff that's on our mind. I think with him, he's he's done a great job. He's uh stepping into like a leadership role, you know, behind the scenes and just just helping out, you know, me and all the young guys cuz still young guys, I'm on my second year. And he's just been uh feeding into everybody, you know, giving everybody wisdom and what helped him, especially him being young uh being in his third year. So, it also helps us cuz you know, it's it's he's it's like bugging me and us and all them, but it's like, man, he just he just got done with his second he just got done with his first year. So, he's able to to give us uh information on what what helped him and and you know, we we can apply it in and do it to our everyday life. >> You talked about this last year and even in the spring a little bit. Mentally, how did you deal with okay, I'm a second round pick, expectations might have been this, but I'm not playing as much as I wanted to. How do you scroll that away and just mentally prepare yourself for another season? >> Yeah, I mean, I'd be lying to say it wasn't tough mentally, but for me, I only know my faith heavy. I know that my Lord and Savior Christ is is in him and he's he's everything that he's brought me out the slums. He's brought me in from the the darkest rooms, darkest places and and once I lean on him, I understand that man, I'm I'm performing for him. I'm not performing for the outside noise and it's it's a it's a one-man audience. So, I'm I'm just trying to be, you know, who he called me to be every single day. And that kind of helped me just to just to ease off, just to not put a lot of stress cuz I feel like stress is for everybody. Stress and the things that make you overthink that that takes away your joy is not from him. You know, the peace and the love, that's what he wants us to feel, you know, feeling the the love that that the Lord put around us and that he instilled in the word. So, you know, I leaned on that heavily heavily and and it's helped me a lot. >> Off day tomorrow, pads on Monday. >> All day. >> At your position, how much do you embrace and anticipate >> Oh. >> getting finally getting the pads on? >> That's where it starts. You know, that's where it starts. I feel like this is like a warm-up, you know, warm-up with no pads and you know, just t-shirts and everything, shorts, but once you put the pads on, that's where everything matters and that's where you have to really, you know, one of the pillars we we want to build off of is is being physical. So, it starts it starts Monday here Monday all the way till, you know, Super Bowl. So, that's that's the goal. >> In the short time you've been roommates with Arden Key, who's better in practice or in the office? So, what have you learned from him in the last few months? >> Man, Arden, he's just he's just allowed me to really look at the game from a different lens. He's helped me slow down the game, slow down everything and just and just how to not look at the big picture, but have blinders on and just just make your process a lot more quicker so you can play free. And that's one thing I love. He's always helping us even when we're not paying attention or we're just so focused in taking notes, he'll he'll call us to the side and and give us more you know little tips and tools of of what else we can we can do that help better our game. >> All right. Thank you. >> Thank you. Appreciate you guys. >> You got it. Fire away. >> And Mo, what what are you looking for in in red zone in terms of like you know the things you look for uh to show the improvement? >> Um just when we get down there executing um positive plays, no negatives. And when teams come out there and play us too hard being able to run the ball down their throats. And um they play us man just winning our winning our one-on-ones. >> Four practices in, what have you seen from Daniel? >> Um he looks like he never got hurt. I mean you see he's throwing dimes left and right on the field um getting out of the pocket scrambling and different things like that. And I think his confidence is building more and more every day. And when we put the pads on, I think it's just taking it to another level. >> From a chemistry standpoint, how how has that evolved from year one to year two of the year? >> Um um it's light and day from last year because you know last year him and AR were splitting the ones reps. So this year coming in he knows it's his team. Um we just went down to Florida a couple weeks ago the whole offense went down there and threw. He got us all together down there at IMG. So we built some chemistry down there. So coming into camp um it's like we never lost a step. >> He's He's taken off running probably four or five times now at this point this week. Does that give you guys a sigh of relief? >> Uh definitely gives us a sigh of relief and um I think it gives himself a sigh of relief that he knows he has the ability and the confidence to go out there and do. You know some guys coming off that injury might not try to escape the pocket and different things like that. But especially being in a practice setting you don't have to go out there and do that. So him just doing that just shows us all that he's ready. >> Mo, what's How would you consider describe this tight end room? >> Um I would say it's very versatile. Uh Tyler Tyler can pretty much do everything. Will Will's like the speedster of the group. You You know, Will come in, he's going he's going to find a way to get the ball. He doesn't like get a lot of game game reps cuz the three of us are do a lot, but whenever Will's on the field, he finds a way to make a play. And um me and Trea, I always call us like the bulldogs of the room. And if we get a chance to get the ball, we're going to try to run run through somebody's face. >> What do you notice from uh Carson Powell's development and uh being so new to the league? >> Oh, man. I tell him I'm like, "Man, you remind me so much of myself when I first got here." Um the things you're messing up, the things you're thinking about, I'm like, "Bro, I was doing the same exact stuff." So, when I see him do it, I try to um coach him through it and just give him little pointers here and there cuz I know it's a lot cuz it's like going to school all over again with the terminology and things like that. So, I know his mind's spinning every day. But, I just try to help him as much as possible. And then having Tom in the room, Tom helps us a lot. And he spends a lot of extra time with him and things like that. So, honestly, he's gotten better and better every day. So, just hopefully see him take that next step starting on Monday. >> What are the areas where you've seen him take the biggest leap, say from OTAs to now? And where do you you still feel like he's got some work to >> Um I would say just, you know, in the run game. That first step is so important with the technique and things like that. So, now he's getting out of his quicker first step, more aggressive. So, now it's just that aspect of shooting your hands cuz you're so they coach you so much on footwork and technique, you forget about the upper body part and being aggressive. So, that's like the next step in his development. Matching his feet with his hands and striking somebody. >> Well, for you, decade in, how did you make it or last this long and end up here? >> I would just say doing everything the coaches asked me to do. Um whether it be Well, I'm in year 10, I'm still playing special teams and things like that. So, guys get up to this age and they don't want to play special teams. But, as someone who's not a starter anymore, they ask you to play special teams, you go out there and do it. And then I would also just being available. I would say that's the biggest thing. Um being available and when my number's called, going out there and doing what I'm asked to do. >> You never envisioned this long or not or did you? >> Uh no, somebody just asked me the other day, "Did you envision playing this long?" I was like, "Honestly, I was just taking it year by year and whatever happened happened." And it's been a great experience so far, so hopefully try to keep it going. >> All right, thanks, Malcolm. Appreciate >> Thank you. >> Good luck, bro.

title: Thin at wide receiver position, Kicker competition heats up at Indianapolis Colts training camp
text: Day five from Colts training camp here at Graham Park has wrapped up. Uh pads on for the first time here, so we got to see a little bit more hitting, a little bit more action. It was a fast-paced practice today. Um getting some kicking reps in early for Blake Groupy. Saw a red zone session early for the ones with Daniel Jones. Um a lot of action. What was your biggest takeaway here from day five at Camp Joel? I >> I just think my biggest takeaway so far is that the defense is ahead of the offense right now. And and really sometimes you say that in terms of like well the offense needs some time to get in sync get in rhythm. I think it's bigger than that. I think the defense is better than the offense right now just in terms of you look at who they have at corner sauce Gardner Trevarious Ward even can Taylor Brit who I know people don't think about but he was a starter for two years in Cincinnati and he is still very young versus a group that doesn't have Alec Pierce right now. It's Lacoan Treadwell. It's Ash Dulan. It just feels like the it's it's a mismatch at wide receiver on the outside with the corners. >> Yeah, we haven't gotten to see this offense at full strength yet. Of course, Alec Pierce still out on the physically unable to perform list. Um we've talked to Shane Styen today. He has not yet given us a firm timeline on when to expect him to be back. Chris Ballard, when we talked to him before camp started last Tuesday, um said that he expected appears to be out one to two weeks. So, we'll maybe see if he gets back next week as the um Colts head to New England or if it's a little bit longer timeline even than that. Um but I think we expected coming into camp that the w even with Alec that the wide receiver situation could be a little bit of a problem. They just are frankly um thinner there than they were even if Alec is healthy. You lose Michael Pitman Jr. in that in that trade to the Steelers in the offseason and um they added Nick Westbrook A but maybe not someone quite at the caliber of Michael Pitman Jr. and then when you have Alec Pierce on the sidelines out waiting to heal up and and finish his rehab process I feel like it really exposes how thin they are at that position. We haven't seen them make a move yet um at least a major move in free agency during camp. We'll have to wait and see if that happens. Yeah, Westbrook Aeen is the one who's really made a couple of big plays, but other than that, what we've seen so far is a lot of what we saw today. Short passes. Daniel Jones has been accurate. He's run the offense well, but he has not been able to get the ball downfield with any regularity because, frankly, guys are covered. Um, my my one big play today, uh, Seth McGawan, the running back for the seventh round running back out of Kentucky, you've been kind of waiting for this day because he's known as a power runner. I just think there's something to him. You can see in the way he moves. He gets north south really easily. And the thing I noticed today, a couple of different times gets through the line, gets hit by some defensive backs, kind of just shrugged him off. They weren't taking people to the ground, but he also just wasn't taking much of a blow when they were trying to deliver it. And I think that there's just some power there that I'm kind of excited to see when we get to the preseason games. feels like a little bit of a change of pace um that you um maybe don't have as much of or you maybe aren't wanting to see Jonathan Taylor be or bruising back when he's leading the league in carries last year with 323 carries. Um big season for him in a contract year. I imagine um they are, you know, they want to run him as much as possible, but I I feel like you need someone that has a little bit more power in those short down situations or some of the red zone areas. Uh and and Seth Bengalen brings a little bit more of that than DJ Giddens. Giddens has some more speed. He's got of course got one more year in the league um as a rookie last year. But another one of those interesting camp battles uh to watch. Another battle. Um we we only saw one end of it today. Um saw Blake Groupy kick again in camp for the second time. Um 6'4 his longest of 57. Looked like it was good from 65. >> Yeah, he looks good. Um the the Colts have said that they will stagger um their kickers. So it wasn't an anomaly or unexpected that we didn't see Spencer Schrader out there today. Um maybe we'll see him tomorrow or or um Thursday when the Colts are back after an off day on Wednesday. But another battle to keep an eye on um in their first time kicking uh we saw Shrader miss one. Uh groupy still perfect was perfect in the one session we saw in OTAA. So we'll we'll see that and follow that. That's all for today here at Colts Camp at Grand Park day five. We'll have a lot of stories on indiestar.com. Go ahead and check those out. Of course, go to our YouTube channel where we'll have um all of our interviews, some clips um and all of our previous coverage through the first four days of camp. I'm Nathan Brown. He's Jo Ericson, Colts and Insiders for the Indianapolis Star. Thanks for watching. >> Good to see you. Um obviously first day in pads today. I thought it went really well. A lot of physicality. Um, good back and forth. You know, defense made some plays, offense made some plays, but it's good to get out here in pads. Um, banging around a little bit. Um, we go from there. So, whenever you're ready. >> How does the energy shift once you put on these pads? >> Yeah, a lot. A big time. I think the guys feel that when you come out here with the pads on. Obviously, it's a lot more physical. Obviously, we're taking care of each other, too, at the same time. It's a long season, but we got to be physical at the point of attack, and uh, I thought guys brought that today. Anthony and Riley had been rotated pretty evenly for most of the week, but Saturday it felt like Riley got quite a bit more action. >> Yeah, I think >> I think that was just the way the reps played out. We had a little long drive drill there and he got that long drive drill which got more of the reps. Um obviously if they would have rotated the other day, that would have been Anony's reps. So, we just rotate those guys. >> I think it was back on Friday. Um we saw Anthony a handful of snaps in that one practice. What did you Was there anything to that from him or from the center or what? Yeah, I think that's just concentration, you know, just getting the snaps, seeing it in um and go from there. >> What are your impressions early on of the kicking competition? Is there anything that Spencer not kicking today? >> Yeah, we're going to rotate those guys and kicking. Um but that's that's going to be a good battle uh for sure. Both those guys are starting kickers in this league. So, that'll be very interesting to see how that plays out cuz I love both those guys. >> Shame we see Buck come out getting some work in. >> Yeah. >> What's he mean to this defense? >> He means everything to this defense. Um he's been a pillar here for so long. Uh 10 year plus. um he leads the right way, works the right way to so to see him out there and get some reps um is huge and obviously that's an ongoing conversation that he'll have with you know myself and the trainers and just make sure his body's right and whatever he needs to get from a team standpoint he'll get uh throughout training camp. >> Can you say what Hunter's doing? >> He's got a hamstring right now. >> What have you seen from >> Yeah, there's no doubt. It's good to get the pads on with him. We're excited to see him in pads. I think he brings a lot of physicality um you know to the football field and so we're really excited about that. He's a downhill runner. Uh when I watch this tape in Kentucky, uh the physicality he ran with, you know, when he gets hit at the line of scrimmage, he usually falls forward for a couple extra yards, which is huge. Um you know, in short yardage situations or just in the middle of the game, uh it's big. So, good to see his growth and, you know, see how training camp plays out for him. >> Is there a little Zack Moss to his game with just the way he kind of cuts? >> Yeah, I think that's a fair assessment. Um yeah, he he's got some good stretch cut stuff ability to him. Um and again, he's not scared of contact, which is awesome at the running back position. You need that physicality. Um at that position, he brings that. >> How good that battle passing? >> He's been good. Obviously, that's a work in progress. Um we'll keep working through that. Um as many touches as we can get those backs out of the back field, you know, in team situations, even seven on seven routes on air, it doesn't matter, you know. I think you just keep working through that uh and see where it goes. But um excited about all those guys. Are you seeing the characters too from receiver so far? >> Yeah, I think there's a good competition going on, especially for that third spot with Duelan and Westbrook and Tread. You know, both those guys are battling like crazy. Um, but they're pulling for each other, too, which is awesome to see. That's that team, you know, not mentality. And, uh, it's good to see that. It'll be interesting to see how that all plays out. >> They match up obviously against a really tough DB squad with Mooney and Sauce. Um, I know you guys know that you'll get Pierce back eventually. Does that make it even a little bit tougher when they're going up against some of the best quarterbacks in the league when they're also trying to >> Oh, I think that's great when you can go up against two of the best in the league uh in practice every day. It's going to make everybody better. So, you know, to have those two guys out there um tight coverage, you know, every single play, especially when it's man coverage, um it's going to make those guys better. >> Shane, do you have any better sense on on Pierce's timeline? >> I don't. I know that he's working. He's heading in the right direction for sure. Um so, I feel really good about that. uh moving forward. >> Obviously Daniel's not taking any hits, but first day in pads for him as well. How how do you like what you saw the whole team in pads and how he played? >> Yeah, good. I think he's been doing a great job. He's progressing every day. Um making plays, getting us in and out of the right play, which is huge. Completing passes, moving the offense down the field, making good decisions. Um so we just got to continue that through camp. >> I think he's been missing last couple days of practice. What's he doing? >> Uh he's got a toe right now. >> Shane, with this tight end group, you seem like you got guys that do a lot of things. Tyler does everything, but do you like the makeup of this group? >> I do. I think, uh, obviously, you know, Tree and Mo are really good blockers for us, um, that we can use in the pass game as well. Obviously, Tyler's a guy that can do it all. Um, and so I think there's some versatility there with that and how we use those guys and that's up as up to us as coaches to put those guys in position to be successful. So, we work that, you know, through camp on how we use those guys and obviously throughout the season. >> What do you think about Mo? I mean, he's still here. You just he just like can't be without >> him. And there's no doubt. Obviously, every year, you know, Mo, you know, maybe a one-year contract, whatever it is, over the past couple years, but he's a guy that's just reliable. He's consistent. He does everything right. Um, and we love them on this football team. >> I think you guys have rotated through like six of your linebackers and ones the first couple days of camp. What What um are you guys looking for in that battle? And is there anything that stood out to you? >> Yeah, I think that's an ongoing battle with all those guys. You know, we're doing a great job. L's doing a great job. Better's doing a great job of rotating those guys. the communication piece of it is going to be huge and then making plays inside the box, you know, making tackles, being great in coverage. Um, and that's a process that we're going through and I'm looking forward to seeing that competition throughout camp. >> Without Hunter out on the team, AJ kind of slid in to go with his first. What did you see out of him today? >> Um, you know, I thought he made some good plays. I thought he was in position a lot of plays. You know, he's a smart guy for a young guy. I think he's got really good instincts. You know, he's always around the ball and you need that at that position. So, it's going to be good to see his growth throughout training camp and obviously throughout the season as well. >> I know Mark West, one of those guys that are challenging for that wider wide receiver three spot has gotten the most reps over the last couple seasons. He's had a couple good plays, especially late last week. Has he stood out to you or what have you noticed from him? >> Yeah, I think he's made some big plays for us. Obviously, a guy, you know, when he was at Tennessee two years ago, you know, I think he had I don't I want to say seven or eight touchdowns. So, he's made some plays in this league. a veteran guy that can play special teams as well. So, really excited about him and uh like I said, we'll see how that competition goes. >> Someone who's carried that level of volume recent, maybe more recently than Treadwell or is that important or does that matter when you guys are looking at >> We're just doing I think Reggie's doing a good job of rotating those guys right now. That's really what camp's for is rotating those guys and see who's going to step up and make the most plays. >> Since we last talked to you, you got in on 11 R1 11s. How's it felt? You said you had to make adjustments. So, how's that been coming along? >> It's coming along good. Um yeah, it was what a couple days ago where I was able to get a couple reps in 11 on 111. Um just feeling everything out and everything for the first time and live reps and I mean neck responded well. Um obviously some you know a little muscle soreness here and there obviously it was expected first you know first time getting back out there but all in all everything was great. >> Is there some sort of treatment plan or rehab? Not rehab but like just recovery plan that you have to take into consideration because of your neck now? Uh yeah, I mean just spending some extra time with recovery and stuff like that. Emphasizing, you know, recovering with my neck and everything, some soft tissue or traction stuff. Um yeah, pretty much in my, you know, recovery routine. >> Look, they working you in like they're playing. What's the next box to check off? Just more work to see how >> Yeah, just the workload, you know what I mean? Just, you know, um gradually increasing my reps throughout training camp. Um yeah, just bridging that gap, you know what I mean? And um you know obviously it was our first time in pads today. Um I only did Indie today and hoping to get some you know some reps with contact tomorrow. So >> how do you assess everything in pads today from the defensive side? >> I mean it's the first day you know what I'm saying? So um you know had some great things, some bad things, things we had to clean up. Obviously it's been a while since the guy's been in pads, you know what I mean? Just like you know getting position on tackling and wrapping up and little things like that. So >> you've been able to put your your kind of coach hat on more lately. What have you seen from Holy Wood and time? >> No. Yeah, just, you know, obviously they they both, you know, both of them they have quickness and everything and just being able to see them, you know, um, continue to get better with their technique each and every day, their hand placement within the run game. Um, it's been fun to see and and their footwork with stunts. Um, yeah, I mean, both of them have been able to, you know, make flashes of uh, plays throughout training camp so far and it's been fun to watch. What have your impressions been of the rookies like Bryce, CJ all see a lot getting a lot of reps at the one you see from there? >> No, just you know they're you know just from day one they've been coachable and everything with the coaches with you know doing what the coaches are asking them to do and um just you know being out there being communicative and um being loud for everybody to hear them and um you know just the confidence they have and uh each and every day they're coming to work and um you know they're doing everything they can to to be out there to help the team. So it's been fun to watch. start. This has been asked, but how therapeutic was it today to get some physicality for the first time since what, October, November last year? >> Yeah. Uh I mean I I just did individuals and some drills today, but it was it was good. Yeah. Hoping tomorrow to get some reps out there. We'll see how everything goes. >> Is it weird like I think I can't remember you ever starting out where you had to be kind of limited. Is it weird? >> Yeah. Yeah. No, it's definitely weird. Um, but like I said, like when I first reported, I mean, just being able to be at this spot, being, you know, coming to camp cleared, you know, was a big goal for me and, uh, you know, I'm just, you know, just trusting the process and everything. So, I mean, but it is a little weird coming in, you know, not really doing much. >> I know the coaching staff is expecting a lot out of, um, Lu to take another league here in year three. What have you noticed from him throughout the spring and this first week of camp on what he's trying to work on? >> Yeah, just the confidence that he has, you know, and everything that he's doing. Um, I feel like, uh, you know, a lot of it, you know, part of the game is, you know, a lot of it's mental as well. And I I just see, you know, the confidence that he has and trusting in his moves and the things that he's been working on, you know, throughout the offseason. Um, he's out there where I feel like I just see, you know, a lot more confidence with him. >> Buck, it's just the start of the second week, but you've got new guys working in at linebacker. This is the first training camp where you have Sauce and Mooney out there together. What sense are you starting to get of what this defense can be? >> No. Yeah, it can be special, you know what I mean, with all the the talent that we have. um you know on all three levels of the defense and you know just you know it's you know this time is all about building that chemistry together being out there on the field together so um it's going to be exciting. >> First of all, what did groupy say about me before >> only [laughter] right? >> What has that relationship been like with Blake through this whole process? >> It's been fun for me. I think I consider myself blessed to be able to compete with Blake uh just cuz we're such good buddies and I want the best for him and I know that he wants the best for me. And then he was one of the the primary guys when I was at Notre Dame that helped to recruit me and make me feel at home. So I have nothing but respect for him. He's an excellent kicker and so far it's it's been great. Yeah, competing has been no issue at all. >> At what point did you feel like you got back to full strength and and had everything and were like reared up and ready to go for this competition? >> I feel like I'm still building. You know, I I think I was blessed because the we have such a good training staff at the Colts that knee-wise I was feeling back to normal pretty fast. I started kicking early, but you're just always working on like tempo and timing and getting back into your routine and rhythm of things. And so, I've tried to frame it as like I'm not trying to get back to where I once was, you know? I'm trying to be the best version of myself right now. And I feel like that's still getting there every single day, trying to set a new standard, get more and more comfortable, and reach a new level. I'm just working on kind of simply simplifying that mindset day in and day out. >> Did you feel like did you feel like you took a big step forward kind of between when you guys broke in June and the start of training camp? It just felt like the first time we saw you kick out here looked a little more like like you. >> Yeah, for sure. Um I had a great summer where I was playing pickup sports. I was playing soccer, pickle ball a little bit, everything. Um, I think that's a large part of like when you're rehabbing from injury is obviously you want to get back to where you were like kicking wise for your job, but it's really like I want to be the same athlete that I was before. So, I want to develop in the weight room when I'm running, when I'm jumping. I want to be just as coordinated, just as fit, just as strong as I was. And then I know that the kicking will sort of follow that. >> First day of pads, like how did the energy shift out there for the whole team today? >> It looked pretty energetic to me. I was watching some guys tackle each other. I'm like, "Oh, are we supposed to be doing that?" I kind of had to get reminded real quick. Um, but it was great energy out there and it's good to see the guys flying around. I haven't taken any hits yet, so I'm I'm all good. But yeah, team's looking really good. >> Do you wait for that first hit? Some kind of >> You probably don't take it till preseason, right? >> Yeah. When I'm getting hit, it's something's going bad. Like if I'm getting into a tackle, it's like something happened. It's not good. And I just try to brace for impact and get him down the best I can. when you're trying to make a comeback like you are right now. How much easier is it making it having a duo like Luke and Rio that's been together for 10 years? >> I mean, I think about all all the time. That's why I love part of the reason I love being here so much is cuz I genuinely love the specialist room and I love being around those guys. Those guys aren't just my co-workers, they're my friends and I get to learn from them every day. It's awesome. I know Shane said that it was scripted today um having poopy kick early and you sit out what on a day like this when you see Blake kick kicking during team reps and you not even though you know that's how it's supposed to run like what are those days like in in >> Yeah, it's a good question because it's kind of a unique situation this year with the rotating days. That's been a good mentality so far. >> Thanks. >> Awesome. Thank you guys. Appreciate you guys. Good. >> These situations where you're battling for a roster spot. Um what are what are these weeks like um for you and your experience before and how you feel like you've been um kicking and working out so far? >> Yeah. Um definitely not new to this, I guess, you know what I mean? I'm um I'm comfortable in competition. It is what it is at our position. Um you're in the National Football League, so what do you expect, you know? Um, but you know, you definitely have to take advantage of your reps. You know, you look at a whole training camp of five weeks and uh you think you have all this time, but at the end of the day, you you know, it's definitely limited. We don't kick every day. Um, so you have to take advantage of your opportunities and and uh, you know, not get cheated. Do you kick I mean other times during the week that we just don't see? I assume. >> Yeah, I mean it's all um it's all scripted out. It's all it's all planned out. Um you know it's all about reps and uh building up towards the season. So uh you know they obviously want as many reps as possible to evaluate and and uh you know make their decision I guess. But uh yeah I mean we're always working. It's you know regardless if you're kicking out there or not you're always doing something. Uh, so, you know, it's kind of a normal to to uh, you know, pick and choose your days during camp depending on when they want you. So, it's uh, you know, you just got to, like I said earlier, you got to take advantage of them, you know, when it's your time. >> Like the regular season where you're going to have only so many reps late during the season for during a game. >> Yeah. During, I mean, during a regular season, you're kicking on Sunday obviously and then Wednesday, Friday, and actually know you're playing Sunday. So, um, you know, it's normal to have days in between. It's just part of the schedule. >> You've been doing really well ever since you got here last year. How much of an impact and go together. They've been together for a decade. How big has that been? >> You know, it's been great just to work with a operation that's that's been together for, you know, I think this is their 10th year. Um, you know, there's probably not a situation or a snap or a hold or condition that those two haven't gone um, you know, through together. So to come here, work with those guys. Uh you know, worked with Rigo before in in the offseason and was out in San Diego at at a big camp working with them and uh you know, it's just great having two veteran guys. J August now. I I haven't put pads on like eight months, so you know, you got to get get a little used to it. Breaking break them in.
