So, it it kind of keeps you on your toes and you know, just keeps you honed into your technique and then Grando is just a a guy who likes to play really like physical and you know, I like guys like that cuz you know, like I said, it builds the callus for yourself for for the season, but uh yeah, they just have a lot of change up. So, it's good for me. >> Uh how are you feeling like physically after after last year and just having to do like the kind of maintenance throughout the season and everything? >> Right. Uh you know, I just try to like really build myself in the off season. Uh try to get stronger and stuff. Uh lost a little bit of weight, but you know, just trying to be able be able to uh you know, be my my my best self this year and uh I think last year obviously with the ups and downs with like you know, injuries or whatever is I think it was just a good uh point of adversity for me just to kind of overcome. >> You like are you like off the maintenance plan now? Are you able to just kind of >> Uh But I I I keep my my I feel like I keep my own maintenance even though like I'm you know, I'm good now but I feel like it's you know, try to keep good. You feel me? So Yeah. >> What's a little bit of weight? >> Uh shoot, maybe like 7 lbs, 7 7 8 lbs. Sounds like a little bit but I feel like sometimes it be a lot of football so yeah, it's cool though. >> Hey, what does David have with this uh team? >> Man, I feel like you know, uh you know, a lot of guys on our o-line is always like you know, it's always like tough guys like hey man, we got to do do this that push through but I feel like Dave like he's just a very wise dude and you know, sometimes we can get caught up in trying to push push push or like trying to like pound on everybody and everything. He kind of comes in like hey, everybody relax like we're good, you know, stuff stuff like that and I feel like that's a good, you know, sense for us cuz sometimes like you know, a lot of the guys are on it's on our offense is a kind of young so you know, having older guys like that like Cam and Eric together with those brains on the o-line is is good for us so >> Uh this is your first year in the pros without a position change going into this >> Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. >> How does it feel just kind of the continuity? >> Uh it's cool cuz you know, you get the reps and I don't know how many reps I've gotten so far but it's just good cuz almost like same sense of callous, right? So just getting that uh muscle memory out there and all that and see if I can try new things. >> I know you you played the position in in college. Is it kind of nice to be back at home there or >> Yeah, I kind of you know, when you go through the playbook and stuff and you kind of find like similar stuff uh that you had in college is it's pretty fun but it's also like man, this is is dope cuz like man, I've been there before uh so you know, stuff like that is it's good for me. >> When y'all in the meeting room, how do y'all like the coaching looking at the film you have full pads on? Did you Did you really judge if y'all successful running the ball considering that you're not tackling the running back to the ground? >> Right. Uh I think it's just like man, where's that first point of contact? Uh you know, like did we win the line of scrimmage? Where did the running back make first point of contact? And if it's in front of the line of scrimmage, hey, that's a plus for us. But if it's not, then like, hey, where can we, you know, work on things like that. >> Has Has the run game been kind of an emphasis for y'all this offseason just like since that kind of wasn't where y'all wanted to be last year? >> Right. Yeah, I think for sure. Um I think Kellen's been like implementing a lot of different run games, different schemes, but I feel like a lot of it's just meant to up our game, right? In the in the run game cuz obviously last year it wasn't our best we didn't want to put on film, but but yeah, I feel I feel like we're making an emphasis on it. >> Well, consistency's key obviously for for everybody, but does does anything change or feel different when like getting acclimated to maybe Travis Etienne's speed or the way that he runs or his vision or anything like that? Like does that impact you guys at all? >> Nah, I wouldn't say too much. I feel like the O-line like we're on our own thing, you know, like whether you put whoever back there, right? We just stick to our rules and stick to our technique and we'll be all right. >> Both those guys are often described as patient, too. What does that do for you as an offensive line knowing that like they'll give you time to >> Right. I feel like it's nice cuz, you know, you get to have a sense of where the like linebackers going to play, whether it's a inside zone, outside zone, and you know, how fast it's going to play, so feel like them and the linebackers kind of have a big part in us. >> What are the reasons >> [clears throat] >> why this team might be poised to make a big jump this season? >> Man, you know, I can't say nothing too early, right? But I I I feel the sense of like, man, you know, we're in the right direction and everything, but I can't say that right now, right? We're we're we got to take it one day at a time and, you know, win the camp.

Uh Romeo Dobs took an end around and Craig Woodson kind of took him to the ground and I was like, "Whoa, okay, it's going to be that kind of day." So, I think that it was uh a little bit of that is brewing. You know, you've been practicing in pads against the same people for multiple practices now. I >> I will just say real quick on that play, I had the same initial reaction that Evan just did on that was like, whoa, whoa. So that I think Hunter Henry may have kind of helped Woodson along with a little bit. I just I don't want people to think that we were. >> Yeah. [laughter] >> Carry on. Carry on. Uh I don't want to make too much of it though, but the connection I thought Tat made it was Tommy Dvito and Matt Holland threw a few touchdowns. I mean, you know, we're getting some of like you said, Ev, it's getting to be a little bit of a grime, but I do think it's worth pointing out, you know, some of these guys on the second team reps that are, you know, consistently making plays. I think Tommy Devito and Baron Morton by that note have both been pretty solid this camp seems like Baron Morton's getting more opportunities than we saw Ben Waldridge get last year and the ball just to Paul's thing it doesn't really hit the ground a lot no matter who's in there I just think it's a positive sign I know look we don't want to see Tommy DeVito we'd like to stick with Drake May for the length of the season but promising sign that this guy came in they gave him basically the backup job and and he's performing pretty well >> yeah I I would say with Dvito it's you want to see those guys be able to showcase their skills skills more so maybe than I'm worried about Tommy Devito. And sometimes we see these backup quarterbacks that frankly are just so inaccurate that you can't really gauge the receivers. And Matt Holland, you mentioned I would say Kahan Booty to an extent as well today. Both those guys whenever they rep with the twos, it's so clear that they're a cut above everybody else that's on the field. Matt Collins had a couple, but I think the best throw of the day was the back pylon throw that Dvito made to booty. Uh and that one was a great throw. >> Yeah. Right on the money. could not be defended because it was just so perfectly placed. So, both those receivers, it's very clear to me when they get down to the twos and they're just, we talk about it all the time, there's seven guys that they need to get reps for and Matt Collins and Kan Booty will sometimes have to rep with the twos and it's just very clear that they're too good for that group of people on an NFL field. So, Matt Collins did almost take out a reporter. I'm not going to name names. Uh he did okay though. It was it [laughter] was pretty close. Uh but it was uh it was a good showing from I think all those guys. Booty, Hollands. Nice practices for them. >> Good back and forth. I thought I thought they were pretty competitive. Um I I agree with you. Those guys caught passes, but I thought there was some some balls they could have caught that they didn't. Both Hollands and and uh Booty. And uh especially with Booty, it's striking to me because generally anytime the ball gets thrown to him and he gets his hands on it, he catches it. Uh there were a couple today that went slant went off his hands. Yeah, that was a clear drop on the sl and and there were a couple other times I thought um Holland showed some frustration with getting getting locked up a little bit. So, uh I did think there was some good back and forth. We heard from Kevin Bard after practice sort of talked about the value of that. You don't want, you know, it's never going to be one side just sort of carrying the day and and I don't think that was the case today. Good good solid competition, good heat I thought uh between the two sides. Maybe it was because we were so much closer >> to the field. You could hear the reactions after plays, but I thought they were getting after it pretty good. >> Yeah, you see the guys are actually pretty big, too, when you're that close to the market. >> Yes. Turns out >> sneaky NFL players sneaky big. >> NFL players sneaky big. >> Do [laughter] >> breaking news here. Uh Gabe Ais starting to ramp up a little bit. Got, you know, one I think one one-on-one rep. Little bit of team. >> I think he tried to sneak into the drill every two seconds and Mike Smith had to keep pulling him back and pulling him back. Uh he went up against Lawrence Mets, who's probably not going to be on the team if we're being honest, but he did beat him uh in the one-on-one and he had a a handful of team reps uh as well in 11on1s and we saw him go right around Marcus Bryant to blow up a run play at one point in practice. So I He looks in like he's in great shape. It doesn't look like he was sitting on the couch waiting to to get the contract done. Uh he looks like a freaking Adonis out there. I mean, if he plays as well as he looks, then we're going to be in good shape. So, I think that's the biggest takeaway so far is that he looks like he's ready to go. He looks eager. He looks like he's in shape, and now we just got to see how he progresses. >> I get to those Colts joint practices next Tuesday. Maybe by that time he'll be full. >> I mean, I think today he was he was pretty much in there. I mean, like like Evan said, he took some team reps and if you're taking team reps, you're sort of ready to go. >> Yeah. Couple uh so a couple housekeeping things. Uh Terrell Jennings, number 26, came off of NFI and was pretty much a full participant. I mean, he jumped in there, some hits. He was running through the line. No, Kaden Wallace. Kyle Williams, we didn't see him initially. Later in practice, he showed up. He looked kind of wet. He was all in full pads. I wonder if maybe he was doing some rehab or something outside. I don't know. But didn't really get into uh any of the team drills. Uh and a new number 96 as well, Casey Rogers. So, starting to see Paul some of that, you know, bottom of the depth chart. No, Kaden Wallace, you know, we don't know what's going on there, but seems like they're rotating guys a little bit. You're starting to see some movement. >> Yeah. You know, and I don't know what the situation is with Wallace, but uh, you know, the defensive lineman, you know, someone, you know, sort of working with the threes gets banged up. They don't really have time for you to miss a practice or two. They got to bring someone in to make sure that those reps get replaced. So, yeah, it's it's part of the balance, but good to see uh both AIS and Terrell Jennings back. And, you know, maybe we'll see Harold Landry before too long. I don't know how much longer, but I mean, Mike Vrabel did talk late last week and said that he was going to be longer than those guys. So, we'll see if that's something that impacts the regular season. >> It's still no Carlton Davis. Evan, I felt like uh I think we all have noticed, you know, some of these younger quarterbacks getting some opportunities here. Krony was in the midst of a couple different things today. Thought, you know, he was good pass breakup on AJ Brown. Then he had one with I I think it I'm not sure one of the lower, you know, just looked like he was going to pick just out muscled him and took the ball away. Couldn't quite come up. >> I I was noticed by Channing. Oh, that was definitely a catch. >> I'm going pick. It's the battle of possession, >> but I feel like he had the ball and then they were on the ground and after he already had possession of the ball, de Janeiro ripped it out. >> Well, you were fighting about that. >> So, I'm >> I'll go with Channon Crowder as the um Canada. I keep calling him Crowder because Mike Gardi wrote uh Crowder in in his uh update and he kept telling me about it. Uh I thought he was sort of the secondary >> member of the secondary who really uh showed up. I thought he got some more reps today with with twos that I hadn't really seen. It's been Prunty and and Miner and those guys. I thought 29 and Blue showed up today and again when they're doing the kickoff returns, he was doing some of those reps too. >> Yeah, it seems like he's got some versatility. Maybe a player that could play inside. Prunty just impresses me though because of his size, speed, length. >> He can carry a go route. I mean, that's for sure. Like he did it twice today. Uh, so I I don't know if he's going to be able to cover the whole route tree just yet. But if you put a guy out there like that that's at least not going to get burned deep, then you feel pretty good about helping him out on the other stuff. So with his length, with his speed, I think he's got that ability to carry vertical routes down the field. And when you play on the outside, that's the majority of what you're going to see. So very early leader, I think, out of that group as like the the fifth quarterback that they might carry. I think Charles Woods is on this team as the fourth guy and I'd say Prunty is making a push right now. >> Yeah, Charles Woods getting a lot of reps still. Carton Davis continues to be out that's offering opportunities to some of these guys. So, we'll see. We're in the dog days of camp now. That's been four padded practices in five days. >> I want a replay on that front. >> We'll try to get the go to the tape before next breakdown, but they'll be back in pads again tomorrow, Tuesday. Supposed to be a beautiful day. If you're able to come on down here to the Gallet Stadium, it's a great take.

title: Will Campbell, Milton Williams, Kevin Byard III & More Address the Media | Patriots Press Conference
text: Does it annoy you when second year tackles keep you waiting? >> I I go with the pass. Yeah, I like. >> What's it been like out there as a group? Will was just kind of saying you guys last year built the base. You feel like this year you grow even more. You feel comfortable with that base as you come into camp here and as you go above this these periods? >> Yeah, we know we out there we out there competing every day. Um Like I said last year I feel like all those young guys including Will just growing and learning. Um You know, with the new guys coming in AVT coming in. Uh Big Mike still being where he at Jared moving to the new spot. Um Big Mo back. So you know, we just continuing to grow. Uh we out there you know, we getting after each other trying to get each other better every day. And you know, that's all we can do. >> What have you seen from some of the second year guys in your position like Eric Gregory and Joshua Farmer in their development so far? >> Now them boys they out there working. They're grinding and and you can see that the hunger to get better each and every day. And you can watch uh some of the one-on-ones and even the team reps. So guys are continuing to get better working their craft and drills and you know, bringing it to life in a team session. So um the more and more we practice the more confidence they're going to build. [clears throat] And then we'll go against a new opponent, you know, we're going to see what they got. >> One of the things that Will talked about was the fact that the offensive line and the defensive line you guys will communicate about, you know, who you need to see, who you need to improve, that kind of stuff. What are those conversations like from your perspective and just something where you're reaching out to an offensive lineman they're talking to you, what's that like? >> Just telling them, you know, I'm always looking, you know, at their stance. It it it any pass tip any pass or run sales that they're giving us up front. Cuz I know other D-linemen across the league looking at the same thing. So if I feel like they're giving away a look, you know, I'm telling them after practice cuz I'm going to use that to my advantage during practice. But after, you know, I'm going to say, you know, I knew y'all was doing this cuz y'all was leaning this way, y'all I looking a certain way or you know, some of y'all communication maybe I didn't pick up on but you know, having those conversations knowing that you know, I'm not the only one listening to those calls is just going to going to help them in the future and help us continue to you know, grow. >> How many times has that happened in camp where you've recognized a tell? It's only been eight practices but this summer, how many times? >> How many practices? >> How many times in practice have you recognized a tell that you just described? >> Shh. Every practice I feel like you know, I can pick up on at least one or two. but they're they're doing a good job of trying to build on it and and play faster and try not to give it away as much. So, you can tell that they're taking my coaching but I'm still trying to you know, get an advantage for myself. >> Okay, no no. >> glean anything from them as well? Are they Are you able to glean anything from the offensive lineman? Do they ever tell you anything that you're doing? >> Um other than you know, they they know a lot of guys that want to try to get on me early cuz they're afraid of my power. So, just me being ready instead of having one two steps to throw a move, probably throw it off one as soon as I come out of my stance, get ready to get their hands down and you know, go from there if I need to you know, throw a counter but um just things like that. Guys are trying to you know, get on me early knowing they won't let me get into them and then throw a move. Um so, I just got to be ready quicker. >> I know it's only been two practices but what are you seeing from Gabe um young edge on the defensive line? >> Just eager to learn, you know. You know, whatever the situation was, you know, he happy to be out there. He happy to you know, be competing and you know, he he a sponge right now. I told him just be a sponge, learn as much as you can cuz you know, we're going to need you this year. And you know, I think he going to be ready for that challenge but you know, he got to go through his own process as a young player and you know, keep getting better each and every time he come out. >> So, what gives you the confidence to say you know Gabe's going to be ready for the challenge? >> Just look at the type of player person he is. Um I talked to him a little bit before he got out here. So, saw him working. You know, he he was ready to be back. And you know, just his mentality. Asking questions in meetings. You know, Vrabel picking on him a little bit. But, that's all a part of it. You know, you take it on the chin and and you roll with it and you continue to grow. And when it's an opportunity for you to show what you can do, you got to show it. >> When you like to hear him sing? >> How does Mike pick on him? >> Did y'all have the >> I think we had the same song. >> Yeah. Let's do it in harmony, Nico. One, two, three. How did Vrabel pick on him? >> No, just like the rookie stuff in a team meeting. Instead of, you know, going up there and singing, you know, he got to get up there and say his name, school, signing bonus, what how much NIL he made. Every time he come up there, he got he got a call on him. So, no. He He been up there about five times. They didn't boo him on the first four. I'm like, man, look. You got to go up there. You got to sing. Sing something and then everybody's singing with you. I think he did good last time. I think he had a joke or something that everybody laughed at. So, maybe Vrabel ease up on him. But, he's a rook. So. >> How much did you enjoy that? >> No, it's funny. I I was in that same position. I was telling him, man, you just got to just do it. Just do it. Show them that you don't care. Yeah, we going to talk about you. But, man, this is a locker room. This is the league. This this how it go. >> Do you remember what your song was back when you were a rookie? >> Uh Bootsy Collins, I'd rather be with you. >> You want to sing some for us? >> No, no. One one-time thing. >> Hey, a question about you and and Barmore. A lot of guys pointing to you two as as your leaders up front. How good do you feel you guys could be together as a combination this year? >> I think it's all about both of us staying healthy as much as possible. And you know, you saw what we did with the impact we had on the games last year. Just continue to have that same impact. Dominating in week in week out no matter who we play, what front we see, you know, it's on us. The defense is going to go as far as as we take them. I said it all the time. I feel like the interior defensive line uh has the most impact on the game probably other than offensive line. So, you know, we most of the time when we all D-line play good, you know, we end up winning the game. So, if we don't win, you know, first people you can look at would be the front. >> Milton, you were talking about um you know, guys are ready for your power and you're working on counters. How much of what goes on in those battles is you want to dictate your will on them or how much of that is like reactionary? Oh, I see him doing this quickly and that's my counter to it. >> It it's it's a split second. It's a split section. Split second. So, there's I'm I'm a power player. So, guys are anticipating on me just running through them. So, they want to try to get on me early. So, if I take a step and he's sitting flat at the line, I got to throw a move or counter right now and then build off of the rush right now. I can't It's not two steps I can't get two steps in and try to get up the field cuz they're just going to try to wide me out. I got to be ready to throw off one step and then, you know, set it up off of that. And then, once they start sitting different or then I can include my power and then start building rushes throughout the game. >> Thanks, Milton. >> How's it going? >> Good. How are you doing? >> How would you describe today's practice just going indoors and and um just how it just went? >> Yeah, I mean, I think it was competitive. Um you know, heavy emphasis on red zone. Um we had some really competitive periods. Matter if it's one-on-ones, team. We worked a lot of different situations. Obviously, still early in training camp, so it's a lot It's a lot of back and forth. Um but no, it's been fun. I think it's just the competitive spirit of this team at every position, every level. Offense, defense is trying to get better and I think we're pushing each other. >> When you say back and forth, there seemed to be some more verbal battles, or at least we were closer to the verbal battles today. Has that been something that's been going on, or is it starting to heat up now cuz you guys are starting to get sick of each other? >> Well, it's definitely heating up a little bit more, but I think it's been kind of it's it's been a lot of back and forth throughout training camp, but um I think just as you know, Vrabel's telling everyone the offense score, they go celebrate, we get pissed off, and so it's kind of just a lot of back and forth, but no, that's what training camp is for. You know, we're not going to be out there um I mean, while we're out there, we're against each other, but we're not about to start throwing hands or nothing like that. But um obviously, as we get closer to these joint practices, you can tell like we're getting to those dog days of camp where, you know, guys are kind of getting a little sick of each other, you want to go up against somebody else, so it's been fun, though. >> I mean, he's got a way now back. How much is Vrabel an instigator >> I wouldn't call him an instigator, but I will say just Vrabel he really can't help himself by like the back and forth a little bit. Like he like if the offense or if the defense is winning, like he's talking trash to the other side, like you're going to let them do that. And I think it's just kind of um he he's a competitor, too, you know what I mean? Like he was like that as a player. I've heard plenty stories of him being here, getting on scout team, picking off Tom Brady, stuff like that. I think he's just um just a competitive guy, so he wants his team to have that same competitive spirit. >> We've talked to some of the guys before about the offense guys, you know, guys on the offensive side of all helping out the defensive side. We've all talked about, you know, getting some tips from the defensive lineman. >> Right. >> When you go up against a tight end, a wide receiver, what are those conversations like in terms of maybe helping them say, "Hey, look, I saw this. Maybe you want to work on that." >> Yeah, I think for me, I'm always asking, like whether it's Hunter Henry or whatever, like how he likes to stem his routes based upon our leverages. So, I kind of get a good feel for that, and then for him, like when he runs his routes, like some guys as a tight end, they're expecting to get pressed, they're expecting safeties to get up on them. So, sometimes tight ends like to either throw an elbow to get a guy off of it, but like Hunter's almost like a two-hand push kind of guy. And so for me it's like I'm trying to work my counter off that is like if he knows I'm going to do this, he's going to two-hand push, maybe I got to switch it up. Maybe just slap his arms down, like mess him up or whatever. I played against a receiver when I was in Tennessee, but he was in LA too as well. But Robert Woods and he was a really good blocking tight I mean blocking blocking tight receiver. And he was really good cuz knowing a a tight a safety's going to come down try to run fit, instead of him just doing this, he would check your hands and basically slap your hands down and it'll throw you off balance and get a good real good block. And I would ask him questions like that. So it's just little small things, nuances of the game just trying to figure out what they like to do and how to counter off of that. >> When it comes from a player as opposed to a coach, does it carry a different weight? And that's no disrespect to the coaching staff, but from a guy who's on the other side of the ball going through it every single snap, do you take it you know, take it into consideration more or less? >> Yeah, for sure. I mean, we're the ones on the field, you know what I mean? And especially looking at a guy like Hunter, we both came in the same time, played a lot of ball. So you're just learning from each other and I think it's the same thing when I'm asking Drake like, "Hey, what are you seeing in these coverages? Hey, we're disguising this. What makes you check to a different call or what makes you motion a receiver over?" It's just those small things getting little nuances and that's what training camp is for. Obviously as we get to the season, there's going to be different things we're going to be looking at as far as game plan against another team, but while we're out here, just trying to get a good sense of what he's looking at, what he's seeing and how I can try to counter off that to try to, you know, make him make a mistake cuz we're all out here trying to we're out here competing and trying to beat each other. That's what it is. >> When you spoke to us last week, you said that the defense was ahead of the offense, which you said at at that point in camp is pretty typical. Now where we are now, do we do you feel like the offense has closed that gap? >> Yeah, I mean, they've been making some plays. I mean, you see there was a lot of touchdowns today. I mean, I will say just it being a red zone day, you know, a 10-yard catch is going to be a touchdown, you know what I mean? So but at the same time as a defense, we got to challenge more and I think that's just what we're working through working through Um as a defense is like, "Hey, situational football. Maybe in the field a 10-yard out cut catch tackle is fine, but in the red zone is a little different. So, maybe you got to slow your pedal down. Maybe you have to tighten up your alignment by challenging the guy or something like that." So, but I think this is what these situations is for. You know, I don't get too bent out of shape by practice results sometimes because it's never as good as you think it is. It's never as bad. I think once you look at the film, you make those corrections. You just try to make a new mistake almost. If If you see If you did someone tape that you made a mistake on, don't make a mistake again. Make a new mistake. So, that's what we're all trying to strive for just just getting 1% better. Nothing's going to be perfect. >> Kevin, over your career, what lately has become more effective when you do disguise? Understanding offenses have changed, quarterback reads have changed, and safety, what's more effective now than before? >> Uh I mean, it's kind of hard to answer that. I think it depends on what we're doing as a defense. I think a lot of it is based upon what we're trying to show the offense cuz it it can depend based on formations, what they're doing. Um you know, a lot of times these these offensive coordinators or quarterbacks on third down so even first and second downs they want to see immediately if it's run I mean, if it's zone or man. So, they may line up one way more than likely going to shift formation or line up somewhere else. So, as a safety for me, I know what they're looking for. They put a tight end all the way out wide more than likely he's going to shift back in. They just want to see if it's run I mean, if it's man or zone. So, we're playing zone I might just line up out there and just run back with him. He think we're in man, go to zone. It's just little stuff like that. So, when I was younger I just like just trying to get lined up. But now, I kind of know that the chess game that the these coordinators are trying to play. And a lot of times nowadays us as a defense or defensive coordinator they're building in these disguises in the calls. So, that's changed over the years, but for me I'm always just trying to play a chess game with the quarterback. And if if you can just make them pump one time or make a little hitch, I mean, that's really all we can ask for. >> How much freedom do you have when it How much freedom do you have when it comes to trying to disguise those intentions based on what you know they're trying to do? And what goes into the communication to make sure you're still on the same page with the rest of the guys? >> Yeah, we got all the freedom in the world. I think a lot of it is just making sure that we're all on the same page cuz I can line up on the line of scrimmage and run to the post, but it doesn't matter if the other safety or the other linebacker or the nickel, we're not being coordinated with the disguise. It doesn't really make a lot of sense. Um because I can show down weak, but if the linebacker's not going to boss over a little bit to kind of give a good disguise, it doesn't really matter. So I think it's just those discussions that we're having on like our back seven meetings and watching film we get to look, "Hey, tomorrow let's switch it up. Let's show this. I can show over tight end." Even though the linebacker may have the tight end in a man, let me show down over him, then I can run back. So it just kind of depends. It's a chess game. Um but like I said, I do we have all the freedom in the world. Um I just always say don't let your disguise uh mess up your actual, you know, rules to whatever play you have. So you can always try to disguise, but sometimes you just don't want to get out of too much out of position. Yeah, no problem. >> Thanks, Kevin. Wet. >> Oh, how do you feel like things are coming as you guys go about your business here? >> I feel good. I feel like each day the offense, you know, uh we're making strides. Uh we're just finding the stuff to get better at each and every single day. Uh and up front just trying to, you know, give all of our play makers time to do what they do and you know, that's all we can do. >> Seems like you've had a strong start to camp when the when the pads came on. Just how are you feeling and how do you feel like you've been over the past like four days? >> Uh I feel good. Uh my body feels good. I'm just, you know, trying to be consistent as I possibly can be every single day and get better, you know, each and every single day and find something that I might not be doing well at a practice and try to that the next day and uh you know, I'm getting you know, great opportunities to go against some good guys. You know, Dre is a guy that I played in a game uh and he's a really good player uh and it's a good work for both of us, I think, cuz we're familiar with each other. I just kind of like a little chess match out there, so it's been fun. I'm uh I've had a lot of fun out there and just excited to keep going. >> Grab the one on the line. If you could confirm it's Dre on I know you guys have a lot of conversations, but kind of helping each other out. Kind of looking for what the other needs or wants or what are those conversations? How do they start? Is it one of those things where you go to Dre on or Dre comes to you or you talk on the field or what's that what's that like? >> I think it's, you know, the nature of the family feeling in this building. you know, as much as we want to kick at practice and they want to kick ours, you know, we're trying we want them to get as many sacks as possible. They want us to give up as few as possible and to see we're all trying to help each other better cuz that's the way that we're going to be successful during the season. So, you know, and it's not just Dre, it's all the D-linemen talking to the O-linemen and vice versa. You know, if we see something that they might be showing that we see that we can take advantage of, we communicate that and they do the same, vice versa. And I and I think that just comes from the the way that, you know, this team is tight-knit and can communicate with each other and just try to help each other become the best player that they possibly can. >> Is that the most competitive day for the run game so far? Did you feel similarly and what's the process of trying to build with the run game when the defense typically has an advantage early? >> Yeah, I mean, just like I said, I'm just trying to go out there and be consistent. You know, we have talented guys on that perimeter, you know, and and the and the backfield. And you know, just giving those guys opportunities, moving [snorts] the line of scrimmage and it's you know, like I said, our defensive front is really talented. Uh so, getting out there, those are game reps. And [snorts] then, you know, those are guys that paid a lot of money to play that position uh and they're really good at it. So, you know, we get great looks every single day at run, pass. So, yeah, it's been good, you know. It's not going to go one side or you know, only that day. You know, it kind of teeters back and forth. They're going to make some plays, but we got to respond and make some back. So, that's just kind of how it's been since the pass came on. >> Last year, when you guys seemed to like come together as a unit, >> [cough] >> wins stacking up and things like that, do you feel like coming into this camp that there's a good confidence level as a base and now you continue to grow that and get better and better? >> Yeah, I think the confidence comes knowing that, you know, the guys that we have on this team. Everybody believes in each other and also, you know, we're in the same systems, you know, for the second year going. Uh, so it's, you know, a lot less thinking. Uh, you know, OTAs, I felt like, you know, last year when I got here it was installed and it taken more time. This year we are kind of unable to, you know, just hit the ground running uh from where we left off. You know, we added in a few new guys, so, you know, we had to teach them, but you know, for the most part we just hit the ground running. I feel like that's how we've been doing it. Uh, and now I feel like that gives you a, you know, sense of confidence uh just with the familiarity of what we're trying to do and trying to get done. >> What have you seen um from Braden Swenson, Elijah Ponder from last year to this year? >> Yeah, they're both really good players. Uh, they both, you know, have done a good job at practice. Uh, you know, I played with Swenson in college. Uh, very familiar with each other. I'm just I'm proud of him. Ponder's, you know, done great things. You know, he worked his tail off in the off season. Was one of the off season award winners and you know, I I love getting to go against them cuz they're faster guys uh off the edge and just being able to get those reps against them. But, yeah, they're I think they're both going to help us this year a lot. >> What have you seen about how Jared Wilson is adapting to his new role at center. >> Looks natural. Looks natural. Uh, I think, you know, it it's been good to see that, you know, he's having fun. You can tell that's what he's comfortable with. He's running the show. He's doing great job communicating and everything like that. So, I'm just excited to see where he can take it during the season. >> Will you know that familiarity is the biggest difference in year two, right? But, in terms of your day-to-day, what's um what's the biggest difference between how you go about your business now and your preparation versus last year? I don't know. Like, I mean, I I just feel like, you know, you kind of said the familiarity. I know what to expect now. You know, I know what it takes to win and play at a high level in this league and then what stuff that can get you hurt. Uh and I don't know. Just trying to be, like I said, more consistent. Not be, you know, not make rookie mistakes, you know, as you would as a rookie and just, you know, try to be a guy out front that they can count on uh and help lead and help lead our room. >> What are some of those rookie mistakes you are looking to avoid? >> Yeah, I mean, just Yeah, I mean, no, whenever you're a rookie, I mean, you know, it's just a lot of information and things like that that can stack up on you in the training camp and, you know, it's nice not having that this year. >> Good. >> Romeo, what's the uh >> What's your process been like so far? You're learning and getting more comfortable on a daily basis with the offense, with Drake, everything you guys are doing. >> Um I mean, obviously, it's a grind to everything. I think the process has been really good. And I love where I am. I love where our team is. I love the intensity of camp practices, things of that nature. And yeah. Things are going really good. >> What's the learning process like in an offense like this where not only do you have to be on the same page as the quarterback, but there's also a lot on your plate in terms of reacting to the picture that you get from the defense? I mean that's a that's a pretty that's a really good question. Uh I mean obviously like I said before just to piggyback off of it it's a it's a process to everything so it just you know, having conversations with the quarterback number one and number two just you know, picking up the installs and just the you know, nuances to this offense so I mean I mean long story short is it's been pretty good. And I just look forward to the day-to-day grind so. >> Romeo, what's your studying process like? Are you a flash cards guy? What what's your process? >> Yeah, I mean I do I do I do uh flash cards pretty often. sometimes I'll just you know take a photo of the concept and then just draw it up on my own. I mean kind of the same thing but you know, I just try to use my memory as much as I can so that I don't you know, play slow. Just go out there and play fast so. >> So you said you love where you're at. How much more comfortable are you feeling day eight of camp you know, as opposed to maybe when you were you know, drinking out of the fire hose in spring? >> Uh yeah, I mean I'm really comfortable. Um you know just uh you know, picking off the OC's brain, Drake's brain. Um just being around the other guys in the room who's been in this offense. I know Max been a part of this offense for quite some time. Um you know, DeMario being under coach McDaniels and Kyle and all those other guys so I mean in the end I know those guys have helped me out when it really came down to it. And our ultimate goal is just to come back with that Lombardi and just go out there and play fast, so. >> Are you Are you a trash talker or do you leave that to the other receivers? >> I leave that to them. You know, if I mean, maybe every here and there, yeah, but it's just not part of my game. It's never been my game since I started playing football. And I would stay very true to who I am. Thank you. >> What makes Josh McDaniels' offense so unique? And how different is it from the the install that you had in Green Bay? I think just being more reactive to say. I mean obviously being in Green Bay, the situation was different because it wasn't as many veterans in our room. So, that played a humongous role just in our process and just how we went about things and um you know, being under McDaniels, I know he's stayed true to this offense for a really long time. Um obviously having time, you know, and Julian and Gronk and all those other guys who's played a huge part in this offense and it just comes down to a high amount of confidence and yeah. >> Is there a lot of film that's being shown of his old Patriot team? >> Uh yeah. Yeah, I mean it just it just shows that, you know you know, this is a pretty solid offense and it's just there's evidence to it, so. >> You mentioned that uh Drake has been a resource for you in learning the playbook. Just what does that kind of look like and how do you feel like your chemistry with him on the field has developed? >> It's growing. It's growing. I mean, and you know, this is like like I said, it's a day-to-day grind. It takes a certain amount of trust. And you know, I'm glad to be around a guy like Drake. He's a leader, he's poised. Um you know, and just a great guy to be around. >> Last one. The competition in the wide receiver room, and how do you push each other to get better? >> I mean, just That's a good question. Just, you know, just set set the standard high. You know what I You know what I mean? Like just fortunate to be around guys like A.J. and Mack who's got a ton of experience and like I said, just skillful players and Keyshawn and and DeMario and Kyle, like it's just, you know, it just keeps us you know, well detailed in everything that we do. And just making sure that we stay on our P's and Q's, so. >> Thanks, Robin. >> No problem. >> Appreciate you guys. >> Thank you. >> All right, y'all. >> Hey, Drake. How are you? >> I'm glad you got the ball over the fence the other day. >> I didn't mean for that to go that far. >> [laughter] >> Maybe just a good place to start there. I mean, just get the pick. I know I'm taking you back to another practice, but just um how you How did it How did that unfold? unfold from your view, and how nice is it to come up it was definitely a great feeling. I mean, just trusting the process and the scheme and the technique. Uh it's something that we talk about all the time. It's just like do your job. And um I mean, you can do your job a million times and just, you know, be in a good spot and like never get the ball your way, but I mean, we have a really good quarterback, so like he really makes bad decisions. But uh I mean, in that situation, I mean, I just think I was able to be in a good spot and like get rewarded and make a good play. But uh the defense needed that. We were talking about getting more takeaways at practice and getting more turnovers. And I think it was just like an energizer at practice, and then I kicked the ball. >> Yo, you wear a lot of hats in this defense. You play safety, but also some of the sliding at linebacker. How are you trying to continue to add to your plate and take another step in this defense? >> Uh I think I'm just trying to continue to be consistent and continue to prove to the staff that I can wear many hats and also like do them as equally as like as the other. I mean, just play safety the same way, play nickel, dime, like wherever they put me, I'm going to play it to my fullest potential no matter what. And I just want them to like be able to trust me and build confidence that no matter where they put me at that I will continue be a helpful part of our defense. >> I know it's your two, so everyone's a little bit more familiar with the playbook, but what's what's different about the system this year as far as you can tell? We see a little bit more three safety at practice. >> Uh, one thing that I'll definitely feel like just being year two in the system, I feel like everything is a lot slower for myself speaking. I mean, versus we're doing like similar things and making adjustments and stuff like that, but at the end of the day there's still things that like, you know, we were running last year and stuff like that. But, uh, for me just I feel like I'm more comfortable in it. I think a lot of guys are more comfortable in it because like, you know, it's it's difficult for everybody like just adjusting the new things, especially if you've never seen it like played a different scheme or anything like that. But, uh, I feel like guys are running around and like a lot faster just because like, especially the guys who were here with us last season, just because like they have that experience in this scheme and everything's a lot more comfortable and like now guys can communicate a lot better, which is a big part of our defense is communication, so I feel I definitely feel like just being here in this system for like my second season, I feel a lot a lot more comfortable. >> What have you been able to learn from Trevon Diggs so far? >> How to get the football. I mean, I mean, he is he's like such an impressive guy. Uh, he's a better man, but I mean, he came in week one and he's asking our coaches like and challenging them about like why we doing things and how is this going to help us get the football, which as a young player it's like, you know, you're a defensive back, you always want the football, but like hearing that that's his process no matter what he's doing is how am I going to get the football in this? Like, what can I do to put myself in a better position to get the football? It's something that I like took a step back. I was like, "Hmm, I don't think I ever really thought like that." I'm I always see ball, get ball, but he's like he's really breaking it down in a in a science type of way of where am I going to be and how am I putting myself in a position to get the football? Cuz if I can't get the football, I'm not doing my job. So, I mean he's just like you can tell he's a vet. You can tell like why he led the league in interceptions last season. And I mean, I'll look forward to working with him like getting ready for the season cuz I feel like all he's going to do is help me be a better player and help everybody around me be a better player. >> What's one thing you've learned from him about having like being able to get the football or trying to get the football? >> I mean it's all about your eyes. Like, having your eyes in the right place. Looking at the quarterback, though studying the quarterback. Like, studying his hitch. Like, when he's like where's his release point. Just like, you know, how strong he is. Like, the concepts that they run. I mean, he he does it in such a like a way that's natural to him that when I first like saw him doing it, I was like, "I need to learn this." Like, all I'm going to do is get better by being near him. >> Have you been able to take that into the field yet? >> I feel like I have. Uh especially with like middle of the field play. Like, whether you're a post or you know, you're somewhere like too high where like he's really good about his feet and not covering like grass for no reason as we say. Like, he's going to put himself in a position where he's doing his job, but where he also can be aggressive and go like jump the route. >> As a defensive back, uh has Drake for you gotten more difficult to read this year um as opposed to this time last year? >> I feel like he has. I mean, I feel like he's always getting better and like he's always getting better at like calling us out where we show something too soon. He's already making the check like where we're like, "Oh, well, now we got to deal with that." Because he like he just knows what he's doing. I mean, I I think that's a testament of like his preparation. I think that's a testament of how well he played last season and having a chip on his shoulder that he wants to be the best and continue to like show why he feels like he is the best. And so like I mean, I definitely feel like Drake is like making it a lot harder for us, but also making us better because like we're learning from him. >> Is he changing more plays at the line this year? >> Uh I don't I can't really speak to that. I don't think he is, but I can just tell he's a lot more like in my opinion like like you know, slower in his like approach where he sees things slow like slower. >> What's the line between trying to put yourself in play make positions and be aggressive, but not over committing or putting yourself in a bad spot? >> Uh I think it's for me about just trusting the scheme and like trusting like the playbook and like knowing where I'm allowed to be and uh asking a lot of questions about like you know, if I do this, how's that going to affect everybody else and like knowing where the rest of my teammates are around me and like just knowing where your help is at if you have help. Just like being comfortable knowing that I can be aggressive and knowing that like I have guys around me who are going to help me. It like definitely helps you like get in the head space of like I'm going to go get this football. >> Yeah, in the first week or so I think you guys as DBs had maybe like four or five pass breakups in teams. And you mentioned the pick being an energizer. What was it like in the room with Kevin, Mr. Go get the ball all the time when it was just slower in that department to start camp? >> I mean after those first few practices he brought us up and he was like we're going to like we need to take aways today. Before we went to any competitive like team activity, he said we need more takeaways. We're going to go out here and we're going to go get the football. Like forget what everybody else is talking about. Forget what the coaches talk about. This is our team. This is our defensive backfield and like it's up to us to go get it because the coaches can't play for us and and I told them I was like I I like I thought that was great to hear just because like he set the tone for us that day. >> Is that the day you got pick? >> Thank you, guys. >> Appreciate y'all. >> How we doing? >> Good. How are you? >> How would that How would you just describe today's practice sort of going inside? How it unfolded? >> Uh it was a good day, uh competitive. Um hot in there, but it was good. >> What about the footing in there? How would you describe the footing? >> [snorts] >> It was a little slick, but it was fun. >> How much do you adjust? >> Um you know, what you do when you get when you're in a little slippery area? >> Uh just keep your footing, be athletic, I guess. >> What do you make of the run game overall? I know you're in early camp. Lanes aren't as always open as they are later in camp, but you guys had a pretty good day, it seemed like, today. >> Oh yeah, they've been great. I mean, offensive line working hard, defensive line, everybody's working hard, doing their job, so uh I mean, it's just up to us to up to us to uh find our gaps, make a read. Every play is different, so um yeah. >> How do you feel like you're progressing as you go from OTAs through camp to where you're at now physically, uh mentally? >> Uh I feel like I'm doing all right, staying on track. Um it's been a minute, so I'm just trying to get back in the swing of things and uh stay focused and do my job. >> There are guys who spend uh a year away from the game and they come back and they say, "Well, you know, I learned this about myself as a player or as a person." Did you pick up anything along the way where you think that you you can apply it moving forward into this year as lessons on or off the field? >> Yeah, I think the the biggest thing was uh I just got a year to learn and kind of uh grow as a as a person and in the offense, just uh take a step back and watch and really learn what it's like to be a pro and uh uh work, you know. >> What were some of those things that you picked up? >> Uh like scheme. Uh just the overall offense, I guess, you know. >> Being in a room with Jam and Stevenson for over a year now, given all his experience in the league. >> Um, Mondre is uh super hard working and uh just kind of how he kind of flows through a game and just his uh fluidity. Yeah. >> How have we seen you work on some of the kick return stuff? Just how comfortable are you with that? How much of adjustment is this kick return setup from what you had to deal with in college? >> I'm pretty comfortable kick returning. I did it all throughout college, so uh it's just very different. It's a lot faster and a lot of things happen in pretty quick and bigger bodies, bigger people, so. >> You have any thought like the different the rule setup, the full field versus >> it's fine. It's cool. It's exciting, yeah. >> You mentioned trying to find your rhythm. I mean, do you feel rust? >> I did for sure at the beginning. Uh I think anybody would, but uh I think it's coming along nice. >> So, you and Terrell and Miles and Jam are all competing. How do you guys push each other? >> Uh we're pretty close, I'd say as a room. Uh it's pretty like friendly competition. We all try to help each other and uh if we see anything, we're always talking, communicating and uh just like we want the best for each other. >> With that closeness in the room, what kind of example does Thomas Brown set and how close have you guys gotten since you've been here? >> What's that? Can you repeat the question? >> Uh with the tightness of the room, how much does Thomas Brown kind of set the example in that way and how is your relationship grown since you got here? >> Who's 20 Deuce? >> Oh yeah, he he's the he's the head of the snake in the running back room. Like he's uh he pushes us all and he's like very technical, very detailed, so I appreciate coach Deuce and uh he really pushes us, yeah. >> The first preseason game of the year is coming up and you got injured last year. What is what are sort of the emotions coming up as you head into the your first game back? >> Yeah, I'm just super excited to uh be out there and compete, show my stuff. >> With the last year, obviously I know you would have preferred to be on the field, but what was in the role that you had the kind of coolest thing you did in and around the team? >> Um just to be be able to be here, be present and uh kind of just watch, you know, learn. Just be around the sport, be around the Patriots and how far we went was awesome, so it's cool to watch that. >> And Land, had you had been injured in the past prior to coming here? Is that sort of the first major setback that you had in your career? >> I mean, it's football, you know, injuries happen, but uh yeah, that would probably be the more major major one. >> And how did you how did you feel like mentally it it challenged you and and how did you attack it? >> Um head on, I guess, you know, just kind of just having that discipline to get in there every every single day rehab and uh just focus on getting healthy. >> Who helped you? I would imagine like you had some support around you to help you get through. Who were some of the people that >> Here? whether it's here or personally. >> Um the trainers, the training staff, they did a great job just uh getting me back right and getting me healthy. >> How much did you learn in terms of growing in a year mentally that you've been able to take on to the field and kind of match that physically in in the pro game? >> Um I would say learning a lot of the more of the like a defensive structure and um just how things move and like just the speed of how quick you got to think as a pro athlete. >> What's the process been like when it comes to protections of actually learning it and studying the playbook versus actually translating it to the field with everything that's on your plate? >> A lot of moving parts. >> It's uh it's easy to look at something on a piece of paper and understand it, but then when the bullets are flying, I mean, you just uh kind of got to settle down and uh go through your rules. >> How do you feel like you've acclimated to a few more blitz-heavy practices in the past few days. >> Um I feel like I've done it all right. Yeah, there's always room for improvement. >> Last one. >> Do you still kind of feel like a rookie? Does it still sort of feel like your first year, in a way? >> Um just getting a little bit cut short a little bit in terms of uh playing time, but uh I don't see it that way. I got to step up and do my job. >> Thanks for coming in.

title: 2 minutes at training camp: A.J. Brown, Christian Gonzalez battle heats up on Day 8
text: All right, the rain couldn't keep the Patriots from practicing here Monday, day eight of training camp, but it could push them indoors where they were for about 2 hours. And this was a spirited, highly competitive practice. Wish it could have been there. But we have a full recap here for you on 2 minutes of training camp. We'll start with Drake May. Got to start with the quarterback. Eight of 14 overall, which was again a competitive red zone practice. a lot of throwing, some running, which is a little bit better. Uh, but that's eight of 14, including one drop. Of course, you want to know about AJ Brown. Look, three catches on five targets and one dislocated thumb, which happened early in practice in a rep against Christie Gonzalez, who we had a lot of battles with. They ended up splitting those battles, both between one-on- ones and full team drills. May's last two throws, both going in their direction. First one, Gonzo gets a hand on, bats it down, AJ comes up with the second catch. His three catches overall though were second most on the team today. Matt Collins coming out of nowhere to be everywhere. Five catches, three touchdowns for him. One drop in the back corner. He threw his helmet at that point. But the bottom line is it's been not a different receiver every single day. This was the Kan Booty show for a while, but the depth of this position is in a better place than it's been I don't know 10 to 15 years. Booty of course had another spectacular grab that actually ended practice here today. He ended up giving up two catches. Would have had a third uh if it weren't dropped by Matt Collins, but also one good rep against AJ Brown. He only gave up one catch on three targets and just like Prunty saw some reps with the starters where you can tell the Patriots coaching staff is really trying to cycle through that depth and say, "Okay, we got Gonzo." Hard to tell because they can't touch Drake May. I'm not sure whether he would have been in or not, but that was one of the successful. text: So Scott says the other day that he wants to make sure that you're you're angrier and meaner this year. Um, you know, I'm I'm about football, you know what I'm saying? About uh what I do on the field and um, how I carry myself on the field and off the field as well. Um, but at the same time um, you know, I'm going go out there and do do what I need to do um, at at the end of the day. >> What are your impressions of number 52? >> Number 52, that boy. See ball get ball. He's going to run fast. He's going to hit hard and he's going to be around the ball at all time. So I think that's like probably the best way to describe our >> the first day of pads is really about evaluating the run game. How did you think you guys ran the ball on the defense? >> Yeah, I think we did well. I think we did well. We ran behind our pads. Um we we got what we can get. Um obviously first day of pass is always going to be a little messy. Um you know, everybody's excited. everybody's um you know ready to get out there and actually you know uh hit you know and be physical. So I think that today was a good valuation of where we're at and like I said tomorrow we going to take a step in the right direction. >> What enables him to get ball >> say it again. >> You said he see ball get ball. What enables him to get ball? >> I mean [snorts] that's just him. That's who he is. You know what I'm saying? Like he's he's a dog. Like you don't really have to um say much, you know, to him. You know, you really just put him on the football field, let him work. Um like I said, I think a lot of his stuff is raw um and natural. I think he's it's God-given. So with the right, you know, coaching, um I think that like I said, he can he can be all world. >> When you hear Harbaugh say, "We're going to be physical. We're going to run. We're going to run. We're going to run." What does that do for you guys in terms of there's a lot on your shoulders. >> Yeah. I mean, I really don't think it's a lot on our shoulders to be honest. Just cuz um we want the ball. You know what I'm saying? We want to run the ball. I think if you look at at Howard Ball and where he's been and all the running backs that he's used and really his whole career, they all been successful. So when he came here, we was all excited. you know, you got a a running coach that's coming to you. So, you know, as a running as a running back room, we excited to to for him to be here, to be honest. Um, obviously, you got other coaches, coach, um, Coach Ro, he's there there's so many coaches on the coaching staff that has had, um, either head coaching jobs or offering the coordinator jobs. So, like we have a lot of, um, people around us that has a lot of knowledge that's doing that's really given off to us. So, u, we was excited to really have coach Harbar come. So, really, we don't see it as um, a lot of weight on our shoulders. Like I said, we see it as opportunity. You know what I'm saying? opportunity to show ourselves, opportunity to um really show the NFL, you know, who we who we are and what we can be. >> And what have you observed about number 65, the other first round pick? >> Uh he's very silent. He don't say much. He don't say much. U field. >> Yeah. Yeah. I know. I know. I'm I was getting there. He like I said, he's very silent. He don't say much, but um when you're on the field, man, you can definitely feel his presence. Um he's going he's going to move people. Like you said, uh when when he got drafted, he's he's out there ready to die. You know what I'm saying? That's that's that's who he is um as a person. I think we have a really good offensive line in general. >> You just said show the NFL who we are and what we can be. So, what can you be? >> Yeah. I mean, I think we can be a premier um running back group. Um, not just me, not just Scott. I think we can be a premier running back group. Um, you know, when you're talking about, uh, you know, there's running back rooms around the NFL. Um, I think that you have, um, you know, a group of people in our room, me, Scott, Motor, uh, E Gray, Turbo, like we all can go in there and execute. Um, I think that's that's what makes a successful room. >> You can't be happy with the the way the offense performed today, right? >> Say it again. the penalties, all the penalties on offense. What why do you think it's been so effective through the years? >> Um, I think he has his schemes to be honest. He he schemes up is so different. like I'm um sitting there in awe really each and every time he gets up to talk. He's very detailed. Um he knows exactly what he's talking about. If he says it's going to be this way versus a certain look, I promise you go out there and that look is going to end up exactly what he says. So um he's been around the game. He's been around winning teams um college level two when he's at Stanford, he said he I think he said he ran a ball like uh one one guy like 40 40 carries one game for like 200 300 yards. You know what I'm saying? So like he's been around the game a long time. Um he has the the stats to to back it up. Um, like I said, and he's very knowledgeable. So, uh, Coach Ro, I mean, you can't really say say enough about him. Um, like I said, he's a good coach, great coach with a lot of knowledge. When >> you say, you mean just like schematically, like the way he gets into >> Yeah. Yeah. Like the scheme. So, the schemes that he's that he's imp uh implementing um throughout our offense. Um, like obviously he's the run game coordinator, so he's he's up there telling us um being very detailed. There's no really no gray gray area. Um, and it's not just one way to run, you know, the ball. He's calling the same run but out of different, you know, formations, different motions. Um, you know, pullers, different pullers, you know, just there a whole bunch of different stuff going on. But again, he's making it very simple and easy for us to learn. >> We we talked a lot to coach Naggie and Coach Callahan and all of that about how many different coaches with all that experience that they have. And I guess the question is, are you getting one message from from this group at all? Is it is it consistent? you know, cohesive message that you're getting from this from this staff. >> Yeah, Coach Nags, um, shoot and all the position coaches, like they all obviously meet every day and they all come together. Um, his word is elegant, simplicity, like everything's supposed to be elegant. It's supposed to look complicated to the defense, but, you know, simple to us as an offense. So, when we go out there, we're all working on one accord. We're all um, you know, working together and making explosive plays. Like, we want to be explosive. We want to move the ball down the field. Um, and I think the way we're doing that is is being simple but also u making the defense think a little bit. >> Last one. >> This offense is seems like it's requiring a lot more of Jackson Dart or a lot different stuff than it was of Jackson Dart last year. I'm curious how you see him adapting to it. >> Yeah, I mean as a quarterback he has so much on his on his plate, man. Um, and like I said, last year it's a different offense than we're running, you know, right now. So, he, like I said, he's adapting right now, but he's doing a great job. He's a great leader, man. He's a great friend. Um, and like I said, for Jackson, I just I I'm um seeing daily um improvements each and every day. Obviously, you make mistakes. We all make mistakes, you feel me? But when you come out the next day, it's a clean slate. He's um like he's a great quarterback, man. Like, he's young. So, you got to understand that there's going to be um some stuff in there that you got to work out, you know, between a young quarterback. But overall, man, Jackson has been out there great leader, great quarterback, seeing the ball, throwing the ball, making uh making plays with his feet. Like, he's doing everything uh that's asked of him, plus some. Um, so and obviously you got Jamus too. Jamus is a great I know everybody don't really talk about Jamus, but Jameus is a great leader, man. He's a great teammate. He's always there. Um, he's always helping out twos, threes, even the ones, man. Like he's always picking us up. So, um, I think we with Jamus and Jackson, um, we have great quarterback room.

title: Harbaugh's Camp is going to be COMPLETELY Different
text: So, there's not a ton to talk about, obviously. Um the Giants did start training camp today, per se. They met in New Jersey at about 12:30 and then they went to West Virginia. And that's really all we have. So, if you have any questions in the chat, uh make sure to ask them. We'll do our best to answer as many as we can. Um but we'll just start with this. Obviously, we know John Harbaugh, his training camp is going to be completely different than Brian Daboll's. Brian Daboll never practiced more than two days in a row. I believe the Giants schedule is they practice four days, have a day off, and then they practice six in a row, if I'm not mistaken. I know it's 10 of the first 11. I I think that. >> 10 out of 11, yeah. >> Put it up. Uh Adrianna, do you think this is a good thing or a bad thing? Because obviously, you practice a lot. If somebody gets injured, you know, people are going to be like, "Oh, John Harbaugh's too tough on the guys." What is your thought about John Harbaugh's training camp as opposed to the way Brian Daboll ran it? >> Well, the Giants also lost three players to soft tissue injuries in May when they were doing nothing. So, the Giants are always going to be injured. Uh we've seen it happen year after year in training camp. I mean, I've been at a ton of training camps. Guys go down left and right when they're not tackling, they're not wearing pads, they're doing god knows what. So, you know, I know we talked about when I think it was Zay Flowers made that comment of like, "So happy with Harbaugh gone, we're not going to be doing padded practices late in the season. That's why we had all these injuries." I mean, the Giants have always always been injured. So, if there are an uptick in injuries because of these back-to-back practices, we'll find out soon enough. But I I [snorts] think that it's the right move for this team. This team is very young. There's a lot of mistakes that need to be fixed. There's a lot that needs to be improved upon. And I also think that there were a lot of players last year that were done with the Brian Daboll way of doing things. It very obviously was not working. And I think you look at the lot of lot of the veterans like Dexter Lawrence and Brian Burns like guys Andrew Thomas who were having really great years for the most part on their own. I know Dex's wasn't that great, but they all had relatively good careers under Brian Daboll, but the team was still losing week in and week out. And I think you get to a point where you're like, well, the we're doing is not working. So we need to switch it up. And I think a lot of them are going to welcome it. I think there are guys who need that type of instruction and I just think at this point you got to try something different and see if it works. And you know, like I said, injuries are going to happen. We all know they get injured all the time doing God knows what whether they're on the field or not on the field. So um so if you don't I don't know. I don't really think it's going to lead to an increase in injuries. I think if anything it should make Giants fans feel like, hey, week one, we should see a pretty good product out there. A a team that has practiced, has been disciplined, and has hopefully learned from their mistakes because if they make mistakes, they're going to get yanked off the field. There's not going to be any of this, oh, well, you can make the same mistake time and time again and and we'll just brush it off and get over it. That's unacceptable these days. Um and like I said, I really think this is what this team needs at this point where they're at. >> Anthony, what's your feeling on the difference between the way Daboll ran camp and the way Harbaugh is going to run it? >> I think one of my biggest criticisms of Brian Daboll over the last couple of years has been the country club style of practice and training camp that he's had. Um in particular, I do remember crashing out on the Fireside Giants podcast about Daniel Jones not taking preseason snaps a couple years ago because I thought that was insane. Like you had guys like Josh Allen out there and Patrick Mahomes and all Lamar Jackson, all these guys were taking snaps in the first preseason game and Daniel Jones wasn't and I just thought it was not a reflection of Daniel Jones, it was a reflection of Brian Daboll and his fear of putting the players out there and his fear of injuries and how that actually holds him back. The Giants in my opinion over the last couple of years were a more injured team than the rest of the teams because they were afraid of the injuries, because they didn't practice and prepare their bodies properly. I think the teams that actually do go out there, they put the pads on, they practice and they kind of put that work in to acclimate their body to being hit consistently, to actually, you know, feeling the grinds of playing football, those are the teams that stay healthy throughout the course of the season and not the teams that are lackadaisical, that lays around and don't prepare their bodies properly. So, I think John Harbaugh is going to have this team prepare their bodies properly. I think they're going to be hitting each other, I think they're going to be physical in practice and I think that's going to make them first of all a healthier team, second of all a more prepared team when the games are actually being played. The Giants have been terrible the first week the first month of the season all throughout the Brian Daboll tenure. Like even when they had the 2022 season where they made the playoffs, they came out of the gates really sluggish in Tennessee. They looked like in that first half. They turned it on in the second half and Saquon Barkley had some magical moment at the end and they won the game and reminder, they actually got lucky in that game on a missed field goal at the end of the game. So, the Giants were not a good football team in the first month of the season any of Brian Daboll's years. That needs to change and hopefully it should considering the track record of John Harbaugh and how good he's been in September, but he's been so good in September throughout his 18 years of being a head coach because he actually puts that work in in July and in August and he actually puts his players through the grind and through the process of preparing their bodies and being fully sharp when the week one kickoff happens. So, I'm confident that this Giants team will be better in week one than they have been in years past because of John Harbaugh and because they're not going to have a lackadaisical summer. >> Chris, what what about what's your opinion about the difference between Daboll's training camp and the way Harbaugh is going to run his training camp? >> Yeah, I mean, we haven't seen it yet, but I mean in terms of hit you know, history and what we've heard in terms of 10 out of 11 practices, the story lines coming out of the Ravens was that he ran hard practices. Like Audray on a set, I think it was Zay Flowers if I'm not mistaken who was celebratory after he left because he knew he knows it's going to be easier training camps. Kind of like Anthony just said and like we talked about last week on the show, you look at Harbaugh's track record, the team under him has a over a 67% winning percentage in the month of September in an 18-year sample size. That's a large sample size with the Baltimore Ravens. He puts a big precedent on having his team as prepared as they possibly can be to start the regular season and it's so important in the NFL to do that. We look at the stat every year, you win your first week, the chances you make in the playoff is so much higher than if you drop week one. So, Harbaugh realizes that and it's why he's going to have this team prepared. And I don't know how you could be upset as a fan, you should be excited as a fan if that were the case. Football is a game of injuries. They they could happen in any which way. You go back to week one. Andrew Thomas got hurt, I believe it was against the Dallas Cowboys when we lost 40 to nothing. Barkley got hurt early in the season several times. So, it's like it is what it is. Like injuries are going to happen and you have to have your team as prepared as possible to be able to overcome those injuries. I'm sure if a player gets hurt in training camp, people are there's going to be a narrative that John Harbaugh is running the players too hard, but at the end of the day, the guy's one of the greatest coaches in the history of the NFL. This is a young team. He's trying to set a culture with this team and he's trying to get them off on the right foot. So, I I welcome it. title: Nick Sirianni on Week 2 of Training Camp
text: Morning [snorts] Nick. Uh how are the meetings changed in terms of like run and pass and do you do you have them together because uh of the difference in how they are so important to each other when you marry them >> in like as far as team meeting or like unit meetings? >> I think previously the run meetings were held separately a lot of them. um >> that was uh you know that was at times in the run game planning but mostly it's always been um when you install you're in here together and naturally it's the same it's very similar as far as [snorts] you know you'll install something there'll be a break and then the offensive line doesn't need to sit in for like the pass drawing. Um and what what Shawn just shows a very good overall view of the offense. He it just when he comes up here, it's just he has everybody's attention, is able to talk to every position.
