Is it different when you're doing a a new type of system? How much of that changes? >> You know again like I said it's very there's a lot of similarities of of how we're installing. Um, I wouldn't say it's, you know, we're in here longer or shorter than than what we have been in the past. Uh, it's just important that all the information gets passed on and that and that we as coaches do a great job of of making sure that the job description is clear um on every every play, on every detail. Um, and and I believe our guys have been doing a really good our offensive staff has been doing a really good job of that. Sticking with the offense in this first full week of training camp, what does a successful week look like to you under Shawn with not only the returners, but some of the rookies, um, Lemon, etc.? >> Yeah, when you're in training camp, it it's so important to put everything out of out of view except for that that particular day. And in training camp, there's going to be back good back and forth between your your offense and your defense. Um there's going to be good back and forth between your corners and your wide receivers and your linebackers and your tight ends. Um and so you're looking for what I'm looking for as far as I guess to say success of a a day is are we when we come in here and we watch as a team um are we getting better at the at the little things? Are we getting better at our fundamentals? Are we taking steps? Are there be, you know, are we taking steps with our things that require no talent? Our ball security. Um, when I say require no talent, just everybody being on the same page at all times. So, you're just looking for little progressions each and every day. It's a it's a marathon. Um, and some days you're going to it's going to look like this and some days it's going to look like this. And it's never it's never just a true line. And I know we all want it to be that way, especially as as coaches, but you know, progression looks very feels like this, but it, you know, it's up a little bit, back a little bit, up a little bit, back a little bit, and you're just trying to get a little bit better each day and and continue that mode of of you getting yourself better. >> What have they noticed about uh Chris Cooper's approach to his job, knowing that so many of those players have only heard one voice in their careers? Yeah, you know, I think again just making sure that his he is very deliberate of his um um job description. Um and I think he's done a nice job of that. Uh he can only be himself and um and do, you know, and coach the way he knows how to coach and I hired him, you know, for a reason. We were really impressed by him and we know he's a phenomenal coach. uh and he's doing a good job of, you know, building relationships with, uh, his players. He's doing a good job of teaching his players. Um, got, you know, obviously I I talk to guys all the time and, you know, I know those guys think very highly of him, um, and have been really impressed, uh, you know, early on here in camp and through the OTAAS. So, you know, building trust is the most important thing. And you build trust by your daily habits. You build trust by, you know, consistently doing the right things. And I I think that's those those are the things that he's been doing. >> Landon acknowledged that he he came back prematurely from surgery last off season. What do what do you think is the organization's responsibility in protecting players from themselves? And have you guys implemented any changes to, you know, ensure further protection for them? >> Yeah, I think we've we always uh first and foremost are going to put the players safety uh at the forefront. Um and that you know we know guys are going to always want to come back uh you know before and that's why we have doctors. That's why we have all the doctors that we have the training staff that we have and we're always thinking about the long-term health of the player and what's best for the player. Um, and so you know that's all and you know at times you're like man I really want this guy out there to you know in this game because he's going to help us win this game. But it's always been our organizational philosophy to take care of the guys um and do what's best for them um as you know to make sure they're stepping on the field you know when when they can be stepping on the field when they're where they're able to. We've only seen the early installations the offense, but what have you seen in in terms of how in the passing game things might uh open up more over the middle? >> Um, you know, again, just early on, obviously, um, there's a progression to everything of how we how we install. Um, I think Sean's got a good progression of of how he's went about it. Um, we'll be in day what four as far as out there on practice today. So obviously each and every day you guys will see more uh things because each and every day there's a new install through the you know first 10 10 or so uh installs that doesn't necessarily mean like today is more of a review day actually but um because they're coming off of an off day and we and their walkthrough was in their install meeting was two days ago. So this will be a little bit more of a review of the some of the things that you've seen. Um, but yeah, again, like I said, um, you know, we're going to we're we're working different things, working different concepts. The guys have done a good job of, uh, learning the new terminology. Sometimes I I compare that to learning a new learning a new language. Um, and um, they've studied hard and I know our our doing a good job as far as limiting the the mental errors and and going out there being able to perform. So, um, I think it's been a good start. you observe from Mai Lemon and Eli Ster so far as they early in their NFL careers and what do you need to see out of them in this stage to show that you know they're making progress and they're at the right track. >> Yeah, I think again you're just looking for improvement in each and everything. I think both of those guys have a great skill set. I think you're seeing uh some of that skill set and then there's still some things that that you know aren't in yet that you're going to see more of um to even show show more of them. But, you know, I love the way Mai goes about his business and, you know, little things like his effort in the run game are awesome. Um, he's got really good quickness that you're seeing. Um, and maybe you don't get to see it every time where he catches the football and and where he shows great quickness, but I sure as heck see it on the film um when he's away from the play or the ball's not going to him or the coverage takes it away. And then I think Eli has a really good feel for, you know, the zone of where where to sit in zones and how to how to get open versus different types of zone coverage. And we know that his athletic ability um will make him, you know, have ability to shake free on third down when it is man coverage. Um and so because he's quick, he's fast, you know, he's explosive. But what I've been impressed with with him is just his ability to kind of read defenses and find the areas of the zone where he needs to sit and be at the right spot at the right time. >> Hey Nick, you guys you guys Nick Nick, you guys have never thrown a ton to the backs. We've seen it a lot out there these first few days. What place does that have in this offense and is something you'd like to do more? >> Yeah, I mean I think that all just depends on the the style of uh or kind of the mode of offense you're in at that particular time. It's different thrown to a back obviously when you're in the gun. um when he's when he's at home sometimes it's more of a check down uh of you know Jaylen going through his progression or Tanner going through his progression or Andy or Cole going through their progressions and finding the back. Um, and so, you know, obviously we have backs that we feel very strongly that they know they they're really good at running the ball, but we also know that, you know, Saquon's had a lot of production in this league um with the pass game. And Will's had, you know, production in college in the past game. And so, we're we're uh we know we have they those guys have that skill set and it's about finding ways to to utilize that. And um but we know that those guys have the ability, but you always want to be multiple in things that you do. And um being able to, you know, throw it to tight ends, throw it to running backs, throw it to receivers, what's getting you the best matchup that particular week. And um we feel like we have good matchups across the field and we'll see how we use those those guys and exploit that week in week out. >> Early Nick, but it seems like Cole Payton has has had more practice reps than we're used to seeing from the number four quarterback. Why is that? Um, you know, again, we we really like that quarterback room. Um, my job as the head coach is to be able to provide enough reps um throughout practice, whether that's in training camp or whether that's in season to allow guys to develop. Um, I think sometimes you can get very zeroed in, especially in training camp where the ones and twos are just getting reps, especially in the season where the ones are getting reps. And I think what we've done a good job of here in the in the past is and and currently is finding ways to work our developmental guys. Um because those guys that might not be they got reps in OTAAS but now the pads come on and and you're in the season or you're in the your training camp of finding ways to get them reps whether that's in walkthroughs or whether that's in developmental periods or whether that's in with the threes uh at the end. Um, but you know, I think uh we're all excited about that quarterback room and Cole's done a nice job. Um, you know, he's he's not afraid to to rip it in there um over top of linebacker. Now, you know, he had those couple picks uh early on um and he'll learn from those and he has learned from those, but I I've liked what I've seen from him so far. >> All right. Thanks. Thanks guys.

title: Football at Four: How is The Eagles Offense Progressing in Training Camp?
text: Football for powered by the Inside the Birds podcast brought to you by the Fanatic Sports Book at Ocean Casino Resort in Atlantic City. Big screens, big bets, game day hits different at Ocean. Well, I don't know when the next concert I'm going to be getting to is. I know that there's a bunch going on. I know a guy who likes concert. Andrew Deco filming in for Mosher on a Monday edition of football at four. What's up, man? How's it going? How's the weekend? >> Good, Mike. Good to be with you. >> Yeah, brother. I know. Football back uh back to work, back to the grind. Let's uh get your observations. Let's start off with Jaylen Herz uh and this offense. Everybody wondering how he looks, how he fits in. What have you seen so far from Jaylen Herz in this new look Eagle offense? >> Yeah, I I mean it's always going to be a work in progress. It's never going to be an overnight fix. They're not going to roll out of bed and have this offense operating on all cylinders. So, it's important to keep that in mind. It's also important to keep in mind that they're going up against a tremendous defense among the NFL's elite every single day. So, it's that old adage of our iron sharpening iron. But for the first three days, I would say the better part of the first three practices, the defense bested the offense and you could see that they're a little bit behind. But I thought today told a little bit of a different story with the offense coming alive a little bit. Jaylen Herz had some really nice throws in the first day of uh of pads. Andy Dalton had a really impressive day as well. I think I think it was a little bit more balanced. Um, but it looks like he's really taken to this, you know, taken to the offense, working through some things. It's all new to him. And it's what you look for at this stage of the game is you want to see a you want to see players, you want to see that side of the ball grow and take strides forward in the right direction throughout summer, throughout training camp. So, that's what I'm looking for. Uh, I want to get your thoughts on the offensive line, Andrew, and how their role might be different this season, uh, with the new coaching staff and the new offense. >> Well, I mean, they're they're just going to be blocking differently. I mean, the angles will be different. Their their focuses and their assignments will be different. Uh, they're going laterally instead of moving uh north and south, getting vertical. Um, and so it should really accentuate their athleticism and it should also help the running backs and allow them to do some different things, unlock them, get them in the open open space and I think just overall alleviate some of the pressure from these offensive linemen and maybe preserve them a little bit more and they don't necessarily have to always adopt that grueling nature that they had to that they were you know uh beholden to um with Jeff Stoutland. that was very successful and this remains to be seen if if it's ultimately going to work but uh the results or the the reviews uh thus far have been pretty promising. >> Andrew Czech football at four uh you wrote a piece over at insidethebirds.com that all of our listeners should go check out. Uh it's about Mai Lemon and the role that he might have. So early on in this camp what uh stands out Lemon uh so far? Yeah, I think a lot of it was going into camp. There was the the school of thought and I also subscribe to that that it was going to take him a little bit of time to learn the offense knowing that he had some time. You know, he had to make up for lost time. He had the hamstring injury during the spring and what I've seen right now is the Eagles wasted little time getting him involved with the first team. He hasn't had a lot of success in terms of receptions and the volume hasn't been there, but they have been targeting him. There was a few different occasions on Saturday's practice where that they tried to get it to him. Whether it was in the red zone and there was a flag thrown on Troder Jr., whether there was a deep shot and it was a hair off a little bit too far in front of him, but he did have some a step down the field on Cooper Deene or or something like that. But I I think it is notable that they're getting him in the mix early. There's not the onboarding process. Now, what I will add is being there today, he was there for individuals, but uh I did not see him participate in any team drills. So, not exactly sure uh what's going well, you know, what the what the reason for that is, but it's something I'll be monitoring for Tuesday's practice >> right now. He had uh some hamstring issues back in the OTAAS. Is that uh is that what uh left him out the last time? Not connected or maybe connected? >> I don't know. I'm not sure. >> All right. Well, Lemon obviously um and Eli Sters, the the the tight end, uh the early part of this camp, does he look like a guy who could have a role or a bigger role uh in this offense? >> Uh he's he's gotten off to a slow start. Again, it's never a sign, you know, it's never cause for concern. Players progress at different rates, but he's clearly a little bit further down in the pecking order with tight ends. Johnny Mont is pretty comfortably the number two tight end right now. He even had a catch uh during one of the team periods earlier in practice, but Sters has been targeted. He was a targeted a couple times today and hasn't done anything really remarkable, but it's it's not something that you you sound any sort of alarm. You want to again, kind of like with the offense, you want to you want to see that the player is taking steps forward in the right direction throughout the summer. And it it's not it's it's going to take a little bit of time. You know, he's going to need a little bit of seasoning there. He's going to have to grow and evolve as a blocker and that's all part of the process. >> Andrew, uh, you wrote about Marcus Eps. I think a lot of people have questions about how big of a role he might have this season. What are we seeing early on from the veteran who, you know, they they brought him back last year late in the year and he had probably a bigger role last year than people thought he would. What are you seeing from EPS and what kind of role he might have this year? Yeah, as as far as EPS or Michael Carter II, neither player has made uh any big play. There's hasn't been a splash play yet, but they've been steady. And I think sometimes when you don't hear a safety's name, that that indicates that they're doing their job. And being where they are supposed to be. But yeah, Marcus Eps is is right now the front runner to be the safety opposite through Makuba. When the Eagles are a nickel, let's not forget that when the Eagles are in base, that will be Cooper Deene at safety. Uh with with Marcus Apps, you're you're not getting there's sort of a trade-off because you're not getting the supercharged athleticism, the the range that you might like, but you are getting someone who's fundamentally sound, who's trusted with Vic Fangio, which by the way, when he was talking about the backend communication, he mentioned how capable Marcus was in doing that. And I don't know that you need to be a superstar to be an effective safety in a Vic Fangio defense. players like Reed Blanketship and you kind of look at some of the safeties that he's worked with in his career. If you're assignment sound, if you're disciplined, if you're not a high variance player and you have a high level football intelligence, more often than not, they're going to find a way to maximize what you do well. And I think right now there's a reason why Marcus Eps is in the driver's seat there at the moment. Although, I am pretty intrigued with Michael Carter the second because of how he moves. I like him quite a bit as a nickelback with the Jets and we'll see if he's able to sort of apply some of his coverage acumen to the uh safety position. >> I like that. Uh I want to get your thoughts on Jayix Hunt because I think he's a very interesting guy. This is year number three. You take a look at um you know he was a third round pick. I think that probably is further along than they thought he would be in his first couple seasons. Where do you see him this year? Yeah, I think that's fair. I think Jix Hunt's going to be and I've said this for three, four months now because I I I could see the progress and talking to some people, you just get the sense that he is prime for a breakout. That's my 2026 defensive breakout for the Eagles. Just a a really fluid athlete, good burst, he's a more well-rounded player, and I think he's grown, and there's no coincidence that it just happens to coincide with snaps. he just needed reps and he's not too far removed from being a safety at Cornell, but you go to Cornell, you're a pretty intelligent dude. And so I think that that also helps him really just absorb his his function within the defense and be able to kind of grow and evolve his role a little bit quicker than maybe some other players were uh might have been able to with that kind of experience. So I I think the fact that he's playing opposite Jonathan Grard should help him. and they have a a very diverse group of edge rushers including Arnold Edi, Nolan Smith, and AJ Fanessa. And I think because of that, there's not any one player that you can key on. I just feel like Jay Hunt's ready to to kick the door down in year three. >> I know uh you wrote about over at insidethebirds.com that defense wins the day. U and you know, this defense is very very good. Uh, do you look at this defense right now as potentially better than the defense we saw last year? >> Yes. And you see I didn't hesitate there. It's because of the continuity. It's another year where a lot of the nucleus of this defense that ascending talent is they're playing together again for another year. You have two players in Cooper Deene and Quinan Mitchell coming off all pro honors. Then you have Jaylook Hunt who was a good player last year, but I think he's ready to be to take it that next step and become a great player this year. I believe that Jonathan Grard is a better pass rusher than Jaylen Phillips. Now, he's got to get on the field and he's going to have to work with the team because he hasn't taken any team reps since he's been a member of the Eagles, but the spirit of it, yes, that that's an upgrade there. And then you you also take into the equation that at least in theory Drew Makuba gives you more range and and upside in that safety position than maybe a Reed blanket ship. Jiad Campbell his skill set, the range, the 80in wingspan should give you more athleticism and big playability at the second level. He's probably going to sacrifice some something in terms of run support. He's not going to be Nico Dean there, but he gives you a little bit more big playability. So, yes, for all those reasons, I I think that if if everything goes according to plan, there's no reason why they shouldn't be. >> All right, we'll get you out with this one on uh you wrote about Jiad Campbell and his role possibly being bigger this season. He played well last year, but how could his role be different this year than it was last year? >> Well, I just think that you you'll probably see Vic Fano maybe give him a little bit more in terms of responsibility. teams are going to look to they're going to look to attack him in a different way now that he has a year of tape on him. He looks like he's added some muscle to his frame. I think Zack Bowen even um revealed as much. There's also the the rushing the quarterback component. Now, I don't I never viewed him as an edge rusher coming out of the draft. I viewed him as an offball linebacker and I know that I got skewered for that, but he's an offball linebacker right now. Uh, I I don't know that I I think you'll see him be able to tap into that dimension where he has that ability where he can rush the quarterback, but I think really where you're going to see him shine is in coverage where he can cover tight ends, he can cover running backs, he's just a really fluid athlete, and you don't often see players uh of his makeup as a linebacker in the NFL. I I I do believe that he's has a big season awaiting. >> All right. Well, we look forward to uh more training camp conversation this week. The birds are back. the Inside the Birds podcast. Check that out on all podcasting platforms. Andrew Deco, he's in for Mosher this week. Plus, on Thursday, we'll take a look at the NFC West, which has maybe two of the best teams in the NFC. We'll look at all of those guys later on this week with Andrew Deco here on Football at 4. Thanks, man. >> Mike, have a great day, man. >> As always, Andrew Deco covering the birds for football at 4 here on the Sports Bass Live on 973 ESPN.

title: ITB: Taking Deeper Look at Eagles First Week of Training Camp
text: [music] >> Hello again everyone and welcome to Inside the Birds. It's Kaplan and DeChellis back. So nice, we did it twice. Andrew, good to see you. >> Great to be with you, Adam. Looking forward to the show. >> Yeah, so on today's show, we're going to kind of tell you a little bit more about the standouts and what went on the first week where they only had three practices plus a walk-through. We'll get into practice schedule this week, which will be a little bit more full. A little bit a little different from last week, which is typical the first week is always lighter. And then we'll get into the transaction. They actually had their first training camp transaction. A veteran was actually released, which happened Sunday. But Andrew, first so you had the three practices. Walk-through of course the media doesn't get to see, but you saw the three practices. You saw every snap. You were you were there. You got to see it quite a bit. What were your impressions overall of this team after three practices? >> This defense is as advertised, Adam. At all three levels, they're they're operating in concert. They just have a really good feel for what one another's doing, and that really shouldn't be a surprise. The better part of this unit has been together for at least three seasons. They're entering their third year with Vic Fangio, and it's to be expected that they're giving the offense some quality work. And I think the offense will ultimately benefit from it having going against a unit, you know, this style. >> Yeah, and remember they're going to play Dallas twice. And they'll be running fit the Fangio scheme, and some others that they'll face will run some of that stuff. So they'll be interesting to see what happens. But yeah, so we got we got through the first part of training camp. Now, the offense as fully expected is far behind the defense in terms of efficiency, but Andrew, I know in your daily DeChellis, you talk about some standouts. So what What you like about the offense that you saw? >> Well, I did like a lot of the under center play action. I thought Jalen Hurts made some of his better throws out of under center and and and the play action passes. And it's going to be a work in progress, but I did see some things that I liked. He's taking more chances than he has that I can remember, which is good to see. We'll see if that [clears throat] carries over into the regular season, but he's willing to throw the ball into tight windows, which is going to be imperative of a true West Coast offense, which this is. And there are certain players that have really stood out to me. Namely Tank Bigsby, the Eagles running back who they acquired last September. I think he stands to have a more defined role this year. You see the the change of pace that he presents and just a lot of juice and explosiveness. I can't wait to see what he can do when the pads come on. Then you look at some of the other receivers. DeVonta Smith, he's as consistent and steady as it gets, but then you're looking at, okay, what are you seeing from Dontayvion Wicks? How is Mekhi Leven progressing? Mekhi Leven was targeted a few different times on Saturday. None of them were complete, but I think it really underscores a more important point here, and that is that they are looking to get him involved. He's seeing a lot of first team reps, and we'll see if they're able to sort of establish some consistency there in getting him the football throughout the summer. >> All right, before we take a deep dive on the offense and we'll then we'll hit the defense. They did have one transaction during the first week, and uh they released Takkarist McKinley as a veteran who was drafted by the Falcons. He's actually a vested veteran. The only defensive tackle that they had who was vested, they released him with a non-football injury settlement, and you were telling me off the air that he was not he was excused on Saturday. Is that correct? >> Excused, not injury related. >> Right. Okay. >> was in a a number of of the players had that designation, and he was one of them. >> All right, so yeah, so he's no longer an Eagle. Uh they are now down to eight defensive tackles on the 90-man roster. Six are guys who actually have playing experience. Uh so Jomo, Davis and Carter who are the starters, Gabe Hall was what who's been This is his third year on and off the Eagles roster, Tyree Robinson of course, and Britain Young is the first guy off the bench. Then you have Zion Wilson, the undrafted free agent out of East Carolina who was a very intriguing player, and of course you are Bernard, so uh look, Quez Watkins was a major long shot to make it anyway, but they won't have him as he was released and uh by the way, he was going to make just under 1.3 million, so they did a settlement, which is going to be far less than he was going to make, but again, he is going to make some money from the Eagles this season uh due the settlement, so as we move on, Andrew, uh back to the offense. The guy uh you know, it's interesting. Dontayvion Wicks, he certainly everyone probably knows about it now, or most people do, uh the big-time catch in Thursday's practice on a broken play, but overall with Dontayvion Wicks, what did you see from him? >> Someone who's really good at creating separation in the short to intermediate levels. He's not someone who's going to threaten down the down the field at least consistently. That's not really his game, but he has a different frame relative to the other players in the room, and going back to his time in Green Bay, Adam, what I noticed about him is he does a nice job of using his body for positioning and doing some of the technical aspects of that job. The The questions with him is can he catch the football consistently? That's been something that's plagued him throughout his time in Green Bay, and needless to say, he's going to undertake a much more prominent role here in Philadelphia, so that's something that's going to be under the spotlight here throughout camp, but he has had He's had a handful of catches, and he's You could see him sort of develop the rapport with Jalen Hurts as as practices you know, progress here, but uh obviously, he's one of the more fascinating cases in this offense because not a lot is known about him. He's never had more than 39 catches in a season, maybe 74 or 75 targets in a season, so he's a big question mark, but I think what's most interesting about this is that clearly Shawn Mannion and Ryan McHaffey, Ryan McHaffey was his wide receivers coach for 2 years in Green Bay. They have a unique perspective on what he can provide and we'll have to see if he's able to to meet the moment here. >> Yeah, see what hurt him is it UVA that he had one really good season and then the rest was just not good enough. So, he dropped plus the 40-time at the combine which was bad, 4.62. So, he ran much better at his pro day and that that helped him at least get drafted, but there's talent there. Uh he's a what you would call a big 6'1 and 3/10 of an inch. He's He certainly looks bigger than that up front. He's got long arms, fairly long arms. So, he was a fifth-rounder by the way with with the Packers in in 2023. So, yeah, he's going to be one of the their their top three receivers, but the question is as we transition to some more of the other receivers here is Quez Watkins who's going to line up mostly in the slot. What are your feelings on him for a guy who missed the majority of their off-season due to injury? >> Yeah, it didn't it doesn't appear as though he's too far behind the eight ball. The Eagles are giving him a ton of first team reps. He's been utilized uh in terms of motion and things like that. He was targeted a few times on Saturday, Adam. None of them were complete. There was one on a deep shot down the sideline where he had a half step on Cooper DeJean. Cooper DeJean was able to close the gap there. The pass was a little long from Jalen Hurts. There was one on during a seven-on-seven period over the middle and you know, Drew Sample was able to break on it, sort of ran through him a little bit there. That was incomplete. Then there was another one in the red zone when they were working on red zone period where Jalen tried to fit one in to him and Jeremiah Trotter Jr. pulled him down and drew the pass interference flag. So, they're getting they're looking to get him involved and they're targeting him. We just got to see some of that develop a little bit more. >> And I'll tell you who's flashed. And if he makes it, he it's he's not going to see much time if he plays at all on offense, but Britain Covey had a number of catches in Thursday's practice. >> Yes, he did. >> they're not in pads or anything. It's the practices are light, but man, he's and they don't like they don't need a slot receiver because they've got Lemon. They don't need a backup slot receiver. It's not necessary. But man, Britain Covey's got good quicks for for a small guy. It's just the the the key here is what could he provide other than punt returning? Not much else, and that's going to be the challenge for him. >> Britain's a hard worker, man. Every every summer that he's been in Philadelphia, he flashes here and there with some receptions. He does have really good short area quickness. That's really fascinating to watch when you watch the receivers go through individuals. Him and DeVonta Smith have a really unique quickness to them when they're doing the drills, but it's going to be very difficult for him, needless to say, but I don't know. I feel like he's a player that is going to be someone in the preseason who really flashes. Now, being that far down in the depth chart, you're not likely to see a role, but he is sort of interesting as a potential manufactured touch player. I just don't know that that would be the case here because of all the players in front of him. >> Yeah, and believe it or not, he actually turns 30 years old in March. It's hard to believe. >> believe it or not, a little fun fact, we share the same birthday. >> Do you really? >> Yeah. >> You're a little bit older, right? No, I'm just kidding. >> Yeah, just a tad. >> Just a tad. So, so as we as we continue on offense, you know, the number one thing coming into this situation with Hurts, with the timing, but also very important is the health of the offensive line. And I know they're not in pads, they're not hitting. The tempo's way faster than it was though in OTAs. If you've watched the linemen, what have you seen from them? >> The angles are something that you're going to notice right away. The first look that you have at the offensive line. I'm speaking to those who haven't seen it yet. I think it should alleviate some pressure from them in relative to the growing nature that they adopted under Jeff Stoutland for many years. It should preserve them a little bit more, but Adam, to a larger point here, from a health perspective, they they seem to be uh right where you would expect them to be. There doesn't appear to be any lingering effects from last season, and that's all you can ask for at this stage. But, it's among the most prominent storylines going into the fall and really throughout the season because as I've mentioned to you, and I've said it on the The Cheko Daily Podcast, it doesn't much matter how much of an evil genius Shawn Marion is in the words of Jordan Mailata. title: Exclusive Interview with Pat McAfee | Pittsburgh Steelers

title: Max Iheanachor, Keeanu Benton IMPRESS, T.J. Watt plan, Mason McCormick taking leap | Steelers Rewind
text: What's going on everybody? Welcome back to another episode of Steelers Training Camp Rewind. Pittsburgh Steelers padded practice. Today the Pat McAfee show is here. It was hyped. Certainly not the usual padded practice that I am used to or you would be used to with Mike Tomlin around. No live tackling, no backs on backers today. Although Mike McCarthy did say he was a backs on backers guy. Potentially we see that tomorrow or some point later in the week, maybe the Saturday night lights practice. Either way, still physical, but not quite the umpth we had, but still plenty to take away. And let's start with the O line Dline one-on- ones because those went nowhere. And there were a lot of notes here. First of all, the one thing that jumped out, the way Keanu Benton and TJ Watt moved around. TJ Watt rushed over the middle. He rushed right and left side. We saw Highmith and Herbig moving around. We saw Cam Hayward even go out a little bit. We saw these guys move around. But TJ Watt beat Maxi Honor on a bull rush right on his left side. Um, like he usually rushes from. He then went to the right side and def promptly defeated Troy Falano with a nasty spin move. Went over the middle. Spencer Anderson got the better of him, but that is what this team is going to do. They continue to talk about moving guys around and versatility. They are not just talking. We have seen that come about. TJ Watt is going to be moving around, but so are the other edge rushers. Now, let's talk about some performance. Keanu Benton, I thought, had a phenomenal day today. Not just in these one-on- ones, but in team drills. He played nose tackle, he played one tech, he played three tech, he played a little four eye, he played a little five. He did a bunch of different things today, and you just saw him in the back field so often. Him and Nick Herbig were absolutely wrecking plays in team drills, but really Benton was someone from the interior they had no answer for. Um, and so I thought he stood out in a huge way. This is a contract year for him obviously, but in that new role, he has breakout potential. Five and a half sacks last year. He could actually eclipse that mark this year and I would not be surprised from the O line side of things. Really am impressed by Maxi Haunted Shore. You know, for the rookie, he did a nice job. He mirrored Alex Highmith [clears throat] on an inside move. He ran Jack Sawyer around the arc. I thought he had a really nice rep against Sawyer again where Sawyer tried to get him inside and he got his hands inside. You know, his hands are still raw. He's got to get them uh timed up right. He's got to get them tighter. It's a little wide. And when Watt ran through his chest, it's cuz he was wide and opened up his pads and was able to really get forklifted. Now, he did a nice job to anchor down. I think he's strong, but guys are going to be able to move him off a spot if he's too wide with his hands. But a really good showing for from him. I thought he looked good in the team drills. Um I thought he had a good day today. I thought Zack Frasier and Mason McCormack were iron walls on the interior of this offensive line. Really good. Just standard business from Zack Frasier. He continues to ascend. I think he has the ability to be a pro war this year, but Mais McCormack looks like he's on a different level. Troy Falano still figuring some things out at left tackle. I think the rust is getting knocked off. He's trying to find that happy medium between overthinking, not playing too aggressive. Seems like James Campin's kind of teaching him to be more cerebral. And I think we're seeing the growth of Troy Falanu's game right before us. You're going to have some, I think, growing pains with that, but I think we've seen a lot of positives there. Brock Hoffman as well. Played a little bit first team right guard. Spencer Anderson had some losses in the one-on- ones, but has been pretty steady. But Hoffman, I think, did a really good job today. Um, I think he looked really good. In terms of the other uh Dlineman, I think Aazio had some really good reps today. There was one rep that I want to highlight where he blitzed into the BC gap and Eli Hidenrike comes and steps up and pops him and I think that's a really good sign. If you're Eli Hidenrike, you need to be showing your pass pro chops. That was something I thought that was really good. Drew Aller had a really nice throw about 55 yards to Cole Burgess in the seven on seven period. Aaron Rogers and DK Metaf continue to have this great connection. Uh, Meetaf made two more catches right down the sideline on Jamal Dean that I thought were really impressive overall. Sleeper that's standing out, two of them. Brandon Smith, 87, wide receiver. He's made some nice catches. It just felt like so awful when I was looking up. Oh, there's 87 again. There's 87. He's open again. It felt really easy for him to to build a connection with Will Howard and Mason Rudolph. And I think that's a real positive. I also thought Deno Slaughter who is playing slot and outside corner. He had a pick of Will Howard in the seven on sevens. I thought was a really good break and then had a few really nice run fits in the team period. So, a lot of positives there for Deno Slaughter as well. The padded practice today, really, really positive stuff. We'll see. We're probably going to be in pads again tomorrow and that's when I will be back, folks. Make sure to like, comment, subscribe, turn notification bell for more.

It's which is what you want as a football coach. You don't you want to you want a a player to do what you want him to do but at the same time you want the player to feel free to express his feelings cuz ultimately he's out there getting bullets thrown at him so or shot at him whatever you want to however you want to say it but but the dialogue's been great. The transparency's been great and so hopefully we stay on that trajectory. >> I am a matter. He said coming into this this year he wanted to play with more better body language, more confidence, aggressiveness. Is that a conversation you guys had? How do you feel that he's done that so >> Uh he first day of pads, you know, he's uh consistency will always be the truest measure performance. So everyone can do it once. The more you prepare, the more confident you are stepping onto the field, the the more urgency you play with, the more violence you play with, the more the louder your voice is, the louder your pads get. So, everything everything gets louder and more demonstrative when you're playing with confidence cuz you're not thinking. You're just go going out there and performing. So, that that's the entire team. Um and it's what we're trying to get them all to get to. Alec uh has really done a great job attacking that. Um you know, first off, James coming out uh Miami, he was a safety. Um he's doing a nice job absorbing it all, attacking it all, and there's a game within a game that happens out on the perimeter with corners. Um, you know, first and foremost, you know, I trust in the call that that's been given and, uh, playing in my technique, playing in the scheme, um, and then trusting that coach has puts us in the right position. Um, he's going to put the guys in their strengths. Um, and then other than that, you know, quarterbacks depending on down the distance, if they trying to just get a first down, if they need a big big chunk, uh, know if you got to play on, play press, if you got to play off. Um, but I think, you know, just trusting what coaches going to call and just trust the technique that you've been doing, um, uh, throughout practices. >> You got the contract, you got the baby, got your mom a new house. Do you kind of have to pinch yourself about what 2026 has been like? >> Uh, yeah, man. A lot's happened so fast. Um, definitely blessed. Uh, beautiful daughter, beautiful wife. Uh, my family's amazing. They're super excited, like I say, about their home. So, it's all coming together. So, I'm happy to be where I'm at. >> Did you clear these guys over there before you said that it was going to be the best quarterback room in >> No, no, no. We ain't I'm I'm not clearing that. I think, you know, to my core, I believe that. I believe we have the right minded guys with me and Flight. Um, you know, we can say the best trio if you want to add that in there, too. But most importantly, you know, I feel like I got a lot of trust in Fly. He got a lot of trust in me. and we push each other how we know we can push each other uh throughout this training camp. I think come season, you know, we'll just display it. >> Where's that trust initially come from when you hadn't really seen it all together? >> Well, I've watched fly from far. Um I knew a lot about him coming in. Um and then just seeing how we work, man, all all summer, you know, we worked out every single day together. Um and we corrected each other, we pushed each other, we made sure that, you know, we were honest with one another. And by doing that, um you know, that just built built the trust and then hanging out outside the field as well. a more successful training camp in preseason look like for you to kind of get you get yourself primed for the season. >> Uh first id say you know staying healthy you know coming out of this staying healthy is the most important part but you know just just hone in on the technique um just finishing on plays um and just you know getting better with the playbook and just building the team team side as far as PBUS picks all that stuff's good and great but you know it matters come come week one and throughout the season. I know you talking to Cam a little you see a lot of guys on defense talking to Cam. Is he a little different as a quarterback when it comes to that kind of stuff? >> Man, I think that's what I expect from a quarterback. I mean, you hear a lot about Cam coming here. Um, but the way he was chirping out there is the same thing that I seen back in New Orleans. It's the same thing that I expect to see from a quarterback who has that edge, who's going to compete, who's going to uh, you know, challenge his corners. And that's what we appreciate. >> You played against Ellis last year and you've been out here on the practice field with him for a few days. How have you seen him grow this this camp? >> Um yeah, I mean I feel like he do a few things. The same that that I seen um you know when we played him, but as far as seeing the way he practices is good, you know, uh a guy who's going to keep his head down and just work super hard. Um you just got to find a balance. >> You had Ridley, you had Ridley in the red zone a lot. Uh seemed like he got on quick and close to him. He had a hard time. >> That kind of uh kind of period you want to have. I I love it when I see Zero come to my side. A guy who's a great route runner, a guy who's going to strain, a guy that's fast. Uh he has it all put together, man. And and you know, going up against him. Uh you know, it allows me to kind of kind of put myself, you know, where where I feel like I'm at. Um you know, but one thing I love about Red is he going to he going to work with you, he going to coach with you, and vice versa. So, uh today it was a good day. >> Cut to the end. [laughter] >> Coach has you guys over an individual working on get off so frequently. What's his message to you guys about that? >> Uh get off is everything. That's uh that's, you know, he say we start our day with, you know, with that just because that's, you know, that's a start of every play for us is get off the rock. Um he say if we get off the rock as as fast as we can and hard as we can, we can make any play we want to. >> How much you feel like you've improved maybe already at that? >> Um man, I feel like I improved in that just like tremendously, man. like um he he he he he he coaches it so well to where it's no thinking. Um you know, you don't have to think about getting off the rock hard cuz it just is is natural. >> Along those lines of get off, you had said one of the biggest things you want to focus on was pad level. How has that come along as far as being able to keep especially as tall as you are keeping your pad level? >> Man, that's it's it's coming along. Um my pad level has gotten way better. Um he he he's taught me little nicks and tricks to to keep my pass down. Um one it helps me in the one it helps me in the run and it definitely helps me when I'm rushing the passer. So I I get a lot more speed. I get a lot more power whenever my pass down. Um and then I get to create I get to create more space like I well I get to take up more space as my pads are down and and I'm getting off the rock so hard. How much of today was a test for all those things that you've been working on like pad level and get off when you put the pads on and have to go against somebody else? >> Um, man, it was definitely a test cuz uh, man, you you would think like whenever the pads come on, everything that he everything that he go over, everything that, you know, we went over throughout OTAAS was just going out the window. It was just how hard you can hit somebody. But, uh, you had to combine that with the fundamentals that we that we preach every day. So, um, today was definitely a test for that. >> What was some of the biggest things you think you learned maybe this off season and maybe 3 4 days into camp? >> Um, man, just to, um, just to never stop rushing. Um, and to never never overthink a rush, you know, or or never overthink a play. Um, just play football. Football is football. Football been football since, you know, I was in the first grade. It ain't never changed. Um, so he always tell me like don't think too much, just go out there and play. Um, if you play hard, everything g everything will handle itself. >> How much do you look forward to the past coming? >> Man, shoot. I've been looking forward to that. You know, it was it it was it was kind of hard just to, you know, try to stop ourselves from going at each other so so hard cuz the O line and Dline, you know, we we've been like that for I don't know what, three months. What was it? Three months, right? Yeah, we've been like that for three months. So, um, when the pass came on, I shoot, you could feel the energy in the in the in the locker room. Nobody was talking. It was just straight music playing and everybody was just ready to go out there and get active. >> What's the like for that defensive line group? I mean, it looks like you guys work with a great deal of urgency. >> That's it. That's his whole message. Um, whenever like if you watch our drills, it's is urgency. Um, it's it's two people going and when when them two people get up, two people are down already, ready to go. So, um, he teaches urgency. Um, whenever the ball's thrown, we urgent getting out the stack. Um, man, whenever we rushing the pass or getting getting the play or getting down for the play, we urgent with that. Urgent with our communication. Um, urgency is everything for for the bel. >> Um, definitely is like everything is so fast-paced. um you know you he tell us not to think so much but um you know you you think a whole lot faster whenever the bullets start flying. So >> with as much with this uh >> as fast as he wants you guys to play >> and guys continually coming on and off the field in waves, you know, and replacing each other. What do you feel like is kind of the right amount of snaps for a guy to get in before he goes and gets that break? >> However many. It don't matter, you know, because um whenever we step up on that field, it's it's it's all or nothing. If you can't give your all, you ain't on the field. Um that's just that's his message. If you can't give your all, run to that ball like, you know, like we said we was, uh you just went on the field. Um so to be honest, it's it's a it's up to you. Like it's up to you how many plays you can go until you know you can come out. You you you you about ready to come out. Now that you're starting to see the game the way that Solid Boy Cup kind of wants you to. Thinking back on college, do you think you overthinking it back then? >> Um, you said, say that again. >> You talked about not overthinking anymore. Do you think you used to overthink? >> Definitely did. Um, cuz you know, it's it's two different styles of play. Um, from where I'm from, we we you know, we getting off the rock as hard as we can. uh up here down when I was at Auburn, we was you know read watching the man, you know, as soon as he soon as he got off, we was reacting to him. Um but here is just like clear your mind, go play ball. >> How did you work on clearing your mind? man, just uh think about my job and nothing else. You know, my job and nothing else. um making sure that I was communicating, but whenever my job came around, it was, you know, it it was thinking about that and then nothing else. >> What would you say are some factors that helped you slow the game down, keep it just football? >> Man, um I really don't know for real. Um, I I kind of treat I kind of treat it just like I was in college, but uh, you know, we don't got school or nothing no more, so it's just amplified. So, it's, you know, more film, um, more studying, more, you know, me coming out here by myself, getting getting some more work in, coming down extra with Coach Tanzel. Um, so it it's it's in a way it's easier to think about just football whenever you ain't really got nothing else to do. >> What's it like being a 21-y old kid out there? with guys who were 30 league. >> Man, it was crazy. I thought Jeff was 30 and I I was like, you know, going out there and playing with them was like, you know, kind of kind of weird cuz, you know, when you in college, I mean, we had a couple guys was like 28. But the the oldest guy I played with was 24 and that was even rare. So whenever I got out there with Jeff, it was like one, this guy he he had to been doing something right because he been here for what, nine years, almost 10 years, something like that. So he had to been doing something right. And it was like, dang, like this is a real life pro out here. And then you got Germaine and uh and John and Jake uh Jacob Martin, like you got them guys, they real life vets out here. And it's like, you know, you see them, they playing hard and and they pushing 30. It's like that's how you got to be. That's how you got to be if you're going to last in the league. >> On how to take care of your body the way he does. >> Uh definitely. Yeah. Um every every other day I come in um I try to pick his mind about something. Uh you know, he he he has his own ways, but he always tell me figure out my own ways, >> man. Just just to crush it, dude. like don't don't go in there and just like go through the motions on it like you know work out hard cuz you know coach Sally even said like go out there crush the workout because you know we want to continue to get stronger throughout this offseason we don't want to just stay we don't want to stay mellow we want to get we want to elevate throughout the offseason >> you see a different side of Jeff when the pass come >> I definitely did Jeff Jeff is a real Jeff is real life like um man he He he intense with it. Um and he plays hard like every every snap he plays hard. Like he's balls to the wall every every snap. Um and then you know between the plays he got a little words here and there and that's that's like the part of diff I love the most cuz like you know he ain't never too tired to talk. You know he's always ready to go. >> Was the 20 push-ups justified near the beginning? Man, >> were you all flat, >> man? Um, I hate doing the push-ups, >> but uh then the offense, you know, I I guess I guess they got us. You know what I'm saying? But, um, you know, that's just all part of competing. 20 push-ups just, you know, just a competing factor for all of us. So, >> there we go.

title: Brant Boyer and 49ers Players Address the Media Following Day 6 of Camp | 49ers
text: let's go cuz he he is a he's a differencemaker and uh you know he's obviously proven and he's and he's done it uh at a very very high level. So you know I'm you know really anxious u we we're all talking about it to get him in our scheme and and uh you know I've watched him and you know really liked what he'd done throughout his career liked him coming out of college and and uh you know he's a hell of a player and he's really tough to tackle and and uh you know he's got speed to take it to the house all the time. So, you know, like again, anytime you can add a guy like that to the roster, you're you're jumping up for joy as a special teams coach. >> It's obviously early, but what's kind of just your process for evaluating the two punters and and what you want to see and ultimately making a decision? >> You know, like you said, it's really early, right? Um but you want to put them in the pressure situations and see how they handle it. you know, we're rotating days and and we're kicking, you know, um a little, you know, trying to get more reps so we get more on tape and, you know, trying to do the best job we can at evaluating and and then then we'll choose one from there. And and uh you know, they're [clears throat] both doing a nice job. Um both have strong legs. Uh you know, it's just the consistency that you look for and and uh you know, so that that's going to be the key is is how do they perform in the preseason games and things like that. And you know, just like any other position, it it's all how they perform perform in the preseason. Is >> there any difference with a left hand a left-handed holder versus a right-handed holder for kicker? >> No. No, cuz it's all based off the kicker. You know, they they've got to line up the one way. So, I think that, you know, um you know, they're both doing a really good job. Both are smooth holders. Um both of have have had extensive work at holding. So, you know, and and that's why we brought them here. They're they've done a nice job so far. and Eddie's comfortable with both of them. >> I don't know how many rookie punters you've had in your career, but I'm going to guess that none of them were 27 years old like Jack Bow Meister is. I mean, do you see um you know a typical rookie with him or can you tell that he's he's had experience? >> Well, I think he's he's very obviously very mature guy. Um you know, he's he's doing a super good job. Um, you know, and so both of them are, like I said, I think that, you know, you go out and you try to find the best guy that you can, no matter what their age is, to compete, right? And because they're going to have to be relied on to to help us win games. And, you know, I think that Jack is doing a nice job of of of competing in this in this competition. And, uh, you know, I think that the longer we can see him, the better. Now, can the roster handle both of them for that long depending on injuries and stuff like that? We're trying. Obviously, you try to want to keep them for as long as you can to see him in more games and and things like that, you know. So, hopefully we can do that. >> Grant, the rookie Pauling seems to catch the punts pretty naturally. How do you see that competition back there? >> I I you know, there's a handful of guys and and to be honest with you, you know, hopefully somebody emerges. Um, you know, I think, you know, Cowing, Pauling, Watkins, um, you know, all those guys are back there. Um, Junior Bergen. Um, so there's a a big handful of guys and and you know, hopefully they can make great decisions and and catch the ball first and foremost and that's that's what's most important. Um, Pauling's got a really good skill set. There's a lot of guys that are have good skill sets. It's a matter of can they make the right decisions? Can they block a gunner when they're supposed to? Can they let a ball hit the ground when they're supposed to? Can they go up and catch a fair catch it when they're supposed to? There's there's a lot more that goes into it than just than just uh returning the ball. But, you know, I think that um those guys that we're trying to find the guy that has the whole package that we can count on every week um that that can catch the ball and make great decisions. >> How how different is this training camp for you compared to last year when you're not sure what the kicker situation was going to be and now you have Eddie who's entrenched in the position? >> Um you know, there's a lot of things that is different about this year obviously. Um, but specifically Eddie. Um, you know, I think that, you know, there was there was so much going back and forth on, you know, what was going to happen and things like that that that it's good to have a guy that that that has done it for me before and and for quite a while. So, um, you know, he he did a great job last year and and couldn't have, you know, done a better job. So, um, you know, he's worked on some things this offseason. I think he's he's uh come pretty far in quite a few things. He's worked on his kickoffs and and uh you can tell he's worked in the offseason despite getting his contract and I was happy as hell to see him get paid for his work. Um you know, he's worked a long time and and stuff like that, but um you know, I I'm really happy for the guy and I think that everybody knows that they can count on him and so it's in a in a good situation. But as far as like you know me coming last year and and being in the second year of the system um everything all all the schemes um the what Colt and Ronnie do a great job of helping me with um you know all the schemes all the stuff they've been in that for a year. So where we are on punt team and our return schemes and everything are way ahead of where we were last year and so you know they have experience of of all the situational stuff that I'm giving them. So, it's um you know, it's a it's it's a welcome relief, that's for sure. You >> mentioned Eddie getting paid. Did did you have any moments of worry that that that might not get done you? What was it what was kind of like when you found out that that >> I've lost too many uh in the past to to not worry about it. So, yeah, you you always worry when you know and but you're always, you know, as as a coach, you're you know, my my whole deal is like I I want to see these guys succeed and I want to see them get paid and you know, that's what they're in the business for. And so, you know, I've had guys I mean, Jason Myers, and you could go down through the list that I've lost, you know, but you know, as as bad as it hurts you, you're you're happy to see them, you know, that they succeed and have and have great careers and and um you know, was I happy to have Eddie back? Hell yeah. You know, cuz you know what you're going to get all the time. And so, [clears throat] um you know, plus he's such a good guy and good guy for the room and stuff like that. So, I was happy to get him back. But anytime specifically you're trying to trying to, you know, one of your main guys is trying is up for a new contract, you know, you hope you get paid, but you hope you can, you know, that you can retain as well. >> Eddie had talked last year about how he had not, you know, up until last year, he hadn't attempted tons of 50 plus yard field goals and how may have been a lack of confidence from previous teams. Did he surprise you with his leg strength just because it hadn't been out there that much? No, I just cuz I've seen him for so long, you know, having him at the Jets and stuff like that. So, I I had no worry about his leg strength and then, you know, evaluating him coming out of college, too. Um, you know, that's his leg strength is not an issue for me at all. >> What is maybe difficult about judging punters in practice? You talked about putting them in pressure situations. How much can you really do that before you get to the >> I mean, you're you're right. It's it's really hard to simulate, right? Um cuz it's, you know, it's the game situations and how are they going to react when it's easy to do out here on the field, but how are they going to react when there's 75,000 people watching you in a national TV game or something like that? So, you try to put them in situations like the, you know, two-minute situations and things like that. Um how good a holder are they in, you know, um you know, whatever it is, you're trying to put them in situations that they'll be facing in these preseason games and then you try to evaluate them from there. And then, you know, when they do get the the preseason games, you know, how do how do they function? Are they, you know, are they super nervous uh in pregame? Are they super nervous when you ask them, "Hey, man, the game's on the line here. You know, we got to do this." And do they execute it when you ask them to? And that, you know, so it's really hard to to simulate that in practice. All >> good. >> Thank you guys. [clears throat] Hola, how's camp going for you so far? >> Camp is going great. Um, my favorite camp, honestly, uh, since I've been here. >> Um, I love this scheme. Sorry. Um, I love this scheme. I love the teammates I got. Um, I'm comfortable this year for for me. Um, and I'm honestly I'm having fun, bro. Having fun. And uh I can't remember the last time I had this much fun. >> Some of the other DBs have talked about how Raheem has kind of stripped away some of the, you know, just hard to grasp details. Just made it made it easier to to grasp, I suppose. Can you do you feel the same way first of all? And if so, can you kind of enlighten us on what that means? >> Absolutely. Um, Raheem's dope, bro. Uh, super dope. Um, he wants football players, you know. um previous schemes we've been in um haven't been that haven't wanted that. You know, uh Raheem wants you to play football. He want instinctive players. He want um guys who can just, you know, get out there and play ball and read the quarterback. So, um scheme fits all of us, man. And uh it's been great to see us transition into this explosive Dback unit. >> When you said that the scheme or you like this system or what is it about it that you like so much? Um, me personally, uh, it it fits more into my strong suits, reading the quarterback, you know, um, being reactive, letting my instincts take over. Um, probably the best part of my game. So, uh, that's what I love about this scheme over the last schemes I've been in. Uh, whoops is a lot similar, but um, yeah. >> How hard was it for you the last couple years with it not being fun to be out there? >> I wouldn't say it wasn't fun the last couple of years. I'm always having fun, you know, out there with the players, you know, that I'm out there on the field with because, uh, it's a war out there, honestly. And, um, whenever you're out and having a war and on a battlefield with all your guys, you know, um, the good, the bad, the ugly, it's always going to be fun, you know, dealing with that adversity together, dealing with the highs and the lows. Um, it it comes with with great memories, man. And, uh, you always enjoy those times. Um, this year just a little different, you know, with a better scheme. Um, I like it. you uh I think today you had a play in the red zone. Were you where you broke up a pass where intended for Jake >> that Brock threw. Were you reading Brock or did you read the route? >> I think I was a man to man coverage there on the backside. Jake tried to run a deep over. Um kind of ran it down, made a play on the ball for the team. >> Yeah. >> In the past with this team, we've kind of heard that the safety positions are almost interchangeable. The free and strong maybe not so specific. Is it a little different? Is it maybe a little more separate between the free and the strong this this season? No, we're pretty much interchangeable. We pretty much do the same jobs. Uh, you know, um, I can go in the boundary, I can go on the field. They're pretty much the same jobs, you know, either way. But, um, yeah, they're pretty interchangeable. >> J, how much have you enjoyed having Dre back, >> man? Uh, Dre, Fred, man, all those guys, man. But, um, Dre, man, bro, he he was the enforcer, man. when I in 23 when we went to that Super Bowl run and uh his energy, his passion, his aggression, bro, is is it it feeds the whole defense, man. So, uh super dope to have him back, man. Gave me a lot of memories being out there with him. Uh and that's been one of the funnest parts about this year. >> With Dre and Debo back, does it feel like you guys have some unfinished business from that group you're >> Yeah, man. It is. It definitely do feel like that. Um you know, we know we came up short in 23. uh all these guys man and the good thing about it they got something to prove you know Debo has something to prove Dre has something to prove and um and not not to nobody else not to no outsiders more to their self you know um me as well you know so uh for all of us to be fighting you know for something personally but also as a whole you know for um the team it's pretty dope to see man it's going to be dope >> what what is it was it about you know maybe the past last year's defense or previous year's defense that maybe didn't suit your strengths as well in your in your opinion? [clears throat] [snorts] >> Um, I'm not going to even uh go there, man. And um what what happened last year is what happened last year, you know. Um cuz things have been better, of course. Uh but uh I'm not going to, you know, hold nobody accountable to that. Uh I'll just hold myself accountable and um take whatever come with that, you know. But what happened last year was last year. >> How much fun has it been able to go against Mike Evans and then what does he bring to that wide receiver William when you guys were facing them? >> OG Mike man. Uh Mike dope man. I remember when we first got here I brought up a rep we had my rookie year in the red zone. Uh cover zero rep I had against him man. And um he's been dope to work with man. He got a lot of old tricks man. And uh been absolutely helping us get better as a defensive unit. And um seeing him out there is dope, man. watch him make plays, watch him run routes. He's his all-time pro, one of the the the best receivers to ever play the game, man. And uh it's a it's a privilege to be out there on the field with him. >> Going going into a contract year, is that is that something you allow yourself to think about or are you just focused on what you do on the field? Let that take care. What what's kind of your approach to to this this year? >> Focus on what I take like when I get out on that field, man. I don't think about none of that. Um I I'm literally out there. I'm having fun, man. I I can't think of nothing outside of it's it's so detailed. This game is so detailed and so one play focused that uh your mind just has to be on the day, the moment, the now, you know. So, uh that that stuff, you know, I don't even worry about that. I'm here to play football. >> How do you ch how do you know you you know, you took some public criticism from some ex players this year in the offseason. You got a lot of people who want to get grade you, judge you, evaluate you. How do you block out some voices and hear others? How do you compartmentalize that whole thing? >> Um, it's something we do as humans. You know, we we like to judge and, you know, um, put our own perspectives and our own opinions on others. Um, whether they're are completely wrong or completely right, you know, everybody feels like their opinion should be evaluated, should be taken serious. And, um, it's all opinions at the end of the day. Um, the guys in this building know what's going on. Uh, my teammates know what's going on. My coaching staff and my owners know what's going on. So, uh, I'm really just focused on them, man. And the people in this building, making them proud, making the franchise proud. Um, all the outside noise, it doesn't bother me, you know? I'm not really a big social media guy. >> What's your What's your favorite NBA team? >> Oh, man. Rest in peace Kobe, man. But back then it was the Lakers, man. Man, I love Brian, but man, I was a big Kobe fan, man. And um now I'm rocking with Golden State, man. So, I switched up a little bit. Um Steph Curry fan now. So, uh I like the Warriors, man. >> I thought it might be the Knicks. What did Mike Brown did he address the team after? >> Respect to the Knicks. I didn't grow up a Knicks fan, though, man. Um you know, congrats to that whole franchise and Mike Brown. He just broke the team down today. Great guy. um he does he's been with the Warriors as well, you know, so uh it's dope to see him go over there and get a win, man. And he preached a lot about culture today and uh I feel like he sent a great message to the team. >> All right, thanks D. >> Thank you guys. I appreciate it. Yes, good chance. >> Kyle, so many of you, your guys teammates seem to be really genuinely excited that Debo's coming back. Where does that excitement come from? >> It comes from a lot of things. Oh, wow. I didn't know this was on. Um Debo's the best. He's such an incredible teammate. He's such a good friend. Uh he's an incredible football player. So, we're really happy to have him in the locker room just cuz he brings the best vibes and positivity, but we're also happy to have him on the field because he's still got juice and he still can go out there and make good plays. He came in, he looks like he's in phenomenal shape. Uh his first day in pads, he's making an impact right away and just looked like the old Debo. So, uh, I can't say enough positive things about how excited we are to have him. >> Have you spoken to Ricky Pierce all since he got the news that he's going to have to have surgery? >> Yeah, I have. And, uh, it's it's just really unfortunate how things have played out for him. I I feel for him so hard. Uh, cuz I know I know for him what it it's frustration in that he knows that he can be a really good wide receiver in the NFL and he and he's shown it. He's he's had some incredible games. title: The Good and Not So Good from Day 6 of 49ers Training Camp
text: The 49ers just wrapped up day six of training camp. Here's who stood out. Keep in mind, Mike Evans sat out with a quad strain that could sideline him for multiple weeks. I kid you not. More on him in a minute. The good, defensive end Romeo Height. He's getting a ton of reps with the starters at defensive end because Nick Bosa isn't participating in team drills. And while Height is a work in progress against the run, today he ran past a reverse that came right at him. He clearly is talented as an edge rusher. Today he even beat Trent Williams around the edge during 11-on-11s. Yes, Trent Williams. Height has an uncanny ability to dip his shoulder underneath the hands of the offensive tackle and turn the corner. If he stays healthy, he could have double-digit sacks as a rookie. Cornerback Deommodore Lenoir. He shut down Deebo Samuel on the first rep of one-on-one drills. Samuel ran a go route up the sideline and Lenoir outran him. Samuel actually stopped running mid-route because he was losing the race. Lenoir also broke up a pass intended for Jake Tonges near the sideline during 11-on-11s. Now that Mike Evans is injured and Brandon Aiyuk is essentially gone, there's no reason to ever throw the ball near Lenoir during practice. He's far and away better than every healthy wide receiver on the field. Cornerback Renardo Green. He won all three of his reps during one-on-ones, which is rare for a cornerback. To be fair, he faced Demarcus Robinson, Wesley Grimes, and Jordan Watkins, not exactly Pro Bowlers. Still, Green ran the routes for those receivers and broke up the passes easily. He's also better than every healthy wide receiver on the field. Cornerback Ifeanyi Princewill Umenigbo. He broke up a pass from Mac Jones that was intended for Junior Bergen in the red zone. Princewill Umenigbo is beginning to make plays in coverage. He's one of the most promising rookies in camp. Cornerback Jacob Robinson. He broke up a long pass from Mac Jones that was intended for Colton Dowell near the left sideline. Robinson had a good camp last year as an undrafted free agent rookie before breaking his arm during the preseason, missing the rest of the year. Now he's healthy and picking up where he left off last training camp. Safety Jair Brown. He broke up a potential touchdown pass from Brock Purdy that was intended for Jake Tanjus. If Kittle had been the intended target, the pass probably would have been a touchdown. But, Kittle is injured and Tanjus is much slower than him, so Brown could catch up and tip the ball away. Hopefully, he'll get to face tight ends who are slow as Tanjus all season. Quarterback Brock Purdy, he was accurate, decisive, and he protected the football, which is all you can ask from him right now. Would it be nice for him to make lots of plays down the field and in the red zone? Sure, but his receivers aren't open. Any time the defense decides to play man-to-man coverage, Purdy either can force a pass to a heavily covered backup or scramble or throw the ball away. Today, he almost got picked by Tatum Bethune while trying to force a short pass to Patrick Taylor Jr. It's heartbreaking. The best thing he does is throw the ball with touch over the middle, but right now there's no one over the middle we're throwing to. Kittle is injured. Jauan Jennings is gone, and Brandon Aiyuk is on the reserved left squad list, so every throw is a 12-yard out to Deebo Samuel Robinson or a screen to Deebo Samuel or a check-down to Christian McCaffrey. What else is Purdy supposed to do? He needs help. So does Mac Jones. Quarterback Chris Rourke, he faked a handoff, rolled to his left, stopped, turned back to his right, and fired a 25-yard strike downfield to Jake Tanjus running a deep over route. That was a pretty throw. Rourke is big, he moves well, and he has a strong arm. I'm eager to watch him play during the preseason. I just might pick him up and stash him on the taxi squad of my dynasty team. The not-so-good. Wide receiver Mike Evans, he missed practice with a quad strain that could keep him sidelined for the next few weeks. Keep in mind, Evans will turn 33 in August and is coming off a season in which he gained just 368 yards. Before he injured his quad, he made some plays in the end zone because he's tall, but his route running looked labored and clunky. Now, it seems highly unlikely that he'll play more than 12 games this season just because his body keeps breaking down in new ways. This is what old age does to people. Wide receiver De'Jon Stripling, he missed his second consecutive practice with hamstring tightness. If his injury truly is minor, he should be back at practice on Wednesday after the team's day off. We'll see. Running back Khalan Black, he missed practice with an adductor strain, which is a fancy way to say a groin pull. Now, the top three backup running backs behind Christian McCaffrey are injured, and the best healthy backup running backs currently on the field are Sincere McCormick, a practice squad player, and Khalil Herbert, who has been on the team for a day. Tough times. The electrical substation, in a week it has taken out nearly a dozen players. The 9ers insist that the substation is a nothingburger, but as long as their players keep going down in bunches every day, eventually they're going to have to move their practice facility somewhere else just to see what happens. In 2014, that substation was greatly expanded to accommodate Levi's Stadium. Since then, the 9ers have been among the league's most injured teams every year with the exception of 2023. I predict the 9ers will have a new training camp site in two years. Honestly, they should move this training camp somewhere else immediately before the substation takes out anyone else, me included.
